#### Other ways of reporting considered

(1) Leave c0250 and c0300 empty on rows 0030, 0001 and 0031-0035: boe_b0742 [8,0], passes, because no evaluation exists where nothing is reported. Annex II has no instruction that exempts these rows, the DPM leaves the cells open and the Bank's own boe_b0314_6 / boe_b0314_1_x scope them, so this is an omission the gateway tolerates, not a compliant reading. (2) Report c0250 / c0300 on row 0030 only and leave the bucket rows empty for those two columns: [8,2], fails (852 against 0, 12 against 0). (3) Report row 0030 as the sum of the bucket rows, 24 'obligors' and 1,460 days: [10,0], passes, but it counts each obligor once per facility and reports a sum of averages, contrary to pp.111 and 114. (4) Nothing in the filing-indicator precondition or defaults helps: the rule has dv: 0 on row 0030 and an empty-sequence default on the bucket rows. No Annex-II-faithful, complete way of reporting the position satisfies the rule.

#### Proposed change

Remove c0250 and c0300 from the scope of boe_b0742 (c0035 can go with them: it has no data point on rows 0030-0035): scope({t: OF08.01.01.01, c:0020;0040;0050;0060;0070;0080;0090;0110;0150;0160;0170;0171;0172;0173;0180;0190;0200;0210;0251;0252;0253;0254;0260;0280;0281;0282;0290, z:0001;0002;0006;0009;0010;0011;0012;0015;0016;0017;0018;0019;0020;0021;0022;0023;0024}), expression unchanged. If a check on the two columns is wanted, make it a WARNING bound rather than an identity: {r: 0030, c: 0300} i<= isum({r: 0001; 0031-0035, c: 0300}) and {r: 0030, c: 0250} i<= imax of the bucket rows' c0250.

#### EBA precedent

boe_b0742 has no EBA equivalent (the conversion-factor rows are new in OF 08.01), but every EBA sum rule on C 08.01 leaves both columns out: v0337_m ({r0010} = {r0020} + {r0030} + {r0040} + {r0050} + {r0060}) has columns (0110;0150;0160;0170;0171;0172;0173;0180;0190;0200;0210;0220;0255;0256;0257;0260;0280;0290); v0338_m has (0020;0090;0110;0260;0290); v0340_m and v4769_m likewise omit 0230, 0240, 0250 and 0300 (EBA validation rules list, sheet 3.5). In the Bank's own set, boe_b0752_22/_23/_24 (OF 08.01 r0070 = sum of OF 08.02 on c0230, c0240, c0250) and boe_b0744 / boe_b0745 (which had c0250 and c0300 in scope) were in v4.0.0 and are absent from the v4.1.1 workbook, rule book and package; elsewhere the Bank's rules treat c0250 as an average - boe_b0758 checks OF 08.01 r0070 c0250 as the exposure-weighted average of OF 08.02 (as boe_b0756 and boe_b0757 do for c0230 and c0240; none of the three is in the taxonomy package, so the gateway does not run them), and boe_b0749, the FIRB-sheet twin of boe_b0748, leaves c0250 out of its scope. The Bank has published no reason for removing the earlier rules (not in the release note, nor in the known-issues logs of 27 August and 16 November 2026; neither boe_b0742 nor a sibling is on the November 2026 deny list, which leaves boe_b0746_1 active).

#### Who is affected

Every IRB firm (FIRB or AIRB) filing PRA001 under taxonomy v4.1.1 from the first Basel 3.1 reference date that has off-balance-sheet items in more than one conversion-factor row on a non-retail sheet (0001, 0002, 0006, 0009-0012, 0022-0024) and reports c0250 or c0300 on those rows: in practice any corporate or institution book with both committed facilities (40%) and another Table A1 item. Retail class sheets are not affected (c0250 is not reported; c0300 counts exposures).

#### What a firm can do meanwhile

Report the figures the instructions require; do not change correct figures to satisfy the rule. An Error-severity break blocks the submission at the gateway: if the gateway rejects the return on this rule, raise it with the PRA, citing this issue.

#### What the rule requires

**OF 08.01 against OF 08.03 (boe_b0737).** On each of the 17 IRB sheets: the number of obligors on the OF 08.01 Total row (r0010 c0300), minus the sum of the numbers of obligors on the three counterparty-credit-risk rows (r0040 SFT netting sets, r0050 derivative netting sets, r0060 cross-product netting sets), must equal the sum of the numbers of obligors over the eight top-level PD ranges of OF 08.03 (c0060). Blocking (ERROR).

**OF 34.07 against OF 08.01 (boe_b1035 and its siblings).** Per sheet: the number of obligors on the OF 34.07 Total row (r0180 c0030) must equal the sum of the numbers of obligors on OF 08.01 rows 0040 (SFT netting sets), 0050 (derivative netting sets) and 0060 (cross-product netting sets), column 0300. Blocking (ERROR), 17 rules.

#### What the instructions and rules say

> For all exposure classes, with the exception of the exposure class ‘retail’ and, for other exposures classes, the cases mentioned in the second sentence of Article 172(1)(e) of the Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part, the institution shall report the number of legal entities/obligors which were separately rated, regardless of the number of different loans or exposures granted.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 08.01 column 0300 NUMBER OF OBLIGORS, PDF page 114

> The number of legal entities or obligors allocated to each bucket of the fixed PD range. The number of obligors shall be counted in accordance with the instructions in column 0300 of template OF08.01. Joint obligors shall be treated the same as for the purpose of PD calibration.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 08.03 column 0060 NUMBER OF OBLIGORS, PDF page 120

> This template excludes counterparty credit risk (CCR) exposures (Counterparty Credit Risk (CRR) Part and Chapter 6 of Title II of Part Three CRR).
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 08.03 general remarks, paragraph 77, PDF page 119

> Exposures that are subject to counterparty credit risk shall be reported in rows 0040-0060 and, therefore, shall not be reported in this row.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 08.01 row 0020, PDF page 115

> Netting sets containing only SFTs, as defined in Article 4(1)(139) CRR. [...] Netting sets containing only derivatives listed in Annex II CRR and long settlement transactions as defined in Article 272(2) CRR.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 07.00 rows 0090 and 0110 (to which OF 08.01 rows 0040 and 0050 refer), PDF page 94

> The number of legal entities or obligors allocated to each bucket of the fixed PD scale, which were separately rated, regardless of the number of different loans or exposures granted.

> CCR exposures (determined at counterparty level) shall be allocated to the appropriate bucket of the fixed PD scale based on the PD estimated for each obligor assigned to this exposure class
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 34.07 rows 0010 - 0170, PDF page 207

> the institution shall report the number of legal entities/obligors which were separately rated, regardless of the number of different loans or exposures granted.
>

> Netting sets containing only SFTs, as defined in Article 4(1)(139) CRR. SFTs that are included in a contractual cross product netting set and therefore reported in row 0130 shall not be reported in this row. [...] Netting sets containing only derivatives listed in Annex II CRR and long settlement transactions as defined in Article 272(2) CRR.

#### Why a correct return fails

**OF 08.01 against OF 08.03 (boe_b0737).** Write N for the distinct obligors on a sheet, A for the obligors with a non-CCR exposure (what OF 08.03 counts, because OF 08.03 excludes CCR), and S, D, X for the obligors with an SFT, a derivative and a cross-product netting set. Annex II defines every one of these cells as a count of legal entities 'regardless of the number of different loans or exposures granted'. The rule asserts N - (S + D + X) = A. That is an identity only when no obligor sits in two of the groups. If B obligors have both a loan and a swap, N - D = A - B, so the rule is short by B. If an obligor has both an SFT and a derivative netting set, S + D counts it twice and the left side is short again. Separately, the boe_b0836 family requires S + D + X = the number of CCR counterparties in OF 34.07, while boe_b0737 requires S + D + X = N - A (the CCR-only obligors): the two cannot both hold once an obligor has a loan and a CCR netting set, where N (row 0010) is the distinct count that p.114 asks for. The rounding allowance is at most 0.5 per integer fact stated with decimals 0 (0.5 x 4 = 2 in the example, at most 0.5 x 12 = 6 if every CCR row and every PD range is reported; none for a count stated with decimals INF, which the Filing Manual's rule 2.18 also allows), so about seven overlapping obligors always break the rule.

**OF 34.07 against OF 08.01 (boe_b1035 and its siblings).** OF 34.07 counts each CCR counterparty once ('determined at counterparty level', 'regardless of the number of different loans or exposures granted'). OF 08.01 row 0040 counts the obligors with an SFT netting set and row 0050 the obligors with a derivatives netting set. A counterparty with a repo agreement and a derivatives agreement - and no cross-product netting agreement, so nothing in row 0060 - is one obligor in OF 34.07 and is counted in both OF 08.01 rows. With K such counterparties the right side exceeds the left by K. The allowance is at most 0.5 per integer fact stated with decimals 0 (0.5 x 4 = 2 with all four facts reported, 1.5 with rows 0040 and 0050 only), so two such counterparties can break the rule and three always do; a count stated with decimals INF (allowed by the Filing Manual's rule 2.18) has no allowance, and one is enough.

#### Worked example

One FIRB return with two sheets (reference date 31 March 2027). Sheet 0012, corporates - other general corporates - non-SME: 30 obligors - 10 with a loan only, 10 with a loan and an interest-rate swap hedging it, 10 with a swap only. OF 08.01: r0010 = exposure value 2,400,000, RWEA 1,443,000, 30 obligors (legal entities); r0020 (loans) 2,000,000 / 1,200,000 / 20; r0050 (derivatives netting sets) 400,000 / 243,000 / 20; r0070 as r0010. OF 08.03, which excludes counterparty credit risk: the 20 borrowers in PD ranges r0050 (12 obligors, exposure value 1,200,000, RWEA 660,000) and r0060 (8 obligors, 800,000, 540,000). OF 34.07: the 20 swap counterparties in one PD band and the Total (exposure value 400,000, PD 0.40%, LGD 40%, average maturity 3 years, RWEA 243,000, density 0.6075). boe_b0737 computes 30 - 20 = 10 against 20. Sheet 0006, institutions: 12 banks, all with a derivatives netting set and 10 of them also with a repo netting set, no cross-product netting. OF 08.01: r0010 = 900,000 / 339,000 / 12; r0040 (SFT netting sets) 300,000 / 76,000 / 10; r0050 600,000 / 263,000 / 12; r0070 as r0010. OF 34.07: one PD band and the Total (900,000, PD 0.20%, LGD 45%, 12 obligors, average maturity 2 years, RWEA 339,000, density 0.3767). boe_b1035 computes 12 against 10 + 12 = 22, and boe_b0737 12 - 22 = -10 against no OF 08.03 obligors on the sheet. The amount ties boe_b0736 / boe_b0738 and the OF 34.07 checks hold.

#### Other ways of reporting considered

**OF 08.01 against OF 08.03 (boe_b0737).** (a) Total reported as 20 + 20 = 40: every rule passes in Arelle, but r0010 then counts ten legal entities twice, contrary to 'regardless of the number of different loans or exposures granted' (p.114). It is rejected on the wording of p.114, not on test results: the convention 'row 0010 = the OF 08.03 count plus the CCR rows' always satisfies boe_b0737. With the total reported otherwise, when the 20 borrowers have a drawn loan and an undrawn commitment as well, the rule fails with the total reported as the distinct count (30) and as the sum of the category rows (60) alike - boe_b0737 is [0,1] either way. (b) r0050 c0300 counting only the 10 swap-only obligors: boe_b0737 passes, boe_b0846 fails [0,1] because OF 34.07 has 20 CCR counterparties. (c) r0050 c0300 left empty: boe_b0737 [0,1] and boe_b0846 [0,1]. No Annex-II-compliant way of counting satisfies the rule.

**OF 34.07 against OF 08.01 (boe_b1035 and its siblings).** (a) OF 34.07 c0030 counting a counterparty once per netting-set type (22): boe_b1035 passes [1,0], but the cell is then not the number of legal entities 'regardless of the number of different loans or exposures granted' (p.206) and not 'determined at counterparty level' (p.207). (b) De-duplicating across OF 08.01 rows 0040 / 0050 has no basis in the instructions (each row is its own netting-set population) and would need an arbitrary allocation rule. No compliant alternative found.

#### Proposed change

**OF 08.01 against OF 08.03 (boe_b0737).** Deactivate boe_b0737, as the EBA did with v09775_m on 2021-03-10. If a check is wanted, replace it with a one-sided warning that is true for distinct counts: {t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0010, c: 0300} i>= isum({t: OF08.03.01.01, r: 0010; 0040; 0050; 0060; 0070; 0100; 0130; 0170, c: 0060}), severity WARNING, same sheet scope. The amount siblings boe_b0736 / b0738 / b0739 / b0740 are not affected by this point (amounts are additive).

**OF 34.07 against OF 08.01 (boe_b1035 and its siblings).** In each of boe_b0836, b0837, b0840-b0853 and b1035 replace 'i=' by 'i<=' ({t: OF34.07.01.01, r: 0180, c: 0030, z: S} i<= isum({t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0040; 0050; 0060, c: 0300, z: S})) and set severity WARNING; or deactivate the 17 rules, as the EBA has done (deleted from release 3.2 onward). The inequality also survives the two population differences between the templates (slotting, PI-12; exposures cleared through a CCP, PI-13).

#### EBA precedent

**OF 08.01 against OF 08.03 (boe_b0737).** boe_b0737 restates EBA v09775_m (the Bank's own v4.0.0 workbook names it as the equivalent). In the EBA validation rules list v09775_m is severity Warning, deactivated on 2021-03-10 and never reactivated in any release sheet from v3.0 to 3.5 (the formula was re-expressed in 3.2.0 and stayed deactivated). Its siblings v09773_m - v09778_m carry the same deactivation date - including v09774_m (exposure value) and v09776_m (RWEA), which are additive - so the EBA's deactivation does not single out the non-additive count; from 3.2.0 the EBA formula also sums over sheets s0001-s0017 rather than applying per sheet.

**OF 34.07 against OF 08.01 (boe_b1035 and its siblings).** The EBA family is v10521_h - v10537_h ({C 34.07, r0180, c0030, sNNNN} = C 08.01 r0040 + r0050 + r0060 c0300, one per sheet), added in release 3.0.0 with severity Warning, never Error. In the v3.0 and v3.1 sheets of the EBA validation rules list, v10522_h (s0002 Total F-IRB) and v10526_h (s0006 Institutions F-IRB) are deactivated on 2021-09-10 and v10523_h / v10524_h (the two central-government sheets) on 2022-12-12; in the sheets for releases 3.2, 3.3, 3.4 and 3.5 all 17 are flagged Deleted = y. Matched by sheet code (the Bank kept the EBA codes 0001, 0002, 0006, 0009-0012, 0015-0017), boe_b0837 and boe_b1035 restate rules the EBA deactivated; the example's institutions sheet (0006) is one of them. Note: the EBA-equivalent column of the Bank's v4.0.0 workbook pairs these rules by position, not by sheet (boe_b0841, sheet 0010, is paired with v10526_h, the EBA's sheet 0006 rule), so it should not be quoted as a sheet-for-sheet mapping.

#### Who is affected

**OF 08.01 against OF 08.03 (boe_b0737).** Any IRB firm with obligors that have both a CCR netting set and a loan or commitment in the same exposure class (corporate borrowers that hedge with the lender), or both an SFT and a derivatives netting set (bank counterparties), from the first PRA001 return under the PS1/26 instructions (effective 1 January 2027). Blocking.

**OF 34.07 against OF 08.01 (boe_b1035 and its siblings).** Any IRB firm with at least three counterparties on one sheet that have both an SFT netting set and a derivatives netting set without a cross-product netting agreement - the normal position for bank and large financial counterparties. All 17 sheets in principle; realistic on the institution, corporate and Total sheets. Blocking from the first PRA001 return under the PS1/26 instructions.

#### What a firm can do meanwhile

Report the figures the instructions require; do not change correct figures to satisfy the rule. An Error-severity break blocks the submission at the gateway: if the gateway rejects the return on this rule, raise it with the PRA, citing this issue.

<a id="pi-10"></a>

### PI-10 - boe_b0770 uses sum() where its siblings use isum(), so its summed rows get no rounding allowance

**Status:** identified by rwa-filer, not yet raised with the Bank of England.

**Severity:** ERROR (boe_b0770).

**Effect:** a return that follows the reporting instructions fails it. **Cause:** conflicts with another published rule; the rounding allowance the rule gives.

#### The rules

| Rule | Module | Severity | Part in the issue | Where the issue applies | At the gateway |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| boe_b0770 | PRA001 | ERROR | the rule at issue | every evaluation (a break there may also be the return's own) | run as published |
| boe_b0769 | PRA001 | ERROR | holds on the example (control) | - | run as published |
| boe_b0768 | PRA001 | ERROR | holds on the example (control) | - | run as published |
| boe_b0820 | PRA001 | ERROR | related | - | run as published |
| boe_b0821 | PRA001 | ERROR | related | - | run as published |
| boe_b0822 | PRA001 | ERROR | related | - | run as published |
| boe_b0823 | PRA001 | ERROR | related | - | run as published |
| boe_b0829 | PRA001 | ERROR | related | - | run as published |

boe_b0770, as published in taxonomy 4.1.1 (label: "Sum of PD ranges from 10 to 100|"):

```text
{t: OF08.03.01.01, r: 0130, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v0, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i= sum({t: OF08.03.01.01, r: 0140; 0150; 0160, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True, id: v1, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting})
scope({t: OF08.03.01.01, c:0010;0020;0030;0040;0060;0090;0100;0110,z:0001;0002;0006;0009;0010;0011;0012;0015;0016;0017;0018;0019;0020;0021;0022;0023;0024, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting})
```

#### What the rule requires

The 10 to <100 PD band must equal the sum of its three sub-bands on eight columns. In the interval-arithmetic functions shipped in the Bank's package (Eurofiling's interval-arithmetics.xml, www.eurofiling.info/eu/fr/xbrl/func/) a reported fact carries a threshold of 0.5 x 10^-decimals and anything that is not a fact carries 0 (iaf:splitValueThreshold: 'if (not($item instance of element()) and empty($item[2]) and not(contains(string($item), ";"))) then ($item, 0)'), and iaf:numeric-equal is 'abs($itemA[1] - $itemB[1]) le ($itemA[2] + $itemB[2])'. XPath sum($v1) returns a plain number, so boe_b0770 allows only the parent row's own threshold, where boe_b0767-b0769 (iaf:sum) allow the parent's plus every sub-band's.

#### What the instructions and rules say

> In particular, if numbers are truncated or rounded for reporting, they should not be “adjusted” so that they appear to be visually consistent (i.e. so that they “foot” or “cast”) but should instead be simply reported with the appropriate @decimals value – the validation checks will take into account the declared accuracy to determine if reported values are valid.
>
> - Bank of England XBRL Filing Manual v1.0.1, 30 May 2024, rule 2.18, Note, PDF page 24

> Note: This, combined with the definition of the decimals setting, means that in general monetary values must not be truncated to thousands (since the reported value might then be up to 1000 from the true value, which is more than the 500 implied by decimals=-3, requiring instead decimals= –4 to be consistent), but may be rounded (i.e. to nearest value) to thousands
>
> - Bank of England XBRL Filing Manual v1.0.1, rule 2.18, PDF page 25

> The Bank’s XBRL validation rules use interval arithmetic for validation.
>
> - Bank of England XBRL Filing Manual v1.0.1, rule 2.18, PDF page 23

> test="iaf:numeric-equal($v0,sum($v1))"
>
> - Bank of England Banking Taxonomy v4.1.1 (taxonomy package and data point model), banking_reporting/2026-08-17/val/vr-boe_b0770.xml (and vr-boe_b0769.xml: test="iaf:numeric-equal($v0,iaf:sum($v1))")

#### Why a correct return fails

Take three sub-band exposures of 12,345,400, 8,765,400 and 3,210,400 (total 24,321,200) and a filer that rounds each fact to the nearest thousand and states decimals -3, as the Filing Manual permits and the Bank's own sample instance does. Reported: 12,345,000 + 8,765,000 + 3,210,000 = 24,320,000 against a parent of 24,321,000. Every fact is within 500 of its true value. With isum the tolerance would be 4 x 500 = 2,000 and the rule holds; boe_b0770 allows 500 and the difference is 1,000, so it is unsatisfied. The same arithmetic on the two-row bands (21,111,000 against 21,110,000, tolerance 1,500) passes boe_b0768 and boe_b0769. A filer who reports exact units is unaffected.

#### Worked example

OF 08.03 sheet 0012, column 0010 (on-balance-sheet exposures) only, every fact rounded to the nearest thousand and stated at decimals -3. Bands 0.75 to <2.5 and 2.5 to <10 (controls): sub-bands 12,345,000 and 8,765,000, parent 21,111,000 (true 21,110,800). Band 10 to <100: sub-bands 12,345,000, 8,765,000 and 3,210,000, parent 24,321,000 (true 24,321,200).

Arelle's result on it:

| Rule | Satisfied | Unsatisfied | What the example shows |
|---|---|---|---|
| boe_b0767 | 0 | 0 | - |
| boe_b0768 | 1 | 0 | holds |
| boe_b0769 | 1 | 0 | holds |
| boe_b0770 | 0 | 1 | fails |

<details>
<summary>The example's 10 cells</summary>

| Table | Sheet | Key | Row | Column | Value |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| OF08.03.01.01 | 0012 |  | 0080 | 0010 | 12,345,000 |
| OF08.03.01.01 | 0012 |  | 0090 | 0010 | 8,765,000 |
| OF08.03.01.01 | 0012 |  | 0070 | 0010 | 21,111,000 |
| OF08.03.01.01 | 0012 |  | 0110 | 0010 | 12,345,000 |
| OF08.03.01.01 | 0012 |  | 0120 | 0010 | 8,765,000 |
| OF08.03.01.01 | 0012 |  | 0100 | 0010 | 21,111,000 |
| OF08.03.01.01 | 0012 |  | 0140 | 0010 | 12,345,000 |
| OF08.03.01.01 | 0012 |  | 0150 | 0010 | 8,765,000 |
| OF08.03.01.01 | 0012 |  | 0160 | 0010 | 3,210,000 |
| OF08.03.01.01 | 0012 |  | 0130 | 0010 | 24,321,000 |

</details>

#### Other ways of reporting considered

Report every figure unrounded in units, as the Filing Manual prefers ('reported as known'): passes. Or adjust the rounded parent so that it foots (24,320,000): passes, but the Manual tells firms not to do this. A firm that rounds each fact correctly and declares decimals -3, which the Manual expressly allows, fails boe_b0770 and nothing in the instructions lets it pass.

#### Proposed change

Change sum to isum in boe_b0770 so that it matches boe_b0767-b0769: {t: OF08.03.01.01, r: 0130, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v0} i= isum({t: OF08.03.01.01, r: 0140; 0150; 0160, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True, id: v1}) (XBRL test iaf:numeric-equal($v0,iaf:sum($v1))). Review the five other interval rules that divide a plain sum, boe_b0820, boe_b0821, boe_b0822, boe_b0823 and boe_b0829, for the same substitution.

#### EBA precedent

The EBA original v09756_m is '{r0130} = {r0140} + {r0150} + {r0160}' with 'Arithmetic approach: Interval', the same as v09753_m to v09755_m. The plain sum is in the Bank's v4.0.0 and v4.1.1 workbook text and in the v4.1.1 formula alone among the four.

#### Who is affected

Any firm that rounds monetary facts (to thousands, say) and states the matching decimals, on OF 08.03 band 10 to <100 on any of the eight columns: it fails whenever the rounding errors of the three sub-bands and the parent add to more than the parent's own allowance. Firms that file exact units are not affected.

#### What a firm can do meanwhile

Report the figures the instructions require; do not change correct figures to satisfy the rule. An Error-severity break blocks the submission at the gateway: if the gateway rejects the return on this rule, raise it with the PRA, citing this issue.

<a id="pi-11"></a>

### PI-11 - OF 34.07 band totals sum average maturity and RWEA density, contradicting boe_b0759

**Status:** identified by rwa-filer, not yet raised with the Bank of England.

**Severity:** ERROR (boe_b0834, boe_b0831).

**Effect:** a return that follows the reporting instructions fails it. **Cause:** contradicts the reporting instructions; conflicts with another published rule.

#### The rules

| Rule | Module | Severity | Part in the issue | Where the issue applies | At the gateway |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| boe_b0834 | PRA001 | ERROR | the rule at issue | OF34.07.01.01 columns 0050, 0070 | run as published |
| boe_b0831 | PRA001 | ERROR | the rule at issue | OF34.07.01.01 columns 0050, 0070 | run as published |
| boe_b0759 | PRA001 | ERROR | cannot hold together with it | - | run as published |
| boe_b0830 | PRA001 | ERROR | related | - | run as published |
| boe_b0832 | PRA001 | ERROR | related | - | run as published |
| boe_b0833 | PRA001 | ERROR | related | - | run as published |

boe_b0834, as published in taxonomy 4.1.1 (label: "Total PD (Pre-input floor) is the sum of the stated PD ranges|"):

```text
{t: OF34.07.01.01, r: 0180, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v0, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i= isum({t: OF34.07.01.01, r: 0010; 0040; 0050; 0060; 0070; 0100; 0130; 0170, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True, id: v1, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting})
scope({t: OF34.07.01.01, c:0010;0030;0050;0060;0070,z:0001;0002;0006;0009;0010;0011;0012;0015;0016;0017;0018;0019;0020;0021;0022;0023;0024, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting})
```

boe_b0831, as published in taxonomy 4.1.1 (label: "Sum of PD ranges pre-input floor (%) from 0.75 to 2.50|"):

```text
{t: OF34.07.01.01, r: 0070, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v0, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i= isum({t: OF34.07.01.01, r: 0080; 0090, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True, id: v1, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting})
scope({t: OF34.07.01.01, c:0010;0030;0050;0060;0070,z:0001;0002;0006;0009;0010;0011;0012;0015;0016;0017;0018;0019;0020;0021;0022;0023;0024, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting})
```

#### What the rule requires

boe_b0830 - b0834: on every OF 34.07 sheet, each PD-band subtotal row equals the sum of its sub-bands and the Total row (0180) equals the sum of the eight top-level bands, for each of columns 0010 (exposure value), 0030 (number of obligors), 0050 (exposure-weighted average maturity), 0060 (RWEA) and 0070 (density of RWEA). boe_b0759: on every row including the subtotals and the Total, c0070 x c0010 = c0060. All blocking (ERROR).

#### What the instructions and rules say

> Density of risk-weighted exposure amounts Ratio of the total risk-weighted exposure amounts (reported in column 0060) to the exposure value (reported in column 0010).
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 34.07 column 0070, PDF page 207

> Exposure weighted average maturity (years) Average of obligor maturities in years weighted by their corresponding exposure value as defined for column 0010.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 34.07 column 0050, PDF page 207

#### Why a correct return fails

Two bands with exposure values E1, E2 and densities d1, d2 (RWEA = d x E). boe_b0834 on c0010 and c0060 makes the Total row E1 + E2 and d1E1 + d2E2; boe_b0759 on the Total row then forces its density to (d1E1 + d2E2) / (E1 + E2), which is also what Annex II defines. boe_b0834 on c0070 forces the same cell to d1 + d2. Both hold only if d1E2 + d2E1 = 0, that is only if one band alone carries exposure. The same algebra applies to every subtotal row (boe_b0830 - b0833). For c0050 no second rule pins the cell, but Annex II defines it as an exposure-weighted average, and the sum of two averages is not the average: reporting the Annex II figure fails the rule, reporting the sum satisfies the rule and misstates the cell. c0050 is an integer-typed metric (eba_met:ii791), so the allowance is 0.5 per fact; two bands with maturities of two years or more already exceed it.

#### Worked example

Institutions (FIRB), sheet 0006, three populated PD bands. r0040: exposure value 500,000, 7 obligors, maturity 2 years, RWEA 120,000, density 0.24. r0080: 300,000, 3 obligors, maturity 4, RWEA 180,000, density 0.60. r0090: 100,000, 2 obligors, maturity 5, RWEA 80,000, density 0.80. As Annex II defines them: subtotal r0070 = exposure value 400,000, 5 obligors, maturity (300,000 x 4 + 100,000 x 5) / 400,000 = 4.25 reported 4, RWEA 260,000, density 260,000 / 400,000 = 0.65; Total r0180 = 900,000, 12 obligors, maturity 2,700,000 / 900,000 = 3, RWEA 380,000, density 380,000 / 900,000 = 0.4222. The rules want r0070 maturity 9 and density 1.40, and - with r0070 at those values - Total maturity 11 and density 1.64 (with r0070 at the Annex II values, 4 and 0.65, boe_b0834 asks the Total for 6 and 0.89).

Arelle's result on it:

| Rule | Satisfied | Unsatisfied | What the example shows |
|---|---|---|---|
| boe_b0759 | 5 | 0 | - |
| boe_b0830 | 0 | 0 | - |
| boe_b0831 | 3 | 2 | fails |
| boe_b0832 | 0 | 0 | - |
| boe_b0833 | 0 | 0 | - |
| boe_b0834 | 3 | 2 | fails |

#### Other ways of reporting considered

(a) Subtotal and Total c0050 / c0070 reported as the sums the rules ask for: boe_b0831 [5,0] and b0834 [5,0], but boe_b0759 [3,2] - it fails on r0070 and r0180 - and both cells contradict their Annex II definitions. (b) c0050 and c0070 left empty on the subtotal and Total rows: boe_b0831 [3,2], b0834 [3,2], b0759 [3,2] (an empty cell is read as 0). (c) c0050 and c0070 not reported on any row: boe_b0759 [0,5]. No way of reporting two populated bands passes all six rules.

#### Proposed change

Change the scope of boe_b0830, b0831, b0832, b0833 and b0834 from c:0010;0030;0050;0060;0070 to c:0010;0030;0060 (sheets unchanged), matching EBA v09836_m - v09840_m as reactivated on 2022-03-10. Keep boe_b0759 as it is.

#### EBA precedent

The EBA originals are v09836_m - v09840_m on C 34.07 (band sums) and v09843_m ({c0070} * {c0010} = {c0060}, all rows), all severity Warning. In the v3.0 and v3.1 sheets of the EBA validation rules list the five band-sum rules have columns (All) and are deactivated on 2021-06-30. From release 3.2.0 they are marked 'Change+Reactivate' (reactivated 2022-03-10) with columns restricted to (0010;0030;0060) - the EBA's fix was exactly to drop the averaged and ratio columns. The Bank's scope (0010;0030;0050;0060;0070) drops c0020 and c0040 but keeps c0050 and c0070. These EBA rules are therefore not simply 'deactivated': a reading of the v3.0 sheet alone does not show the 3.2.0 change and reactivation. v09843_m is live in every release sheet.

#### Who is affected

Every firm that reports OF 34.07 with exposure in more than one PD band on any sheet - in practice every IRB firm with CCR exposures - from the first PRA001 return under the PS1/26 instructions. Blocking, and unavoidable: the choice is between failing boe_b0830 - b0834 or failing boe_b0759.

#### What a firm can do meanwhile

Report the figures the instructions require; do not change correct figures to satisfy the rule. An Error-severity break blocks the submission at the gateway: if the gateway rejects the return on this rule, raise it with the PRA, citing this issue.

#### What the rule requires

On sheets 0002 (Total, FIRB or slotting) and 0010 (Specialised lending, FIRB or slotting), the OF 34.07 Total row must equal the sum of OF 08.01 rows 0040-0060 for exposure value (boe_b0873, b0877), RWEA (b0855, b0859) and number of obligors (b0837, b0841); and boe_b0834 requires the same OF 34.07 Total row to equal the sum of its PD bands. All blocking.

#### What the instructions and rules say

In OF CR IRB 2, OF CR IRB 3, OF CR IRB 5 and OF 34.7, “FIRB” in cases where the FIRB approach is applied; and “AIRB” in cases where the AIRB approach is applied.

#### Why a correct return fails

A swap with a specialised-lending borrower whose exposures are on the slotting approach is a CCR exposure: Annex II sends it to OF 08.01 rows 0040-0060 on sheets 0010 and 0002 (it is part of the Total and of row 0080; OF 08.06 has an 'of which: arising from counterparty credit risk' column for it, and the Bank's boe_b0821 ties that column to OF 08.01 row 0080). OF 34.07 allocates exposures to PD buckets 'based on the PD estimated for each obligor'; under slotting no PD is estimated, so the exposure has no bucket. If it is left out of OF 34.07 (the reading of paragraph 75, which lists OF 34.7 as FIRB / AIRB only), the Total is short of OF 08.01 rows 0040-0060 by the slotting CCR amount and the six cross-template rules fail. If it is included in the Total only (the reading of paragraph 130 and of the sheet labels 'FIRB approach or slotting approach'), the Total exceeds the sum of the PD bands and boe_b0834 fails. One blocking rule fails either way.

#### Worked example

A bank with FIRB institutions and slotting specialised lending. Institutions (sheet 0006): 12 derivative counterparties, exposure value 600,000, RWEA 180,000. Specialised lending, all slotting (sheet 0010): 15 income-producing real-estate borrowers, loans with exposure value 3,000,000 / RWEA 2,100,000 and an interest-rate swap each, 150,000 / 105,000 in total. OF 08.01 sheet 0010: r0010 3,150,000 / 2,205,000, r0020 3,000,000 / 2,100,000, r0050 150,000 / 105,000, r0080 3,150,000 / 2,205,000, 15 obligors on each row, c0130 = 150,000; sheet 0002 = 0006 + 0010 (r0050 exposure value 750,000, RWEA 285,000, 27 obligors). OF 08.06 r0095: exposure value 3,150,000, of which counterparty credit risk 150,000, RWEA 2,205,000. OF 34.07: institutions only on sheets 0006 and 0002 (exposure value 600,000, 12 obligors, RWEA 180,000), nothing on sheet 0010 because the slotting swaps have no PD bucket.

#### Other ways of reporting considered

(a) Slotting swaps included in the OF 34.07 Total rows only, since they have no PD bucket: the six cross-template rules pass [1,0] each and boe_b0834 fails [6,8] - on sheets 0010 and 0002 the Total no longer equals the sum of the bands for exposure value, obligors, RWEA and density. (b) Slotting swaps allocated to a PD bucket: every rule passes (boe_b0834 [15,0], the six rules [1,0]), but no PD is estimated for a slotting exposure, so the bucket is invented and contradicts the row instruction on p.207. (c) Reporting the swaps outside OF 08.01 rows 0040-0060 is excluded by the row 0020 instruction (p.115). There is no compliant way through.

#### Proposed change

First settle the instruction: state in Annex II whether OF 34.07 includes slotting CCR exposures (paragraph 75 says FIRB / AIRB only, paragraph 130 and the sheet labels say 'FIRB or slotting'). If they are excluded (the only reading the PD-scale rows can hold): for exposure value, subtract the slotting CCR amount - boe_b0877: {t: OF34.07.01.01, r: 0180, c: 0010, z: 0010} i= isum({t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0040; 0050; 0060, c: 0110, z: 0010}) i- {t: OF08.01.01.02, r: 0080, c: 0130, z: 0010, dv: 0}, and the same on z: 0002 for boe_b0873; for RWEA and obligors (boe_b0855, b0859, b0837, b0841) OF 08.01 has no cell that isolates slotting CCR, so change 'i=' to 'i<=' or deactivate. If they are to be included, OF 34.07 needs a row for exposures without a PD and boe_b0834 must add it. A single change of 'i<=' with severity WARNING would cover the family, but should not lean on PI-13, which remains an open question of interpretation.

#### EBA precedent

Matched by sheet code, the EBA rules on s0002 (Total F-IRB) - v10522_h (c0030), v10539_h (c0060), v10701_h (c0010) - and on s0010 (Specialised lending F-IRB) - v10547_h (c0060), v10709_h (c0010) - were deactivated on 2021-09-10; v10530_h (c0030, s0010) was not deactivated. All are severity Warning and all are flagged Deleted from release 3.2 onward (EBA validation rules list). The EBA does not publish its reason, and the same date also deactivated the three rules of sheet s0006 (institutions, F-IRB, which has no slotting): the pattern is the F-IRB sheets s0002 / s0006 / s0010, not specific evidence for this gap. The CRR Annex II text (CRR COREP Annex II p.185, para 130) labels the C 34.07 sheets 'NO' = Foundation IRB / 'YES' = Advanced IRB with no mention of slotting; PS1/26 paragraph 130 added 'or slotting'.

#### Who is affected

Of the 51 rules that tie OF 34.07 to OF 08.01, this population difference reaches six - boe_b0837, b0841, b0855, b0859, b0873, b0877 (sheets 0002 and 0010) - together with boe_b0834. It affects any firm with CCR exposures (typically hedging swaps) to specialised-lending borrowers on the slotting approach, from the first PRA001 return under the PS1/26 instructions. Blocking and unavoidable for such a firm.

#### What a firm can do meanwhile

Report the figures the instructions require; do not change correct figures to satisfy the rule. An Error-severity break blocks the submission at the gateway: if the gateway rejects the return on this rule, raise it with the PRA, citing this issue.

#### What the rule requires

**Average maturities typed as whole numbers.** No validation rule is at fault. The taxonomy dictionary types the two maturity metrics as integers: eba_met:ii163 'Maturity value (days)' is the only metric of OF 08.01 c0250 (306 cells) and OF 08.02 c0250 (17), and eba_met:ii791 'Maturity value (years)' of OF 08.03 c0080 (306) and OF 34.07 c0050 (323). An integer item cannot carry a fraction, and the Bank's filing manual gives decimals 0 for an integer (it also accepts INF, 'exact as written', for every numeric type).

**Ratios typed as monetary amounts.** The dictionary types eba_met:mi796 'Exposure weighted conversion factors' (OF 08.03 c0030, 306 cells) and eba_met:mi784 'Alpha used for computing regulatory exposure value' (C 34.02 r0040 c0140, 2 cells) as xbrli:monetaryItemType. A monetary fact must carry an ISO 4217 currency unit, and the Bank's filing manual lets a monetary fact be stated as loosely as decimals=-3 (accurate to thousands).

**The same outside the credit-risk tables.** b0805/b0807/b0810/b0812 define the ten-year-average count as an arithmetic mean, isum/count, which in general is not a whole number. b0405 requires the mCVA multiplier cell to be reported. The cell types themselves are fixed by the dictionary.

#### Why it matters

**Average maturities typed as whole numbers.** It does not, provided the figure is rounded. Tested in Arelle: a fractional literal in either metric (912.5 days, 2.5 years) is an XML Schema validity error (xmlSchema:valueError, level ERROR) - the instance is not valid XBRL - and every formula that reads the fact aborts with err:FORG0001; stating decimals="2" on it adds filing-rule error EBA.2.18 ('Integer fact eba_met:ii163 of context c3 has a decimals attribute ≠ 0'). The same return with whole numbers (912 days and 2 years under the rounding the Filing Manual's rule 2.18 prescribes, roundTiesToEven; Arelle accepts any integer) with decimals="0" loads with no message and every rule evaluates. So the type does not block filing: Annex II fixes the unit (days / years) and no precision, the taxonomy fixes whole units, and the two are reconciled by rounding half-to-even as rule 2.18 prescribes. What is left for the Bank: (1) Annex II never says the average is rounded, so a firm discovers it from an XBRL validity error; (2) for the two YEARS cells a whole number is close to uninformative - an average of 2.5 years is filed as 2, of 3.4 as 3; in DAYS the loss is at most half a day and is immaterial.

**Ratios typed as monetary amounts.** It does not. Arelle (filing rules on) accepts <eba_met:mi796 unitRef=GBP decimals="4">0.4</> and <eba_met:mi784 unitRef=GBP decimals="2">1.4</> with no message; the same facts with the pure unit are XBRL-invalid (xbrl.4.8.2:monetaryFactUnit-notMonetaryMeasure, ERROR, plus the WARNING EBA.2.23). So a firm must file a conversion factor of 0.38 as 'GBP 0.38' and alpha as 'GBP 1.4'. The only published alpha cell is C 34.02 row 0040 (IMM), where alpha may be an own estimate (Article 284(4) and (9)), which is why v10633_m tests it as at least 1.2: alpha 1.4 at decimals=-3 satisfies it and 1.19 at decimals=-3 does not. Two consequences need stating precisely: (a) a +/-500 rounding allowance makes the conversion-factor rules vacuous only when the fact is stated at decimals=-3 (the filing manual's minimum for monetary, and a house default applied to every monetary fact): r0070 = 0.38 against r0080 + r0090 = 0.30 + 0.50 satisfies boe_b0768 at decimals=-3 [2,0] and breaks it at decimals=2 [1,1]; (b) v10633_m is a plain '>=' and is unaffected by the type - alpha 1.0 is unsatisfied at decimals=-3 and at 2 alike. The real cost of the typing is that the stated accuracy of a ratio is governed by money conventions: footnote 11 calls more than 2 decimals 'generally inappropriate' for a calculated monetary value, which discourages stating an average conversion factor more precisely than +/-0.005 (the SHOULD is in rule 2.18(c); the footnote is an example, and Arelle accepts decimals=4 on the fact with no message).

**The same outside the credit-risk tables.** OF16.00.01.05 c0110 rows 0020/0040/0070/0090 use boe_met:ii10043/ii10045 (xbrli:integerItemType), the same metric as the yearly counts. The exact mean of ten counts cannot be filed. Arelle confirms that 3.9 raises 'xmlSchema:valueError ... type integer value error: 3.9' and err:FORG0001 inside boe_b0805, so the firm must round, and Annex II gives no rounding convention. A rounded value passes the interval comparison. OF25.03.01.01 r0070 c0030 (mCVA, a pure multiplier fixed at 1) uses boe_met:mi10009 (monetaryItemType), so it needs a currency unit. C14.00.01.01 c0204 (a maturity) uses eba_met:mi663 and C14.01.01.01 c0351/c0361 (a % RW) use eba_met:mi640, both monetaryItemType in the EBA dictionary shipped in the Bank's package. None of these makes a correctly rounded or united value fail a rule. They are typing defects, and that is why this issue is listed with the defects rather than as a clarification question although no rule result shows it: nothing in the text is open to two readings - the taxonomy declares a type the instructions contradict, so a figure the instructions ask for (an average in days or years, a ratio) cannot be filed as they describe it, and only the Bank can correct the dictionary.

#### Other ways of reporting considered

**Average maturities typed as whole numbers.** (1) The fraction with decimals=0: XBRL-invalid (xmlSchema:valueError). (2) The fraction with decimals=2: invalid, plus EBA.2.18. (3) The value rounded to a whole unit with decimals=0: accepted - this is the compliant way and the only one. (4) Leaving the cell empty: no rule requires c0250 / c0080 / c0050 to be present, so it would pass, but Annex II asks for the figure. There is no decimal-typed alternative data point for any of the four cells.

**Ratios typed as monetary amounts.** Pure unit: invalid XBRL (tested). Percent scale (38 instead of 0.38): no instruction supports it and every PRA001 rule compares ratios as fractions. A different data point: none exists for either cell. Stating decimals=4: accepted by Arelle, but discouraged by the SHOULD of rule 2.18(c), which footnote 11 illustrates.

**The same outside the credit-risk tables.** Rounding to the nearest integer is the only fileable option and passes the rules. Annex II does not say to round.

#### Proposed change

**Average maturities typed as whole numbers.** No rule change. (1) Add to Annex II, at OF 08.01 c0250 (p.111), OF 08.03 c0080 (p.121) and OF 34.07 c0050 (p.207): 'The average shall be reported as a whole number of days / years, rounded to the nearest whole unit (ties to even).' (2) For the two cells in YEARS, preferably replace eba_met:ii791 with a decimal metric (xbrli:decimalItemType - the dictionary already has decimal metrics, such as the Bank's own boe_met:ri10063) so that an average of 2.5 years can be reported as such; the Bank already mints its own metrics for these templates (boe_met:pi10057 on OF 08.03 c0050 and OF 34.07 c0020).

**Ratios typed as monetary amounts.** Retype the two data points: OF 08.03 c0030 to a percentage metric (num:percentItemType, pure unit, decimals >= 4 - e.g. a new boe_met:pi... as the Bank did with boe_met:pi10057) and C 34.02 c0140 to a decimal metric (xbrli:decimalItemType, as boe_met:ri10063 'Internal loss multiplier value'). Until then, state in Annex II or the filing manual the accuracy at which these two monetary-typed ratios are to be filed (decimals >= 2, or >= 4), since the general monetary minimum of -3 is meaningless for them. The same pattern elsewhere in the taxonomy: eba_met:mi663 'Exposure-weighted average maturity of assets' (C 14.00 c0204) and boe_met:mi10009 'mCVA multiplier' (OF 25.03 c0030) are also monetary.

**The same outside the credit-risk tables.** Give OF16.00.01.05 c0110 rows 0020/0040/0070/0090 a decimal metric (a new boe_met ri-type 'average number of ...'), or state a rounding convention in Annex II. Type OF25.03.01.01 r0070 c0030 as a pure decimal (ri), or drop the cell, since rule 5.24(2) fixes mCVA at 1. Replace eba_met:mi663 in C 14.00 c0204 with a decimal (years) metric and eba_met:mi640 in C 14.01 c0351/c0361 with a percentage (pi) metric in the Bank's dictionary.

#### EBA precedent

**Average maturities typed as whole numbers.** The metrics are the EBA's own (ii163 in force since 2013-12-01, ii791 since 2021-06-30), so EU COREP has the same constraint. In EBA Q&A 2026_7840 (submitted 23/04/2026, rejected 15/10/2026) a bank wrote: 'as the Maturity is required to be rounded to full days and cannot be delivered with decimals, the rule cannot be met as the rounding will cause a difference between the templates'; Q&A 2026_7881 asked 'should the column 250 of the C.08.01 and C.08.02 be reported as integers or decimals?'. Q&A 2026_7840 was rejected (15/10/2026) because the matter 'has already been identified and will be considered for a forthcoming version of the Reporting framework / release of the respective validation rules'; 2026_7881 was rejected (30/09/2026) as the same matter as 2026_7840. The Bank's counterpart of the rule at issue there (v10667_m), boe_b0758, is not in the taxonomy package, so that rounding conflict cannot arise at the Bank's gateway. No EBA answer says how to round.

**Ratios typed as monetary amounts.** Both metrics are the EBA's (created 2020-11-15, in force 2021-06-30), so EU COREP C 08.03 c0030 and C 34.02 c0140 carry the same typing. The same dictionary types a conversion factor correctly elsewhere: eba_met:pi370 'Credit conversion factor' is num:percentItemType (a dictionary metric that no PRA001 cell uses). No EBA Q&A on the point was found.

**The same outside the credit-risk tables.** mi663 and mi640 are EBA dictionary metrics typed monetaryItemType in the EBA met.xsd shipped in the Bank's package; the defect is inherited. Whether the EBA has since retyped them was not checked. ii10043, ii10045 and mi10009 are Bank metrics.

#### Who is affected

**Average maturities typed as whole numbers.** Every IRB firm filing PRA001 from the first 2027 reference date, on OF 08.01, OF 08.02, OF 08.03 and OF 34.07. No return is rejected if the average is rounded.

**Ratios typed as monetary amounts.** Every IRB firm with off-balance-sheet exposure (OF 08.03 c0030) and every IMM firm (C 34.02 r0040 c0140 is the only alpha cell the taxonomy publishes). Nothing is rejected, but the type decides whether three ERROR rules on c0030 can fail at all (PI-09).

**The same outside the credit-risk tables.** Low impact. OF 16 Part 5 filers must silently round the average counts. mCVA and the C 14 maturity and RW cells must carry a currency unit. No rule fails.

#### What a firm can do meanwhile

No validation result shows this issue. Report as the instructions require, and keep a record of any rounding or convention you had to adopt.

#### What the rule requires

**Retail purchased receivables, row 0105 (boe_b0300-b0302).** boe_b0783 requires OF 09.02 row 0060 (Retail) to equal the sum of rows 0071, 0072, 0073, 0074, 0100, 0105, 0120 and 0130 in each of the twelve monetary columns, on every country sheet. boe_b0291 / b0292 / b0293 require row 0060 on the all-countries sheet to equal the sum of row 0010 across the seven OF 08.01 retail sheets (0015-0021) for original exposure, exposure value and RWEA. A further 22 rules (boe_b0294-b0302, b0304, b1056-b1066, b1071; 21 distinct, because boe_b0304 and boe_b1057 are the same expression) require each of the seven other retail rows to equal row 0010 of exactly one OF 08.01 sheet in those three columns. No rule ties row 0105 to anything in OF 08.01.

**Corporate purchased receivables, row 0049 (boe_b1053-b1055).** boe_b0785 requires OF 09.02 row 0030 (Corporates) to equal rows 0042 + 0045 + 0048 + 0049 + 0050 + 0055 in each of the twelve monetary columns, on every country sheet where row 0030 is reported. boe_b0282 / b0283 / b0284 require row 0030 on the all-countries sheet to equal the sum of row 0010 across OF 08.01 sheets 0009, 0010, 0011, 0012, 0022, 0023 and 0024 for original exposure, exposure value and RWEA. boe_b1034 / b1051 / b1052 require row 0048 = sheet 0022; boe_b0288-b0290 require row 0050 = sheets 0023 + 0024; boe_b1053-b1055 require row 0055 = sheet 0011 / sheet 0012; boe_b0285-b0287 require row 0042 <= sheets 0009 + 0010. Rows 0045 and 0049 have no tie to OF 08.01.

#### Why a correct return fails

**Retail purchased receivables, row 0105 (boe_b0300-b0302).** Take the all-countries sheet and one of the three tied column pairs (OF 09.02 c0010 / c0105 / c0110 against OF 08.01 c0020 / c0110 / c0260). Write S15 ... S21 for row 0010 of the seven OF 08.01 retail sheets. (1) boe_b0783: r0060 = r0071 + r0072 + r0073 + r0074 + r0100 + r0105 + r0120 + r0130. (2) boe_b0291 / b0292 / b0293: r0060 = S15 + S16 + S17 + S18 + S19 + S20 + S21. (3) Seven one-row-one-sheet equalities: r0100 = S15, r0120 = S16, r0130 = S17, r0073 = S18, r0074 = S19, r0071 = S20, r0072 = S21. Putting (3) into (1) and comparing with (2) leaves r0105 = 0: nine evaluations per column (ten for RWEA, where boe_b0304 and boe_b1057 both evaluate), and no step depends on how the firm reads Annex II. A purchased retail receivable has to sit in one of S15 ... S21: Article 147(2)(d) gives retail exactly three subclasses and purchased receivables are not one of them (they are a roll-out class, Art. 147B(1)(g)); Annex II para 76 lists no purchased-receivables sheet; and OF 08.01 row 0175 shows them inside each class sheet. In the taxonomy, row 0105 carries its own exposure-class member (boe_eba_EC:x10011, 'Retail exposures - purchased receivables') and sits beside rows 0100 / 0120 / 0130 under 'Retail' with no 'Of which' label, while no OF 08.01 sheet carries that member. That support for a separate row is not conclusive: the row's data points also carry eba_dim:MCB = boe_eba_MC:x10070 ('Purchased receivables', the member that marks OF 08.01 row 0175), and the Bank's IRB exposure-class hierarchy (EC1001) lists the retail members without x10011. So with r0105 above zero one of three things gives way: the class row is reported net of the receivables and no longer equals its sheet (boe_b0300-b0302 in the example); or it is reported gross and r0060 no longer equals the sum of its rows (boe_b0783); or r0060 is inflated to make the sum work and no longer equals the OF 08.01 sheets (boe_b0291-b0293). The effect is confined to original exposure, exposure value and RWEA on the all-countries sheet; on the separate-row reading the other nine monetary columns of row 0105 and the individual country sheets are subject to boe_b0783 only (on the 'of which' reading boe_b0783 fails on every sheet, in each of its twelve columns where row 0105 is non-zero). Other rules touch row 0105 - boe_b0668 and boe_b0682 (columns 0080 / 0090 / 0100), boe_b0321, boe_b0346-b0349, boe_b0358, boe_b0908 and boe_b1049 - but none forces it to zero. The equalities use interval arithmetic, so 'zero' means zero within the rounding allowance of the reported decimals; at GBP-million scale with decimals -3 (an allowance of 500 per fact) the rules still fail. A possible second mismatch, not tested: every OF 09.02 data point carries risk type eba_TR:x4 (credit risk, counterparty credit risk and free deliveries), while OF 08.01 row 0010 carries eba_TR:x5, which adds dilution risk (row 0180), so dilution amounts sit inside the OF 08.01 totals the ties compare with but outside OF 09.02.

**Corporate purchased receivables, row 0049 (boe_b1053-b1055).** On the all-countries sheet, for each of original exposure, exposure value and RWEA, write S9 ... S24 for row 0010 of the OF 08.01 corporate sheets. (1) boe_b0785: r0030 = r0042 + r0045 + r0048 + r0049 + r0050 + r0055. (2) boe_b0282 / b0283 / b0284: r0030 = S9 + S10 + S11 + S12 + S22 + S23 + S24. (3) r0048 = S22, r0050 = S23 + S24, r0055 = S11 / S12. Substituting leaves r0049 = (S9 + S10) - r0042 - r0045. That looks like a cap, but it is not a real allowance: rows 0042 and 0045 together are all IRB specialised lending, and sheets 0009 and 0010 together are the same population, so on a truthful return r0042 + r0045 = S9 + S10 and r0049 = 0 - with or without specialised lending on the book. A purchased corporate receivable is in one of the corporate class sheets (Art. 147(2)(c) has three subclasses and purchased receivables are not one of them; para 76 lists no sheet for them; OF 08.01 row 0175 shows them inside each sheet). For row 0055 Annex II is explicit - it is what is 'not reported in 0042-0050' - while rows 0048 and 0050 (pp.143-144) have no such carve-out, so for receivables of SME or financial / large corporate obligors the text has the same gap as for retail; so the receivables go in row 0049 and row 0055 is reported net of them - and then boe_b1053-b1055 fail because row 0055 no longer equals the whole sheet (the algebra as stated is for a firm with one of sheets 0011 / 0012 populated; with both, PI-02 applies as well). Reported the other way round (row 0055 gross), boe_b0785 fails. The only shape that satisfies every rule with r0049 above zero understates row 0042 or row 0045 by exactly the receivables amount. Which corporate row the receivables stay inside depends on the obligor: rows 0048, 0050 or 0055. Confined to the three tied columns on the all-countries sheet; the same failures occur at GBP-million scale with decimals -3.

#### Worked example

A firm with AIRB retail and FIRB corporates, all obligors in one country (reference date 31 March 2027). Retail, AIRB: qualifying revolving 500,000 original exposure / 400,000 exposure value / 120,000 RWEA (OF 08.01 sheet 0015); other retail non-SME 1,000,000 / 1,000,000 / 400,000 (sheet 0017), of which 100,000 / 100,000 / 60,000 are purchased retail receivables - 'other retail' because they are neither qualifying revolving nor secured by residential property (Art. 147(5A)-(5C)); row 0175 shows them on sheet 0017 and on the AIRB total sheet 0001 (1,500,000 / 1,400,000 / 520,000). Corporates, FIRB: financial and large corporates 500,000 / 450,000 / 300,000 (sheet 0022); other general corporates non-SME 1,000,000 / 1,000,000 / 700,000 (sheet 0012), of which 100,000 / 100,000 / 80,000 are purchased corporate receivables (Art. 153(6)); FIRB total sheet 0002 1,500,000 / 1,450,000 / 1,000,000. OF 09.02 all countries, columns 0010 / 0105 / 0110, as Annex II rows 0049 and 0055 are written, and with row 0130 reported net of row 0105 on the separate-row reading (row 0130's own instruction carves out only row 0120; read literally, row 0130 is gross and boe_b0783 fails instead, alternative (B)): r0030 = 1,500,000 / 1,450,000 / 1,000,000; r0048 = 500,000 / 450,000 / 300,000; r0049 = 100,000 / 100,000 / 80,000; r0055 = 900,000 / 900,000 / 620,000 (what is 'not reported in 0042-0050'); r0060 = 1,500,000 / 1,400,000 / 520,000; r0100 = 500,000 / 400,000 / 120,000; r0105 = 100,000 / 100,000 / 60,000; r0130 = 900,000 / 900,000 / 340,000 (other retail net of the receivables in row 0105); r0150 = 3,000,000 / 2,850,000 / 1,520,000. Only sheet 0012 of the two other-general-corporate sheets is populated, so the per-sheet comparison of PI-02 plays no part. Every roll-up and cross-template rule holds except the three retail and the three corporate row ties.

#### Other ways of reporting considered

**Retail purchased receivables, row 0105 (boe_b0300-b0302).** (Figures in thousands.) Four other ways to report the same position, each run through Arelle. (B) Row 0105 as an 'of which' of other retail - r0130 = 1,000 gross, r0105 = 100, r0060 = 1,500: boe_b0783 [0,3], everything else satisfied. (C) As B with r0060 raised to 1,600 / 1,500 / 580 so the rows add up: boe_b0291, b0292, b0293 [0,1] each. (D) Receivables kept out of every OF 08.01 retail class sheet (sheet 0017 = 900, only the AIRB total sheet carries them): boe_b0291-b0293 [0,1] each, and it is not what para 76 or row 0175 describe. (Z) Row 0105 left empty: passes, but omits the figure Annex II asks for in row 0105. Reporting row 0105 only on country sheets, or only in the nine columns without a sheet tie, would leave original exposure, exposure value and RWEA at zero on the all-countries sheet for a row that has exposure. The same algebra applies if the receivables qualify as qualifying revolving or property-secured retail (sheets 0015, 0018-0021): the tie that breaks is then boe_b0294-b0296 or the b1056-b1066 / b1071 family. None of the alternatives is both Annex-II-compliant and rule-satisfying.

**Corporate purchased receivables, row 0049 (boe_b1053-b1055).** (Figures in thousands.) Five other ways to report the same position, each run through Arelle. (B) Row 0049 as an 'of which' of row 0055 - r0055 = 1,000 gross, r0049 = 100, r0030 = 1,500: boe_b0785 [0,3], everything else satisfied. (C) As B with r0030 raised to 1,600 / 1,550 / 1,080: boe_b0282, b0283, b0284 [0,1] each. (D) Receivables kept out of every OF 08.01 corporate class sheet (sheet 0012 = 900, only the FIRB total sheet carries them): boe_b0282-b0284 [0,1] each, and not what para 76 or row 0175 describe. (E1) The firm also has 300 / 300 / 240 of slotting specialised lending on sheet 0010, reported truthfully as r0045, with r0049 = 100 beside r0055 = 1,000: boe_b0785 [0,3] - having specialised lending does not create room. (E2) As E1 but r0045 understated to 200 / 200 / 160: every rule satisfied. This is the 'cap' - it passes only by misstating specialised lending by the receivables amount, and still counts the receivables in both row 0049 and row 0055. (Z) Row 0049 left empty: passes, but omits the figure Annex II asks for. None of the alternatives is both Annex-II-compliant and rule-satisfying.

#### Proposed change

**Retail purchased receivables, row 0105 (boe_b0300-b0302).** State in Annex II whether OF 09.02 row 0105 is a separate breakdown row (rows 0071-0074, 0100, 0120 and 0130 reported net of purchased receivables) or an 'of which' row, then align the rules. Fix A - row 0105 stays a separate row, as the template hierarchy, its own exposure-class member (boe_eba_EC:x10011) and boe_b0783 already treat it: subtract the same sheet's row 0175 in each one-row-one-sheet rule. boe_b0300 becomes {t: OF09.02.01.01, r: 0130, c: 0010, dv: 0, filter: dim(this(), [eba_dim:CEG]) = [eba_GA:x1], id: v0} i= {t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0010, c: 0020, z: 0017, dv: 0, id: v1} i- {t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0175, c: 0020, z: 0017, dv: 0, id: v2}; make the same change in boe_b0294-b0299, b0301, b0302, b0304, b1056-b1066 and b1071 (column pairs c0010/c0020, c0105/c0110, c0110/c0260), and add the missing tie for the row itself: {t: OF09.02.01.01, r: 0105, c: 0010, dv: 0, filter: dim(this(), [eba_dim:CEG]) = [eba_GA:x1], id: v0} i= isum({t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0175, c: 0020, z: 0015; 0016; 0017; 0018; 0019; 0020; 0021, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True, id: v1}), with its c0105/c0110 and c0110/c0260 twins. boe_b0783 and boe_b0291-b0293 stay as they are. Fix B - row 0105 is an 'of which' row: remove 0105 from boe_b0783, i.e. {t: OF09.02.01.01, r: 0060, dv: 0, id: v0} i= isum({t: OF09.02.01.01, r: 0071; 0072; 0073; 0074; 0100; 0120; 0130, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True, id: v1}); keep boe_b0336 (r0060 >= r0105); label the row 'Of which: purchased receivables'. Under either fix, say whether dilution-risk amounts (OF 08.01 row 0180) belong in row 0105, since its definition cites Article 157. The template already treats purchased receivables this way elsewhere: OF 08.07 reports the Article 147B roll-out classes with purchased receivables as separate rows (0200 corporate, 0240 retail) whose sum is row 0260 (Annex II p.135, boe_b0779). Separately, boe_b0304 and boe_b1057 are the same expression; one can be withdrawn.

**Corporate purchased receivables, row 0049 (boe_b1053-b1055).** Fix A - matches Annex II as written for row 0055 (what is 'not reported in 0042-0050'; rows 0048 and 0050 would need the same carve-out) and the template, where row 0049 is a sibling row with its own exposure-class member (boe_eba_EC:x10013): subtract row 0175 of the same sheets in each class-row tie. boe_b1053 becomes {t: OF09.02.01.01, r: 0055, c: 0010, dv: 0, filter: dim(this(), [eba_dim:CEG]) = [eba_GA:x1], id: v0} i= isum({t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0010, c: 0020, z: 0011; 0012, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True, id: v1}) i- isum({t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0175, c: 0020, z: 0011; 0012, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True, id: v2}) - which also supplies the isum the rule lacks today; the same for boe_b1054 and b1055 (c0105/c0110, c0110/c0260); boe_b0288-b0290 with z: 0023; 0024; boe_b1034, b1051, b1052 with z: 0022. Add the missing tie for the row itself: {t: OF09.02.01.01, r: 0049, c: 0010, dv: 0, filter: dim(this(), [eba_dim:CEG]) = [eba_GA:x1], id: v0} i= isum({t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0175, c: 0020, z: 0011; 0012; 0022; 0023; 0024, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True, id: v1}), with its exposure-value and RWEA twins (leaving out the specialised-lending sheets 0009 and 0010, whose rows 0042 / 0045 are not netted; or net those rows as well). boe_b0785 and boe_b0282-b0284 stay as they are. Fix B - if 'of which' is what the Bank intends: remove 0049 from boe_b0785, i.e. {t: OF09.02.01.01, r: 0030, id: v0} i= isum({t: OF09.02.01.01, r: 0042; 0045; 0048; 0050; 0055, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True, id: v1}); keep boe_b1050 (r0030 >= r0049); and amend Annex II row 0055 so it no longer excludes row 0049. Either way, tie row 0045 to OF 08.01 (today it has no cross-template rule, which is what lets an understated row 0045 pass), and say whether dilution-risk amounts (OF 08.01 row 0180) belong in row 0049.

#### EBA precedent

**Retail purchased receivables, row 0105 (boe_b0300-b0302).** The EBA's C 09.02 has no purchased-receivables row (CRR COREP Annex II pp.123-124, rows 0010 to 0150). In the BoE v4.0.0 extract, boe_b0783 is mapped to EBA v2245_h ({r0060} = +{r0110} + {r0100} + {r0070}), deactivated 2014-05-19 and reactivated 2015-02-27, so live (Error) in the EBA list up to 3.5; boe_b0291 and boe_b0300 are mapped to v0440_m and v0475_m, both deactivated 2014-04-16 and reactivated 2015-02-27 (live); boe_b0336 is mapped to v4778_m ({r0060} >= {r0110}, the EBA 'other retail' row); boe_b1056-b1066 and b1071 have no EBA equivalent. The picture is of row 0105 added to an inherited roll-up without the inherited sheet ties being adjusted - an inference, not something the Bank has stated. Not on the Bank's known-issues logs of 27 August and 16 November 2026.

**Corporate purchased receivables, row 0049 (boe_b1053-b1055).** The EBA's C 09.02 has no corporate purchased-receivables row (CRR COREP Annex II p.123: corporate rows 0030, 0042, 0045, 0050 only). In the BoE v4.0.0 extract, boe_b0785, boe_b1034 and boe_b1050-b1055 have no EBA equivalent (rules the Bank wrote); boe_b0282, boe_b0288 and boe_b0285 are mapped to EBA v0425_m (deactivated 2015-09-09, reactivated 2018-04-17), v0435_m (2014-04-16 / 2015-02-27) and v0430_m (2015-09-09 / 2017-04-27), all live. (The EBA list's Explanation sheet: a reactivated rule applies again 'for that taxonomy version onwards'.) Not on the Bank's known-issues logs of 27 August and 16 November 2026.

#### Who is affected

**Retail purchased receivables, row 0105 (boe_b0300-b0302).** Every firm with IRB permission that holds purchased retail receivables under the IRB approach (roll-out class Art. 147B(1)(g)), from the first PRA001 return under PS1/26 (reference dates from 1 January 2027). Every firm that files OF 09.02: Annex II para 85 makes the all-countries sheet due from every institution, though Reporting (CRR) Part Chapter 5 Article 5(5) (PS1/26 Appendix 1 p.481) can be read as gating the whole template on the 10% non-domestic threshold. ERROR severity.

**Corporate purchased receivables, row 0049 (boe_b1053-b1055).** Every firm with IRB permission (FIRB or AIRB) that holds purchased corporate receivables under the IRB approach (roll-out class Art. 147B(1)(c)), from the first PRA001 return under PS1/26 (reference dates from 1 January 2027). Every firm that files OF 09.02 (Annex II para 85 makes the all-countries sheet due from every institution, though Reporting (CRR) Part Article 5(5) can be read as gating the whole template on the 10% non-domestic threshold). ERROR severity.

#### What a firm can do meanwhile

Report the figures the instructions require; do not change correct figures to satisfy the rule. An Error-severity break blocks the submission at the gateway: if the gateway rejects the return on this rule, raise it with the PRA, citing this issue.

boe_b1043, as published in taxonomy 4.1.1 (label: "Change in exposure due to FCCM shall be consistent across templates for the relevant exposure class|"):

```text
isum({t: OF08.06.01.01, r: 0095, c: 0031, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True, id: v0, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting}) i= isum({t: OF08.01.01.02, r: 0080, c: 0100, z: 0002; 0010, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True, id: v1, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting}) i* 0.5
```

boe_b1042, as published in taxonomy 4.1.1 (label: "to ensure that exposure value is equal to exposure after CRM substitution effects pre-conversion factors minus change in exposure due to FCCM|"):

```text
{t: OF08.06.01.01, c: 0040, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v1, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i= isum({t: OF08.06.01.01, c: 0020; 0031, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True, id: v0, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting})
scope({t: OF08.06.01.01, r:0005;0015;0025;0035;0045;0055;0065;0075;0085;0095, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting})
```

#### What the rule requires

boe_b1043: the sum, over every type of specialised lending, of OF 08.06 total row 0095 column 0031 '(-) Change in exposure due to FCCM' (data point boe_met:mi10095, eba_dim:CRM = eba_CP:x6, MCY = eba_MC:x195) must equal half the sum over sheets 0002 and 0010 of OF 08.01.01.02 row 0080 column 0100 'Exposure after CRM substitution effects pre-conversion factors / Of which: off balance sheet items' (eba_met:mi116, MCY = eba_MC:x246, no CRM dimension). That is the same right-hand side as boe_b0818, which ties it - correctly - to OF 08.06 column 0030 (also mi116 / MCY x246). So the rule requires the FCCM change to equal the slotting off-balance-sheet exposure before conversion factors. boe_b1042: on every row of every OF 08.06 sheet, column 0040 'Exposure value' must equal column 0020 'Exposure after CRM substitution effects pre-conversion factors' plus column 0031.

#### What the instructions and rules say

#### Why a correct return fails

boe_b1043. Write F for the summed OF 08.06 r0095 c0031 and X for the slotting off-balance-sheet exposure before conversion factors (OF 08.01.01.02 r0080 c0100, shown on both sheets 0002 and 0010, so the rule's right-hand side is 2X x 0.5 = X). The rule demands F = X. boe_b1044 makes every c0031 cell <= 0, so F <= 0; boe_b0315_2 makes c0100 >= 0, so X >= 0. The three hold together only when F = 0 and X = 0, and boe_b0818 then forces column 0030 to zero as well. So a return passes only if the firm has no off-balance-sheet slotting exposure at all AND reports no FCCM effect at all. Any undrawn slotting commitment (X > 0, F = 0) fails it; any slotting loan with financial collateral under the FCCM (F < 0, X = 0) fails it. The two quantities are unrelated: c0031 is a reduction for collateral, c0100 is an 'of which' of exposure. The right-hand side is boe_b0818's, apparently carried over when the rule was written. Both boe_b1043's summed variable and boe_b1042's filter also list eba_TA:x0 ('Not applicable/All activities') among the type members beside the five named types, so an all-types sheet filed beside the type sheets would be counted twice (see PI-03). The matching OF 08.01 quantity is c0101 + c0102 on row 0080 (boe_b1040: c0104 = c0090 + c0101 + c0102). boe_b1042. Column 0040 is the exposure value under Articles 166A-166D, i.e. after conversion factors (Art. 166C(1)); column 0020 is before conversion factors; column 0031 is, by its instruction, only the FCCM reduction. For an undrawn commitment of nominal N with conversion factor CF and no collateral: c0020 = N, c0031 = 0, c0040 = CF x N. The rule needs CF x N = N, true only at CF = 100%. Table A1 gives 40%, 50%, 20% and 10% for the commitments and trade items a specialised-lending book normally holds. The Bank's own OF 07.00 rule boe_b0471 (c0200 = c0150 - 0.9 c0160 - 0.8 c0170 - 0.6 c0171 - 0.5 c0180) applies conversion factors between the pre-CF and post-CF columns; boe_b1042 has no such term.

#### Worked example

A firm with slotting permission has one undrawn project-finance commitment, slotted Satisfactory: nominal 1,000,000, an 'other commitment' at the 40% conversion factor (Table A1 row 5), no collateral. Annex II asks for: OF 08.06 (type of specialised lending = project finance, eba_TA:x129) rows 0065 and 0095: c0010 1,000,000; c0020 1,000,000; c0030 1,000,000; c0031 0; c0040 400,000; c0050 400,000; c0080 460,000 (115% x 400,000, Art. 153(5) Table A). OF 08.01.01.01 row 0080 on sheets 0002 and 0010: c0020 1,000,000; c0090 1,000,000; c0104 1,000,000; c0110 400,000; c0260 460,000. OF 08.01.01.02 row 0080 on both sheets: c0100 1,000,000; c0120 400,000. boe_b1043 is unsatisfied (0 against 1,000,000) and boe_b1042 on rows 0065 and 0095 (400,000 against 1,000,000), while every sibling tie-out (b0816, b0817, b0818, b0819, b0820, b0822) is satisfied. A fuller version of the same return gives the same verdicts. Second position, run separately: a drawn project-finance loan of 1,000,000, slotted Good with 2.5 years or more remaining, secured by financial collateral C = 100,000 with Cvam = 80,000 under the FCCM (for example cash, with a 0% volatility adjustment, and a maturity factor of 0.8 for a mismatch): OF 08.06 c0020 1,000,000, c0031 -80,000, c0040 920,000; OF 08.01 r0080 c0090 1,000,000, c0101 0, c0102 -80,000, c0103 -20,000, c0104 920,000, c0110 920,000; no off-balance-sheet item. boe_b1042 is satisfied [2,0] and boe_b1043 is unsatisfied [0,1] (-80,000 against 0).

#### Other ways of reporting considered

(1) Leave c0031 blank instead of 0: boe_b1043 still [0,1] (an empty sum is 0), boe_b1042 still [0,2]. (2) Report c0031 = +1,000,000 so boe_b1043 holds: b1043 [1,0] but boe_b1044 [0,2], boe_b0311 [0,2] and boe_b1042 [0,2]; and a positive figure contradicts the '(-)' label and the column's definition. (3) Report c0031 = -600,000, using it to carry the conversion-factor effect so boe_b1042 holds: b1042 [2,0] but boe_b1043 [0,1]; and -600,000 is not an FCCM reduction. (4) For the collateralised loan, report c0031 = 0 so boe_b1043 holds: b1043 [1,0] but boe_b1042 [0,2], and the FCCM reduction of 80,000 goes unreported. (5) Omit the off-balance-sheet 'of which' columns: boe_b0818 / b0820 then fail against OF 08.01.01.02, or both templates misstate the position. (6) Report column 0040 before conversion factors: contradicts Art. 166C(1) and the column 0110 instruction, and breaks RWEA = risk weight x exposure value. No Annex-II-compliant reporting of either position satisfies the rules.

#### Proposed change

boe_b1043: replace the right-hand side with the OF 08.01 slotting FCCM columns - isum({t: OF08.06.01.01, r: 0095, c: 0031, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True}) i= isum({t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0080, c: 0101; 0102, z: 0002; 0010, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True}) i* 0.5. That is the quantity boe_b1040 already defines (c0104 - c0090) and the one boe_b1042, b0817 and b0819 imply for an on-balance-sheet exposure. boe_b1042: replace the equality with an upper bound, same scope - {t: OF08.06.01.01, c: 0040, dv: 0} i<= isum({t: OF08.06.01.01, c: 0020; 0031, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True}) - and, if a lower bound is wanted, add {t: OF08.06.01.01, c: 0040, dv: 0} i>= isum({t: OF08.06.01.01, c: 0020; 0031}) i- {t: OF08.06.01.01, c: 0030, dv: 0}. The two bounds collapse to today's equality whenever column 0030 is zero, and hold for any conversion factor between 0% and 100% (checked by hand on both example positions: 0 <= 400,000 <= 1,000,000 and 920,000 <= 920,000 <= 920,000). An exact identity is not available because column 0031 is not split between on- and off-balance-sheet items. Until corrected, both rules should be deactivated or downgraded from ERROR. One point needs settling first: Annex II does not say whether OF 08.06 column 0031 is measured before or after conversion factors for a collateralised off-balance-sheet item; OF 08.01 columns 0101-0103 are before conversion factors (they feed column 0104, 'pre-conversion factors'), and the replacement boe_b1043 assumes column 0031 is too.

#### EBA precedent

None for the defective rules: boe_b1042, b1043 and b1044 have no EBA equivalent (blank in the Bank's v4.0.0 rule workbook), and column 0031 is a Bank addition - the EBA C 08.06 has no FCCM column ('FCCM' does not occur in the CRR COREP Annex II). The sibling boe_b0818 restates EBA v09789_m, which the EBA deactivated on 2021-06-10, changed and reactivated in release 3.2.0 and deactivated again on 2025-06-10; it remains a Warning. The same holds for v09787_m-v09794_m, which the Bank restates as boe_b0816-b0823, and v09795_m (boe_b0829); the Bank runs them as ERROR.

#### Who is affected

Every firm with slotting permission that files PRA001 OF 08.06 under taxonomy v4.1.1 (instructions effective from 1 January 2027). boe_b1043 (ERROR) fails for any such firm with at least one off-balance-sheet slotting item - undrawn commitments are normal in project, object and commodities finance and in IPRE/HVCRE development facilities - or with any financial collateral recognised under the FCCM on a slotting exposure. boe_b1042 (ERROR) fails for any such firm with an off-balance-sheet slotting item whose conversion factor is below 100%.

#### What a firm can do meanwhile

Report the figures the instructions require; do not change correct figures to satisfy the rule. An Error-severity break blocks the submission at the gateway: if the gateway rejects the return on this rule, raise it with the PRA, citing this issue.

### PI-17 - boe_b0555 / boe_b1036 treat the volatility and maturity adjustment as a subset of Cvam

**Status:** identified by rwa-filer, not yet raised with the Bank of England.

**Severity:** ERROR (boe_b1036); WARNING (boe_b0555).

**Effect:** a return that follows the reporting instructions fails it. **Cause:** contradicts the reporting instructions; states as a rule what holds only as a tendency.

#### What the rule requires

OF 07.00: column 0130 '(-) Financial collateral: adjusted value (Cvam)' <= column 0140 '(-) of which: Volatility and maturity adjustments' on every in-scope row and sheet. OF 08.01 (sheets 0002 and 0010): column 0102 <= column 0103, the same two quantities for slotting exposures. With the signs Annex II and the Bank's own sign rules impose (c0130 = -Cvam, c0140 = Cvam - C) the rule reads -Cvam <= Cvam - C, i.e. C - Cvam <= Cvam: the adjustments may not exceed what is left of the collateral.

#### Why a correct return fails

Signs first. The '(-)' label and paragraph 9 make both columns non-positive; boe_b0699 (c0150 = c0110 + c0120 + c0130) and boe_b1040 (c0104 = c0090 + c0101 + c0102) make the Cvam column a deduction, so c0130 = c0102 = -Cvam; Annex II gives the other column as (Cvam - C), which is <= 0 because haircuts and the maturity factor only reduce collateral. Collateral C = 100: with Cvam = 80, c0130 = -80 and c0140 = -20, and -80 <= -20 is TRUE. With Cvam = 19.6, c0130 = -19.6 and c0140 = -80.4, and -19.6 <= -80.4 is FALSE. In general -Cvam <= Cvam - C exactly when Cvam >= C/2 (Arelle: satisfied at Cvam = 80 and at the boundary 50, unsatisfied at 46.26 and 19.6). The rule reads 'of which' as 'part of', but the adjustment is not a part of Cvam: it is the difference between the collateral's value and Cvam, and the two are complements that sum to -C. Nothing in the definitions bounds one by the other. Realistic ways to fall below C/2: (a) a maturity mismatch - Art. 239(2) scales by (t - 0.25)/(T - 0.25), which is 0.2 for 1.2 years of protection against an exposure of five years or more, and below one half whenever t is under about 2.6 years against five; (b) haircuts alone - a secured loan (20-day liquidation period) against listed non-main-index equity in another currency takes 42.426% + 11.314% = 53.74%, leaving Cvam = 46.26% of C. Over-collateralised exposures reach the same condition: Article 239(2) caps the volatility-adjusted collateral value at the amount of the exposure, so with an exposure of 100 and main-index equity of 400 at a 28.284% haircut, c0130 = -100 (25% of C) and c0140 = -113.14, which is unsatisfied. That route depends on reading C as the whole collateral value; if C is the collateral allocated to the exposure (139.44 of the 400), c0140 = -39.44 and the rule holds.

#### Worked example

Two positions in one return, each with cash collateral of C = 100,000 (a 0% volatility adjustment) whose residual maturity of 1.2 years falls short of a loan of five years or more, so Art. 239(2) scales it by (1.2 - 0.25) / (5 - 0.25) = 0.2: Cvam = 20,000, and the volatility and maturity adjustment is Cvam - C = -80,000. (1) A standardised corporate loan of 1,000,000 under the FCCM: OF 07.00 sheet 0008 row 0010: c0010 1,000,000; c0040 1,000,000; c0110 1,000,000; c0120 0; c0130 -20,000; c0140 -80,000; c0150 980,000; c0200 980,000; c0220 980,000. (2) A slotting project-finance loan of 1,000,000 (Good, 2.5 years or more, 90%) under the FCCM: OF 08.01 sheet 0010 row 0080: c0020 1,000,000; c0090 1,000,000; c0101 0; c0102 -20,000; c0103 -80,000; c0104 980,000; c0110 980,000; c0260 882,000. boe_b0555 compares -20,000 with -80,000, and boe_b1036 likewise; the arithmetic and sign rules on the same cells hold. With collateral of the same maturity as the loan (Cvam = 100,000, adjustment 0) both rules hold.

Arelle's result on it:

| boe_b0555 | 0 | 1 | fails |
| boe_b0699 | 1 | 0 | holds |
| boe_b0733 | 2 | 0 | holds |
| boe_b1036 | 0 | 1 | fails |
| boe_b1037 | 1 | 0 | holds |
| boe_b1038 | 1 | 0 | holds |
| boe_b1040 | 1 | 0 | holds |
