#### Other ways of reporting considered

(1) Report the adjustment as a positive number (+80,000): boe_b0555 becomes [1,0] but boe_b0733 fails [1,1]; on OF 08.01 boe_b1036 becomes [1,0] but boe_b1038, an ERROR, fails [0,1]; and paragraph 9 expects no positive figure under a '(-)' label. (2) Leave the 'of which' column blank: both rules pass because the missing cell defaults to 0 (boe_b0555 [1,0]; boe_b1036 [1,0]) - but that omits a figure Annex II asks for whenever a haircut or maturity mismatch applies; the rule rewards not reporting it. (3) Report Cvam before the cap, or scale the adjustment down with the cap: no instruction supports either, and an uncapped c0130 breaks boe_b0699 on an over-collateralised exposure. (4) Positive c0130: breaks boe_b0699 / b1040 and the sign rules. No compliant reporting of a position with Cvam below C/2 satisfies the rules.

#### Proposed change

Deactivate boe_b0555 and boe_b1036, as the EBA did with v0008_h on 9 September 2015. No inequality between the two columns follows from their Annex II definitions: c0130 + c0140 = -C says only that both are non-positive, which boe_b0733 (OF 07.00 c0130, c0140 <= 0) and boe_b1037 / boe_b1038 / boe_b0306 (OF 08.01 c0102, c0103 <= 0) already check, and the arithmetic is checked by boe_b0699 and boe_b1040. If the Bank keeps boe_b1036 while it reviews, lower it from ERROR to WARNING so that it matches boe_b0555 and cannot reject a correct return.

#### EBA precedent

boe_b0555 is the EBA's v0008_h (the Bank's v4.0.0 rule workbook labels it DESCRIPTION 'v0008_h'; the v4.1.1 workbook keeps only the short label). In the EBA validation rules workbook v0008_h - C 07.00.a rows 0010-0080, {c0130} <= +{c0140}, type Hierarchy, severity Warning (non-blocking) - carries 'Deactivated on' 2015-09-09 and no reactivation date on every sheet from v3.0 to 3.5. The labels and the defining formulas of columns 0130 and 0140 are the same in the EBA's Annex II (pages 88-89) and PS1/26 Annex II (page 85) - only the cross-references to the CRR and the PRA Rulebook differ - so the Bank has switched back on, against unchanged definitions, a check the EBA has kept off for eleven years. The EBA tried both directions: sheets v2.0-v2.2 carry v0008_h as '{c130} >= +{c140}', deactivated on 2014-04-16; from v2.3 it was flipped to '{c130} <= +{c140}' and deactivated on 2015-09-09. The workbook does not record why it was deactivated. boe_b1036 has no EBA equivalent: it applies the same idea to the Bank's new slotting columns, at ERROR.

#### Who is affected

boe_b0555 (WARNING, non-blocking): every firm using the Financial Collateral Comprehensive Method on standardised exposures, on any in-scope row or sheet of OF 07.00 where the summed adjustments exceed the summed Cvam - books with maturity-mismatched collateral (protection under about 2.6 years against exposures of five years or more), with equity collateral in another currency, or with collateral well above the exposure. boe_b1036 (ERROR): firms with slotting permission that recognise financial collateral under the FCCM on slotting exposures, same conditions, on sheets 0002 and 0010. From the first PRA001 return under taxonomy v4.1.1 (instructions effective 1 January 2027).

#### What a firm can do meanwhile

Report the figures the instructions require; do not change correct figures to satisfy the rule. An Error-severity break blocks the submission at the gateway: if the gateway rejects the return on this rule, raise it with the PRA, citing this issue.

<a id="pi-18"></a>

### PI-18 - boe_b1075 builds the all-approaches CVA total from the standardised-only BA-CVA cell

**Status:** identified by rwa-filer, not yet raised with the Bank of England.

**Severity:** WARNING (boe_b1075).

**Effect:** a return that follows the reporting instructions fails it. **Cause:** contradicts the reporting instructions.

#### The rules

| Rule | Module | Severity | Part in the issue | Where the issue applies | At the gateway |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| boe_b1075 | PRA001 | WARNING | the rule at issue | every evaluation (a break there may also be the return's own) | run as published |
| boe_b1076 | PRA001 | WARNING | related | - | run as published |
| boe_b1092 | PRA001 | WARNING | related | - | run as published |
| boe_b0706 | PRA001 | WARNING | related | - | run as published |
| boe_b0716 | PRA001 | ERROR | related | - | run as published |

boe_b1075, as published in taxonomy 4.1.1 (label: "Total CVA Risk Exposure Amount under all approaches is the sum of CVA risk exposure amounts calculated using each CVA risk approach|"):

```text
{t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0640, c: 0010, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v0, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i= {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0641, c: 0010, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v1, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i+ {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0642, c: 0020, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v2, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i+ {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0643, c: 0010, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v3, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting}
```

#### What the rule requires

b1075 (label: "Total CVA Risk Exposure Amount under all approaches is the sum of CVA risk exposure amounts calculated using each CVA risk approach") requires r0640 c0010 = r0641 c0010 + r0642 c0020 + r0643 c0010. The XBRL formula says the same as the workbook (vr-boe_b1075.xml: $v2 is filtered to boe_dim:AEV = boe_eba_AP:x10031, i.e. the column 0020 cell of row 0642). b1076 requires r0640 c0020 = the same three cells, so whenever both evaluate they force r0640 c0010 = r0640 c0020. In the taxonomy, r0640 c0010 and c0020 are reportable; r0642 c0010 and c0020 both reportable; r0641 and r0643 reportable in c0010 only (c0020 greyed). So b1075's BA operand is in the wrong column. b1076 reads column 0010 for the SA and AA rows because they have no standardised-only cell; whether that is right in every case is the related question below.

**A related question: a return without column 0020 (boe_b1076).** b1076 compares the standardised-only CVA total (r0640 c0020, default 0) with two operands that exist only in column 0010 (r0641 SA-CVA and r0643 AA-CVA). A firm that reports SA-CVA or AA-CVA in column 0010 and nothing in column 0020 is therefore told 0 = its CVA figure.

#### What the instructions and rules say

> Where firms have IMM permission and choose to use this methodology for calculating the exposure at default (EAD) for the purposes of BA-CVA, column 0010 must be completed using the IMM and column 0020 must be computed using the Standardised Approach to Counterparty Credit Risk (SA-CCR) only.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 02.00 row 0642 (1.6.2 Basic Approach (BA)), PDF page 38

> 0010 All approaches See instructions concerning specific positions regarding rows.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 02.00 columns, PDF page 39

> Captures risk exposure amounts calculated under standardised approaches per exposure class, where relevant.  Rows containing totals by risk type should reflect entire current portfolios using standardised approaches only.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 02.00 column 0020, PDF page 39

> 1.6 TOTAL RISK EXPOSURE AMOUNT FOR CREDIT VALUATION ADJUSTMENT Point (d) of Article 92(3) of the Required Level of Own Funds part See CVA template
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 02.00 row 0640, PDF page 37

> The standardised total risk exposure amount shall be calculated as the sum of points (a) to (f) of paragraph 3: (a) after having taken into account paragraph 4; and (b) calculated without using any of the following approaches or as if permission to use the following approaches has not been granted:
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Appendix 1: the PRA Rulebook instruments (Basel 3.1), Required Level of Own Funds (CRR) Part, Article 92(3A), PDF page 15

> (iv) the Internal Model Method approach set out in Section 6 of Chapter 6 of Title II of Part Three of CRR;
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Appendix 1: the PRA Rulebook instruments (Basel 3.1), Article 92(3A)(b)(iv), PDF page 15

> EADNS is the exposure at default of the netting set, calculated in the same manner in which the firm calculates exposure at default for determining own funds requirements for counterparty credit risk, in accordance with either Sections 3 to 5 of Counterparty Credit Risk (CRR) Part or Section 6 of Chapter 6 of Title II of Part Three of CRR;
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Appendix 1: the PRA Rulebook instruments (Basel 3.1), Credit Valuation Adjustment Risk Part, rule 4.3, PDF page 400

> The columns Standardised approaches only (Output floor) (0020) and Standardised approaches including multiplier (Output Floor) (0030) are a requirement for Internal Multiplier (IM) firms in scope of the Basel 3.1 standards:
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 02.00 general remarks, Scope, PDF page 28

> for the purposes of complying with the obligations of this Part on an individual basis, the total risk exposure amount of a ring-fenced body that is a member of a sub-consolidation group and an institution which is not a stand-alone institution in the UK shall be the un-floored total risk exposure amount calculated in accordance with paragraph 3;
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Appendix 1: the PRA Rulebook instruments (Basel 3.1), Required Level of Own Funds (CRR) Part, Article 92(2A)(c), PDF page 14

> 1.6.3. Alternative Approach (AA) Own funds requirements for credit valuation adjustment risk in accordance with Chapter 6 of the Credit Valuation Adjustment Risk Part of the PRA Rulebook.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 02.00 row 0643, PDF page 38

#### Why a correct return fails

An IMM firm on BA-CVA has two different BA-CVA figures by construction: rule 4.3 makes it use IMM EAD for its real requirement (r0642 c0010, part of U-TREA), and Art. 92(3A)(b)(iv) makes it recompute without the IMM for S-TREA (r0642 c0020). Annex II p.38 tells it to report both. The all-approaches total is r0640 c0010 = r0641 c0010 + r0642 c0010 + r0643 c0010. b1075 instead adds r0642 c0020, so it holds only when r0642 c0010 = r0642 c0020. With BA-CVA 80 (IMM EAD) and 100 (SA-CCR EAD): b1075 reads 80 = 0 + 100 + 0 and is unsatisfied; b1076 reads 100 = 0 + 100 + 0 and is satisfied. The Bank's own ERROR rule boe_b0793 treats r0640 c0020 as distinct from c0010 in the same way: with the output-floor multiplier r0035 c0030 = 0.6, r0010 c0030 = 60 = 0.6 x 100 is satisfied and 48 = 0.6 x 80 is not.

**A related question: a return without column 0020 (boe_b1076).** Annex II makes column 0020 a requirement only for IM firms in scope of the floor. A firm outside that scope (a non-IM firm, or a solo return of a UK subsidiary under Art. 92(2A)(c)) that leaves column 0020 empty and has AA-CVA 50: r0643 c0010 = 50, r0640 c0010 = 50. b1076 evaluates with r0640 c0020 defaulted to 0: 0 = 0 + 0 + 50, unsatisfied. Same for SA-CVA (r0641). For BA-CVA only, b1076 does not evaluate (all four of its cells are absent), but b1075 fails, because r0642 c0020 defaults to 0 (r0640 c0010 = 100, r0642 c0010 = 100: 100 = 0 + 0 + 0; Arelle [0,1]). An IMM firm on the Alternative Approach meets a different gap: CVA Risk Part 6.2(2) makes its AA-CVA 100% of its counterparty credit risk requirement under the IMM, and Art. 92(3A)(b)(iv) excludes the IMM from the standardised total, but r0643 has no column 0020 cell and Annex II's IMM sentence (p.38) covers BA-CVA only; reporting r0640 c0020 = 100 (SA-CCR) against r0643 c0010 = 80 (IMM) fails b1076 (Arelle [0,1]). This is put as a question because a compliant alternative exists for the first case: the firm can complete column 0020 voluntarily (r0640 c0020 = 50), which satisfies the rule, and the Bank's ERROR rule boe_b0716 already forces r0040 c0020 on every firm with SA credit risk, so in practice column 0020 is not optional (Arelle: an Alternative-Approach firm with SA credit risk and no column 0020 fails boe_b0716 [0,1] as well as b1076). Annex II's scope sentence also uses 'IM firms' (p.28; p.39 uses it for OF 02.01) without defining the term.

#### Worked example

IMM firm in scope of the output floor, all CVA on BA-CVA, no SA-CVA or AA-CVA. BA-CVA risk exposure amount 80,000 using IMM exposure values, 100,000 recomputed with SA-CCR exposure values. Annex II asks for r0642 c0010 = 80,000, r0642 c0020 = 100,000, r0640 c0010 = 80,000, r0640 c0020 = 100,000 (r0010 c0010 = 80,000 is included only so that boe_b1092 can evaluate).

Arelle's result on it:

| Rule | Satisfied | Unsatisfied | What the example shows |
|---|---|---|---|
| boe_b0706 | 2 | 0 | - |
| boe_b1075 | 0 | 1 | fails |
| boe_b1076 | 1 | 0 | - |
| boe_b1092 | 1 | 0 | - |

<details>
<summary>The example's 5 cells</summary>

| Table | Sheet | Key | Row | Column | Value |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| OF02.00.01.01 |  |  | 0642 | 0010 | 80,000 |
| OF02.00.01.01 |  |  | 0642 | 0020 | 100,000 |
| OF02.00.01.01 |  |  | 0640 | 0010 | 80,000 |
| OF02.00.01.01 |  |  | 0640 | 0020 | 100,000 |
| OF02.00.01.01 |  |  | 0010 | 0010 | 80,000 |

</details>

#### Other ways of reporting considered

(a) Report r0640 c0010 = 100, the standardised figure: Arelle passes all four rules, but r0640 c0010 and r0010 c0010 then overstate the firm's un-floored CVA requirement by 20, against column 0010 'All approaches' and Art. 92(3)(d). Not compliant. (b) Report the SA-CCR figure in both columns of r0642: contradicts p.38 'column 0010 must be completed using the IMM'. (c) Leave r0642 c0020 empty: b1075 then reads 80 = 0 and b1076 100 = 0; both fail, and p.38 requires the cell. (d) No filing indicator, precondition or greyed cell removes the rule: r0642 c0010 is a reportable cell (datapoint with eba_dim:APR = boe_eba_AP:x10005 and no boe_dim:AEV), and the rule's only precondition is the OF 02.00 filing indicator. No compliant alternative satisfies b1075.

**A related question: a return without column 0020 (boe_b1076).** Completing column 0020 voluntarily (S-TREA figures equal to the column 0010 figures for a firm with no models) satisfies b1076 and is not forbidden by Annex II, which only says the column is 'a requirement for' IM firms in scope. That alternative exists, so this is a scope-guard gap, not a contradiction a compliant return cannot escape.

#### Proposed change

In boe_b1075 change the third operand from column 0020 to column 0010: {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0640, c: 0010, dv: 0} i= {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0641, c: 0010, dv: 0} i+ {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0642, c: 0010, dv: 0} i+ {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0643, c: 0010, dv: 0}. In the formula (vr-boe_b1075.xml) that is one change: filter boe_boe_b1075.v2.f0, boe_dim:AEV member boe_eba_AP:x10031 -> eba_AP:x0. Verified in Arelle on a copy of the package with that one change.

**A related question: a return without column 0020 (boe_b1076).** Either state in Annex II that column 0020 is completed by every firm (which is what boe_b0716 already enforces), or guard the rule on the total being reported, in the form the Bank already uses in boe_b0793: if not(isNull({t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0640, c: 0020, dv: emptySequence()})) then {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0640, c: 0020, dv: emptySequence()} i= {r: 0641, c: 0010, dv: 0} i+ {r: 0642, c: 0020, dv: 0} i+ {r: 0643, c: 0010, dv: 0} else true(). Verified in Arelle on a copy of the package with that change. For an IMM firm on the Alternative Approach, add an r0643 column 0020 cell, or an Annex II instruction on what r0640 c0020 holds for it.

#### EBA precedent

EBA v0215_m (C 02.00, ERROR, live) is the same identity with every operand in one column: "{r0640, c0010} = {r0650, c0010} + {r0660, c0010} + {r0670, c0010}". The Bank's own known-issues log has the same class of defect fixed before: issue 2 (LVR001, boe_b0021) "The validation rule uses C0020 Daily/ Monthly average for R0520 CET1 capital reported when it should use C0010 Accounting balance sheet value." (amended in hotfix 3.5.1). boe_b1075/b1076 had no EBA equivalent recorded in the v4.0.0 workbook, which already carries boe_b1075 with r0642 c0020 - the defect is not new in v4.1.1 - and neither rule is in the August or November 2026 known-issues logs.

**A related question: a return without column 0020 (boe_b1076).** Known-issues log issue 6 (LVR001) is the same pattern, accepted and fixed by the Bank: "Non- LREQ firms are not expected to report every data item within the LV47.00.00.01 template. These firms will report some data points in scope of validation rules boe_b0017, boe_b0019 and boe_b0021 but not others causing the validations to fail."

#### Who is affected

Every firm that uses IMM exposure values in BA-CVA and is in scope of the output floor, on every PRA001 return from the first Basel 3.1 reference date (1 January 2027 onwards), whenever the IMM-based and SA-CCR-based BA-CVA figures differ. WARNING severity, so the return is accepted with a warning. (A BA-CVA firm that leaves column 0020 empty fails it too: see the related question.)

**A related question: a return without column 0020 (boe_b1076).** Firms that hold SA-CVA or AA-CVA and leave OF 02.00 column 0020 empty - non-IM firms and solo returns outside the floor's scope - and IMM firms on the Alternative Approach, from 1 January 2027. WARNING only.

#### What a firm can do meanwhile

Report the figures the instructions require; do not change correct figures to satisfy the rule. A Warning-severity break does not stop the submission: explain it when you submit, citing this issue.

<a id="pi-19"></a>

### PI-19 - boe_b0718: the branch its label describes never runs (r5860 has no default)

**Status:** identified by rwa-filer, not yet raised with the Bank of England.

**Severity:** ERROR (boe_b0718).

**Effect:** as published it never runs, so it checks nothing. **Cause:** the published text and the rule as run differ.

#### The rules

| Rule | Module | Severity | Part in the issue | Where the issue applies | At the gateway |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| boe_b0718 | PRA001 | ERROR | the rule at issue | every evaluation | run as published |
| boe_b0793 | PRA001 | ERROR | related | - | run as published |
| boe_b0706 | PRA001 | WARNING | holds on the example (control) | - | run as published |
| boe_b1091 | PRA001 | WARNING | related | - | run as published |

boe_b0718, as published in taxonomy 4.1.1 (label: "If the ASA requirement for all desks (applicable only to IMA firms) is populated, the firm is an IMA firm. The Market Risk SA requirement for output floor purposes would then be equal to that amount. If the ASA requirement for all desks (applicable only to IMA firms) is blank, the firm must be either an SSA firm or an ASA firm. The SA requirement for output floor purposes would be equal to the sum of the firm's SSA requirement and the ASA requirement for ASA desks only, with one of the two expected to be blank depending on the firm's approach|"):

```text
If Not(IsNull({t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 5860, c: 0020, seq: False, id: v1, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting})) then {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0520, c: 0020, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v0, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i= {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 5860, c: 0020, seq: False, id: v1, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} else ({t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0520, c: 0020, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v0, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i= {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0530, c: 0010, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v2, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i+ {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0571, c: 0010, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v3, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting})
```

#### What the rule requires

What a firm reading the workbook believes: an ERROR rule that checks the standardised market-risk figure for the output floor in both cases. Label, verbatim: "If the ASA requirement for all desks (applicable only to IMA firms) is populated, the firm is an IMA firm. The Market Risk SA requirement for output floor purposes would then be equal to that amount. If the ASA requirement for all desks (applicable only to IMA firms) is blank, the firm must be either an SSA firm or an ASA firm. The SA requirement for output floor purposes would be equal to the sum of the firm's SSA requirement and the ASA requirement for ASA desks only, with one of the two expected to be blank depending on the firm's approach". What the gateway does: the formula (vr-boe_b0718.xml) declares <variable:factVariable xlink:label="boe_boe_b0718.v1" bindAsSequence="false" id="boe_boe_b0718.v1" /> with NO fallbackValue (v0, v2, v3 have fallbackValue="0"), and test="if (not(empty($v1))) then (iaf:numeric-equal($v0,$v1)) else ((iaf:numeric-equal($v0,iaf:numeric-add($v2,$v3))))". A fact variable with no fallback and no matching fact produces no evaluation, so when r5860 c0020 is absent the assertion is not evaluated at all. Only the then-branch can ever run. The formula is a faithful serialisation of the workbook's own expression, which already lacks the default on v1; it is the label that describes the else-branch. No other PRA001 rule checks r0520 c0020 against r0530 + r0571 (every rule touching rows 0520/0530/0571/5860 was listed: b0706, b0718, b0720, b0793, b1091, b1092).

#### What the instructions and rules say

> dv prefix is a prefix to define a default value for a variable, that will be used, if no data will be found, in the example, the default value is set to defaultValue (optional). If the default value will not be specified, an evaluation may return no results - in most cases, all facts must have value (from the report itself or the default value); the only function, that is able to handle null values for facts is isNull.
>
> - Bank of England validation rules workbook, Banking Reporting v4.1.1, sheet 'Note', row 21 (definition of dv)

> IsNull | Returns TRUE if fact specified by a variable node is null, otherwise FALSE.
>
> - Bank of England validation rules workbook, Banking Reporting v4.1.1, sheet 'Note', row 30

> 1.3.4 Risk exposure amount for Position, foreign exchange and commodities risks under advanced standardised approaches (ASA) - for all desks [This is only applicable for IMA firms] The ASA own funds requirements for all positions, calculated for purpose of output floor.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 02.00 row 5860, PDF pages 35-36

> The ASA own funds requirements for relevant desks (i.e., all desks for ASA firms). This is not applicable to SSA firms.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 02.00 row 0571, PDF page 34

> The fallback value for $v1 is incorrectly set as zero and it should be emptysequence. The validation will not function as expected when  $v1 isn't reported.
>
> - Bank of England Banking taxonomy known-issues log (27 August 2026), issue 12, boe_v0775_m_1

#### Why the rule never runs

A correct return does not fail; the defect runs the other way. For every firm that is not an IMA firm (r5860 blank, as Annex II requires), the rule is silent whether or not r0520 c0020 equals r0530 c0010 + r0571 c0010: Arelle gives [0,0] on a return where they agree (300,000 = 0 + 300,000) and [0,0] on one where they do not (500,000 against 0 + 300,000). The workbook's own Note says a missing default 'may return no results' but also that IsNull is the function that handles null facts, so a reader expects the else-branch to run. Two consequences were measured: (1) of the presence test: a non-IMA firm that writes an explicit 0 in r5860 c0020 - a row Annex II marks as applicable only to IMA firms - instead of leaving it blank is taken down the then-branch and fails an ERROR rule (r0520 c0020 = 300,000 against r5860 = 0; Arelle [0,1]); (2) the obvious repair on its own (dv: emptySequence() on v1) would make the else-branch fail any firm that reports market risk in column 0010 and does not complete column 0020 (r0520 c0020 defaults to 0 against r0571 = 300,000; Arelle [0,1] on a copy of the package with that change), so the repair needs a guard.

#### Worked example

ASA firm with no internal model for market risk: ASA requirement 300,000 in r0571 c0010 and r0520 c0010; r5860 blank as Annex II requires; r0520 c0020 misreported as 500,000. The label says this is an error; the gateway says nothing.

Arelle's result on it:

| Rule | Satisfied | Unsatisfied | What the example shows |
|---|---|---|---|
| boe_b0706 | 1 | 0 | holds |
| boe_b0718 | 0 | 0 | not evaluated |

<details>
<summary>The example's 3 cells</summary>

| Table | Sheet | Key | Row | Column | Value |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| OF02.00.01.01 |  |  | 0520 | 0010 | 300,000 |
| OF02.00.01.01 |  |  | 0520 | 0020 | 500,000 |
| OF02.00.01.01 |  |  | 0571 | 0010 | 300,000 |

</details>

#### Other ways of reporting considered

Tried to find a path that makes the else-branch run: an IMA firm populates r5860 and takes the then-branch; a non-IMA firm that leaves it blank gets no evaluation; a non-IMA firm that writes 0 gets the then-branch (and an ERROR). The pivot variable (always execute = yes) does not help, because a fact variable without a fallback still blocks the evaluation. Nil facts are not admitted (no nils attribute). There is no input that reaches the else-branch.

#### Proposed change

Give both nullable cells an empty default and skip a return that reports neither: if isNull({t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0520, c: 0020, dv: emptySequence(), id: v0}) and isNull({t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 5860, c: 0020, dv: emptySequence(), id: v1}) then true() else (if not(isNull({t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 5860, c: 0020, dv: emptySequence(), id: v1})) then {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0520, c: 0020, dv: 0, id: v0} i= {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 5860, c: 0020, id: v1} else {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0520, c: 0020, dv: 0, id: v0} i= {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0530, c: 0010, dv: 0, id: v2} i+ {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0571, c: 0010, dv: 0, id: v3}). In formula terms: fallbackValue="()" on v0 and v1 and test "if (empty($v0) and empty($v1)) then true() else (if (not(empty($v1))) then (iaf:numeric-equal((if (empty($v0)) then 0 else $v0),$v1)) else (iaf:numeric-equal($v0,iaf:numeric-add($v2,$v3))))"; this exact text was run in Arelle on a copy of the package. If the Bank does not want the else-branch, the label should be cut back to the IMA case. Optionally test r5860 for a non-zero value instead of presence, so a zero-filled cell is not read as 'IMA firm'.

#### EBA precedent

No EBA equivalent (v4.0.0 extract: none). In v4.0.0 the rule was a plain sum, "{t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0520, c: 0020} = {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0530, c: 0010} + {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0571, c: 0010} + {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 5860, c: 0020}"; the if/else was introduced in v4.1.1 and lost the default. The Bank has logged an analogous error before, the converse one (a fallback of zero where an empty sequence was needed): known issue 12, boe_v0775_m_1, in the PRA_IFRS entry point (PRA104-107). boe_b0718 is not in the August or November 2026 known-issues logs or on the deny list.

#### Who is affected

Every PRA001 filer that is not an IMA firm: the check its label promises is never applied. In addition, any such firm (or its software) that zero-fills r5860 c0020 gets an ERROR.

#### What a firm can do meanwhile

The rule checks nothing on a return like this: check what it was meant to check yourself.

#### What the rule requires

What a firm reading the workbook believes: seven ERROR checks on OF 91.01 (ASA general interest rate risk) - positive sensitivities >= 0, negative <= 0, net = positive + negative, scenario total = delta + vega + curvature for the low / medium / high scenarios, and total risk exposure = 12.5 x own funds requirement - applying to the template as reported, i.e. on both of its sheets. What the gateway does: each formula carries a variable-set filter <df:dimension><df:qname>eba_dim:PRP</df:qname></df:dimension><df:member><df:qname>eba_PL:x0</df:qname></df:member> (e.g. filter boe_boe_b0527.f68). eba_PL:x0 is PRP's default member (EBA dim-def.xml: dimension-default arc from eba_PRP to pl/mem.xsd#eba_x0). Every one of OF 91.01's 1,144 cells is on sheet 0001 (PRP = boe_eba_PL:x753, 'Dedicated general interest rate internal hedge portfolio', 572 cells) or sheet 0002 (PRP = eba_PL:x51, 'Other trading book positions', 572 cells). No fact can match, so the seven rules never produce an evaluation. The workbook names no sheet at all. Of the 729 enforced PRA001 rules that reference a fixed-sheet table, these seven are the only ones whose reference names no z code (neither in the reference nor in the scope); the other 722 list the sheets explicitly, as the two neighbouring OF 91.01 rules boe_b0931 (z: 0001) and boe_b0931_1 (z: 0002) do. This reads as the formula generator treating 'no z' as 'no sheet' (an inference from the filters; the Bank does not document it).

#### What the instructions and rules say

> Where applicable, this template shall be reported separately for the following portfolios: • Dedicated general interest rate internal hedge portfolio, as referred to in paragraph 9 of Trading Book (CRR) Part Article 106; • Other trading book positions
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, 5.8.2 OF 91.01, General Remarks, PDF page 255

> This is net unweighted delta sensitivities to risk factors, i.e. the total sensitivities of positive sensitivities and negative sensitivities from columns 0010-0020
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 91.01 column 0030, PDF page 256

> z prefix is used to define the sheet or group of sheets from which data should be extracted, in the example, the sheet will be identified by a code sheet1,
>
> - Bank of England validation rules workbook, Banking Reporting v4.1.1, sheet 'Note', row 20

> <df:dimension> <df:qname>eba_dim:PRP</df:qname> </df:dimension> <df:member> <df:qname>eba_PL:x0</df:qname> </df:member>
>
> - Bank of England Banking Taxonomy v4.1.1 (taxonomy package and data point model), fws/banking/banking_reporting/2026-08-17/val/vr-boe_b0527.xml (identical filter in the other six files)

#### Why the rule never runs

No correct return fails. The rules are published as ERROR, 'Include in XBRL: yes', 'Deactivated: no', and are never evaluated on any return, right or wrong. A return that breaks all seven on sheet 0002 (and boe_b0281 and boe_b0541 on sheet 0001 as well) is accepted: Arelle reports [0,0] for each of the seven while the two rules that name their sheet evaluate on the same facts (boe_b0931 [0,1], boe_b0931_1 [1,0]).

#### Worked example

OF 91.01 row 0010 with every one of the seven identities deliberately broken on sheet 0002 (positive sensitivity -5, negative +7, net 999, each scenario total 10 against components 1 + 1 + 1, total risk exposure 1 against own funds requirement 10), and on sheet 0001 a negative 'positive' sensitivity and r0010 c0160 = 10 against a largest scenario total of 4 (so that boe_b0931, which names its sheet, is seen to fail).

| boe_b0541 | 0 | 0 | not evaluated |
| boe_b0931 | 0 | 1 | - |
| boe_b0931_1 | 1 | 0 | holds |

#### Other ways of reporting considered

Looked for any way a fact could bind: OF 91.01 has no cell without a sheet (the taxonomy has 572 cells on each of sheets 0001 and 0002 and none without a sheet), and PRP = eba_PL:x0 is not a member any OF 91.01 data point carries, so no reporting choice changes the outcome. The other OF 91 tables (91.02-91.10) are single-sheet and their 57 rules leave PRP open, so the defect is confined to these seven.

#### Proposed change

Name the sheets, as every other rule on a sheeted table does. Either add z: 0001; 0002 to each reference or scope (e.g. boe_b0527 scope({t: OF91.01.01.01, r:0010;...;0380, z:0001;0002, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting}); boe_b0281 {t: OF91.01.01.01, r: 0010; ...; 0380, c: 0010, z: 0001; 0002} >= 0; boe_b0541 {t: OF91.01.01.01, r: 0010, c: 0170, z: 0001; 0002, dv: 0} i= {t: OF91.01.01.01, r: 0010, c: 0160, z: 0001; 0002, dv: 0} i* 12.5), or split each rule per sheet as was done for boe_b0931 / boe_b0931_1. In the formulas that means dropping the eba_dim:PRP = eba_PL:x0 set-filter so the sheet is matched fact by fact (shown to work in Arelle on a copy of the package with that change). Because these checks have never run, they should be tested on real data before being switched on as ERROR.

#### EBA precedent

None found; these are Bank-authored (boe_b) rules for the UK ASA templates. Not in the August or November 2026 known-issues logs.

#### Who is affected

Every ASA market-risk filer of OF 91.01, every period: seven published ERROR checks give no protection, and vendor software built from the workbook will apply checks the gateway does not.

#### What a firm can do meanwhile

The rule checks nothing on a return like this: check what it was meant to check yourself.

#### What the rule requires

**Expressions cut short in the workbook.** Each rule is an allowed-values list for a country cell (C 14.00 c0190 'Country of origin of the ultimate underlying of the transaction'; C 06.02 c0050 'Jurisdiction of incorporation'). The workbook gives three different versions of the list for the same rule: the 'Expression' cell is exactly 32,700 characters long and stops mid-reference ('... seq: False, id: v'; 287 opening braces against 286 closing; 286 complete alternatives, the last being eba_GA:_4O); the 'Simplified Expression' cell is complete and has 336 alternatives; the 'Label' cell names 359 entries (it includes [KOSOVO]). The cut is at 32,700 characters, below the 32,767-character limit of a spreadsheet cell: both cut cells end at exactly that length, which suggests a limit in the Bank's export (an observation; the Bank documents no such limit). What the gateway does: there is no formula for either rule (no vr-v4011_a*.xml or vr-v4023_a*.xml anywhere in the package; 'Include in XBRL' = no). But both cells are enumerated items in the taxonomy: eba_met:ei86 and eba_met:ei152 are declared type="enum:enumerationItemType" with enum:linkrole=".../dict/dom/GA/GA4_1", a hierarchy of 359 members. An XBRL processor validates the value against that list. So the rule is not 'never run' in effect: its intent is enforced by the data type, against 359 members, 23 of which are missing from the Simplified Expression (eba_GA:XK Kosovo, eba_GA:_6P to _6U, _6Z, _7Y, _7Z, _8A, _9B and eleven eba_GA:IMF.CL_AREA.* codes) and 73 of which are missing from the truncated Expression.

**Rules the package does not carry, and boe_b0756 as written.** Counts, measured on the workbook and the package: 1,486 rules; 1,441 'Include in XBRL: yes' and exactly 1,441 assertion files in fws/banking/banking_reporting/2026-08-17/val (same ids, no extras, none missing); 45 'no', none with a formula anywhere in the package. Of the 45, 7 are also deactivated (all WARNING: v7363_m, v7364_m, v7667_a, v7380_m, v7381_m, v7386_m, v7387_m) and 38 are active (17 ERROR, 21 WARNING). The 38 active rules are two different things. (A) 15 checks that nothing in the package performs: ERROR boe_b0755, boe_b0756, boe_b0757, boe_b0758 (OF 08.01 r0070 against exposure-weighted sums over OF 08.02), boe_b0903 (reference-date format); WARNING v8731_m (C 09.04), v7371_m (C 14.00/C 14.01), v7338_m (C 14.01), v09805_m (C 34.01), v10494_s (C 34.02), v10288_h and v10328_s (C 34.03), v10487_s (C 34.04), v10491_s (C 34.05), v10481_s (C 34.09). (B) 23 allowed-value lists on enumerated cells, which the taxonomy enforces through the data type (Arelle: enumie:InvalidFactValue): ERROR v4010_a, v4011_a, v4014_a, v4015_a, v4018_a, v4020_a, v4021_a, v4022_a, v4023_a, v6305_a, v6577_a, v7299_a; WARNING v6520_a, v7668_a, v7675_a, v7676_a, v7677_a, v7678_a, v7679_a, v10270_a, v10475_a, v10476_a, v10564_a. For 16 of them the workbook list equals the taxonomy's hierarchy member for member (v4010_a, v4014_a, v4015_a, v4018_a, v4020_a, v4022_a, v6305_a, v6577_a, v7299_a, v7675_a, v7677_a, v7678_a, v7679_a, v10270_a, v10475_a, v10476_a); v7676_a matches as far as checked; 6 are narrower than what the taxonomy accepts (v4011_a and v4023_a: 336 of 359; v4021_a: 4 of 5, eba_PL:x71; v6520_a: 8 of 14; v7668_a: 13 of 18; v10564_a: 2 of 3, eba_ZZ:x427). 16 of them are on the credit-risk tables: boe_b0755-b0758, v8731_m, v09805_m, v10475_a, v10494_s, v10288_h, v10328_s, v10476_a, v10487_s, v10491_s, v10270_a, v10564_a, v10481_s. Of those, 12 are checked by nothing (4 ERROR, 8 WARNING) and 4 are allowed-value lists (v10475_a, v10476_a, v10270_a equal to the taxonomy; v10564_a narrower). What a firm reading the workbook believes: the row says ERROR, Deactivated = no, and the Note sheet does not define the 'Include in XBRL' column, so the rule looks binding. What the gateway does, as far as the published package shows: no assertion exists, so an XBRL processor running the Bank's package never evaluates them.

#### What the instructions and rules say

> = [eba_GA:_4O] or {t: C06.02.01.01, c: 0050, dv: [Default], seq: False, id: v
>
> - Bank of England validation rules workbook, Banking Reporting v4.1.1, sheet banking_reporting, row v4023_a, column 'Expression' (last 60 characters of 32,700)

> <xs:element name="ei152" type="enum:enumerationItemType" substitutionGroup="xbrli:item" id="eba_ei152" xbrli:periodType="instant" nillable="true" model:domain="eba_exp:GA" model:hierarchy="http://www.eba.europa.eu/xbrl/crr/role/dict/dom/GA/GA4_1" model:fromDate="2013-12-01" model:creationDate="2013-12-01" model:modificationDate="2019-04-30" enum:domain="eba_exp:GA" enum:linkrole="http://www.eba.europa.eu/xbrl/crr/role/dict/dom/GA/GA4_1" />
>
> - Bank of England Banking Taxonomy v4.1.1 (taxonomy package and data point model), www.eba.europa.eu/eu/fr/xbrl/crr/dict/met/met.xsd, element ei152

> preventing this validation from being serialized into xbrl. Consequently, it's being omitted from the taxonomy output.
>
> - Bank of England Banking taxonomy known-issues log (27 August 2026), issue 18, v11871_m: the Bank's own description of a rule that is not serialised

> No temporary solution. The validation hasn't been serialized and is therefore excluded from the taxonomy package
>
> - Bank of England Banking taxonomy known-issues log (27 August 2026), issue 18, solution column

> Exposures and the respective LGDs for large regulated financial sector entities and unregulated financial sector entities as defined in Rules 1.3 and 1.4 of the Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part shall not be included in the calculation of column 0230, but only be included in the calculation of column 0240.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 08.01 column 0230 (basis for the boe_b0756 algebra), PDF page 111

#### Why it matters

**Expressions cut short in the workbook.** It does not fail at the gateway. The harm is on the firm's side: a firm or vendor that builds the allowed list from the workbook's Expression (286 codes, unparseable) or Simplified Expression (336 codes) will reject values the gateway accepts. Measured: C 06.02 c0050 = eba_GA:XK (Kosovo, named in the rule's own Label, absent from both expression cells) and = eba_GA:_6P are accepted by Arelle with no message; eba_GA:x29, a GA member outside hierarchy GA4_1, is rejected with enumie:InvalidFactValue. (C 06.02 was run in Arelle; C 14.00 c0190 under v4011_a rests on the identical declaration.)

**Rules the package does not carry, and boe_b0756 as written.** At the gateway nothing fails, because nothing runs. Two consequences. (1) Firms and vendors that implement the workbook as published will run checks the gateway does not, and one of them is wrong as written. boe_b0756's right-hand side subtracts raw exposure, isum(c0140), from an LGD-weighted sum; the identity that matches Annex II p.111 is c0230(r0070) x (sum c0110 - sum c0140) = sum(c0230 x (c0110 - c0140)). Two grades (exposure 600 and 400, of which large financial sector entities 100 each, LGD 40% and 30%): Annex II gives r0070 c0230 = 36.25%; left side 0.3625 x 800 = 290; right side as published 0.40 x 600 + 0.30 x 400 - 200 = 160; with the corrected right side 290. So boe_b0756 applied literally fails every sheet that holds a large or unregulated financial sector entity. boe_b0757 and boe_b0758, which have the sums-of-products form, hold whenever columns 0240 and 0250 are the exposure-weighted averages Annex II defines (pp.110-111). boe_b0755 holds if OF 08.01 column 0010 is the exposure-weighted average PD of the CRR instruction that PS1/26 did not carry over (PI-29). (EBA Q&A 2026_7840 argues that v10667_m, boe_b0758's counterpart, cannot be met exactly because maturity is reported in whole days.) This algebra is hand-worked; it cannot be run in Arelle because no formula exists. (2) For six allowed-value rules the gateway accepts values the workbook says are not allowed, e.g. C 34.06 c0050 = eba_ZZ:x427 'No CCP' passes Arelle although v10564_a lists only QCCP and NON-QCCP.

#### Other ways of reporting considered

**Expressions cut short in the workbook.** Not applicable in the usual sense (no correct return fails). Checked the opposite risk instead: no value in either workbook list is outside the taxonomy's 359-member list (Simplified Expression minus taxonomy = empty), so a value the workbook allows is never rejected by the gateway.

**Rules the package does not carry, and boe_b0756 as written.** Not applicable: no correct return fails at the gateway. Considered whether the rules might be applied outside XBRL: the workbook's Note sheet does not define 'Include in XBRL', the v4.1.1 release note does not mention it, and the Bank's own known-issues log describes a rule that is not serialised as 'excluded from the taxonomy package'. Whether the gateway runs any non-XBRL check is not determinable from published material, so 'never run' is proven for the XBRL layer only.

#### Proposed change

**Expressions cut short in the workbook.** Publish the complete rule text: split the expression so it is not cut at 32,700 characters, or replace the disjunction with a reference to the hierarchy the taxonomy already uses (GA4_1). Bring the three cells into line with each other and with the taxonomy: Expression (286 complete alternatives), Simplified Expression (336) and Label (359) should all carry the 359 members of GA4_1. State in the workbook's Note sheet what 'Include in XBRL: no' means and that allowed-value (_a) rules are enforced by the enumerated data type.

**Rules the package does not carry, and boe_b0756 as written.** (1) Define the 'Include in XBRL' column in the Note sheet and say whether a rule marked 'no' is applied by any other means. (2) For the 15 checks with no formula: either serialise them or mark them Deactivated / informational so they are not read as binding ERROR rules. (3) Correct boe_b0756 before it is ever serialised: {t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0070, c: 0230, dv: 0} i* (isum({t: OF08.02.01.01, c: 0110, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True}) i- isum({t: OF08.02.01.01, c: 0140, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True})) i= isum({t: OF08.02.01.01, c: 0230, dv: 0} * ({t: OF08.02.01.01, c: 0110, dv: 0} - {t: OF08.02.01.01, c: 0140, dv: 0})). (4) Reconcile the six allowed-value lists that are narrower than the taxonomy's enumeration (v4011_a, v4023_a, v4021_a, v6520_a, v7668_a, v10564_a): either narrow the hierarchy or widen the list; the EBA itself widened v10564_a to {x425, x426, x427} on 2022-03-10.

#### EBA precedent

**Expressions cut short in the workbook.** These are EBA allowed-value (_a) rules carried into the Bank's workbook. In the EBA list (10 June 2026, up to framework 3.5) v4011_a is live (ERROR); v4023_a was deactivated on 2020-03-10 and reactivated on 2020-12-21. Not in the Bank's known-issues logs.

**Rules the package does not carry, and boe_b0756 as written.** boe_b0755-b0758 descend from EBA v10664_m-v10667_m (C 08.01.a / C 08.02, WARNING). The EBA deactivated all four on 2021-03-10. It reactivated v10664_m, v10666_m and v10667_m on 2022-03-10 (framework 3.2.0) with sums-of-products right-hand sides, flagged Not implemented in XBRL. v10665_m (the original of boe_b0756) was deactivated again on 2024-06-13 and is not active in the 3.5 sheet. In v4.0.0 the Bank carried them as ERROR and in XBRL with the EBA's pre-3.2 right-hand side (sum(c0010) * sum(c0110) and so on); in v4.1.1 it rewrote the right-hand sides as sums of products and marked all four 'Include in XBRL: no', which matches the EBA's 3.2.0 correction and its 'Not implemented in XBRL' flag. The stray '- sum(c0140)' in boe_b0756 comes from that rewrite (v4.0.0: sum(c0230) * (sum(c0110) - sum(c0140))). The v4.0.0 forms were not weighted-average identities either - each reduced to r0070 equalling the sum of the grade values - and the v4.1.1 rewrite corrected three of the four. v10564_a, which the Bank carries with QCCP and NON-QCCP only (eba_ZZ:x425, x426), had that form in the EBA's v3.0 / v3.1 sheets and was deactivated on 2021-06-10; the EBA reactivated it on 2022-03-10 (framework 3.2.0) with x427 added, so the Bank carries the EBA's withdrawn form. Known-issues log issues 18 and 19 show the Bank records rules that fail to serialise; none of these 45 is listed.

#### Who is affected

**Expressions cut short in the workbook.** C 06.02 (group solvency) and C 14.00 (securitisation details) filers. No effect at the gateway; affects firm-side or vendor pre-validation built from the workbook.

**Rules the package does not carry, and boe_b0756 as written.** All PRA001 filers: 15 published checks (5 ERROR) that the package does not apply, 12 of them on OF 08.01/08.02, C 09.04 and C 34.01-34.09. Firm-side and vendor validators built from the workbook are affected, most by boe_b0756.

#### What a firm can do meanwhile

No validation result shows this issue. Report as the instructions require, and keep a record of any rounding or convention you had to adopt.

<a id="pi-23"></a>

### PI-23 - OF 08.07: boe_b0779 sums the share column 0050 down the roll-out classes; boe_b0778 requires shares to equal 100% while its label says 'shall not exceed'

**Status:** identified by rwa-filer, not yet raised with the Bank of England.

**Severity:** ERROR (boe_b0779, boe_b0778).

**Effect:** a return that follows the reporting instructions fails it. **Cause:** contradicts the reporting instructions; the published text and the rule as run differ.

#### The rules

| Rule | Module | Severity | Part in the issue | Where the issue applies | At the gateway |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| boe_b0779 | PRA001 | ERROR | the rule at issue | OF08.07.01.01 columns 0050 | run as published |
| boe_b0778 | PRA001 | ERROR | the rule at issue | every evaluation (a break there may also be the return's own) | run as published |
| boe_b1045 | PRA001 | ERROR | holds on the example (control) | - | run as published |
| boe_b0320 | PRA001 | ERROR | holds on the example (control) | - | run as published |

boe_b0779, as published in taxonomy 4.1.1 (label: "Total risk-weighted exposure amount reported by roll-out class|"):

```text
{t: OF08.07.01.01, r: 0260, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v0, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i= isum({t: OF08.07.01.01, r: 0180; 0190; 0200; 0210; 0220; 0230; 0240; 0250, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True, id: v1, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting})
scope({t: OF08.07.01.01, c:0010;0020;0050;0060;0070;0080;0090;0100;0110;0120;0130;0140;0150, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting})
```

boe_b0778, as published in taxonomy 4.1.1 (label: "Sum of the stated percentages shall not exceed 100%|"):

```text
isum({t: OF08.07.01.01, c: 0030; 0040; 0050, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True, id: v0, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting}) i= 1
scope({t: OF08.07.01.01, r:0180;0190;0200;0210;0220;0230;0240;0250;0260, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting})
```

#### What the rule requires

**The share column summed down the roll-out classes (boe_b0779).** For each of thirteen columns of OF 08.07 (0010, 0020, 0050 and 0060-0150), the Total row 0260 must equal the sum of the eight roll-out-class rows 0180-0250. Twelve of those columns are amounts (exposure value, risk-weighted exposure amount). Column 0050 is the percentage of a class's total exposure value that is under the IRB approach (data type percentage, metric eba_met:pi824); the other two percentage columns 0030 and 0040 are not in the scope.

**Shares must equal 100% where the label says 'shall not exceed' (boe_b0778).** c0030 (share under a permanent-partial-use permission) + c0040 (share under a roll-out plan) + c0050 (share under the IRB approach) = 1 on every roll-out-class row and on the Total row. The published label states an upper bound; the formula is an equality.

**The two rules together.** On row 0260: boe_b0779 requires c0050 = sum of the class rows' c0050; boe_b0778 requires c0030 + c0040 + c0050 = 1. Together: c0030(0260) + c0040(0260) = 1 - sum of class IRB shares. Only seven PRA001 rules touch OF 08.07 (boe_b0320, b0778, b0779, b1045-b1048) and none bounds columns 0030, 0040 or 0050 between 0 and 1: boe_b0320's non-negativity covers the amount columns only.

#### What the instructions and rules say

> TOTAL Institutions shall report the sum of the values reported in rows 0180-0250 for each of columns 0060-0150.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 08.07 row 0260, PDF page 135

> PERCENTAGE OF TOTAL EXPOSURE VALUE SUBJECT TO THE INTERNAL RATINGS BASED APPROACH (%) Institutions shall report the percentage of the total exposure value for each roll-out class for exposures that are subject to the IRB approach. Institutions shall calculate this percentage by dividing point (1) by point (2) below:
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 08.07 column 0050, PDF page 131

> (2) Total exposure value for all exposures in that roll-out class as reported in column 0020.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 08.07 column 0050, point (2), PDF page 131

> 84. Columns 0070 to 0150 shall cover the risk-weighted exposure amounts for the full spectrum of exposures, so the sum of each row for those columns shall be 100% of the risk-weighted exposure amounts for each roll-out class.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 08.07 general remarks, PDF page 130

> OTHER Institutions shall usually leave this column blank. In exceptional circumstances, such as where an institution has acquired exposures to which it applies the Standardised Approach, but it has not yet received permission under Article 148(1) or Article 150(1) of the Credit Risk: Internal
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 08.07 column 0140, PDF page 133

> Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part, these exposures shall be reported in this column.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 08.07 column 0140 (continuation on the next page), PDF page 134

> Institutions shall report the percentage of the total exposure value for each roll-out class that is subject to the Standardised Approach in accordance with a permission granted under Article 150(1) of the Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part. Institutions shall calculate this percentage by dividing (1) by (2) below:
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 08.07 column 0030, PDF page 130

> Institutions shall report the percentage of the total exposure value for exposures that are subject to a roll-out plan under Article 148(1) of the Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part for each roll-out
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 08.07 column 0040, PDF page 130

> 84. Columns 0020 to 0040 should cover the full spectrum of exposures, so the sum of each row for those three columns should be 100% of all exposure classes except of securitisation positions and deducted positions.
>
> - CRR COREP Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, C 08.07 general remarks, the text PS1/26 replaced, PDF page 116

#### Why a correct return fails

**The share column summed down the roll-out classes (boe_b0779).** A share does not add down rows. With class shares s_i and class weights w_i = class exposure value / total exposure value (w_i > 0, sum of w_i = 1), the total row's IRB share is sum(w_i x s_i); the rule demands sum(s_i). They are equal only if sum((1 - w_i) x s_i) = 0, i.e. when a single class holds all the exposure or no class has any IRB exposure. For any IRB firm with exposure in two or more roll-out classes the equality is false. The instruction's own row-0260 sum stops at columns 0060-0150 and does not reach column 0050. Example: s = (0.8, 1.0), w = (0.25, 0.75): the total is 0.95, the rule demands 1.8.

**Shares must equal 100% where the label says 'shall not exceed' (boe_b0778).** The three shares are defined by the basis on which an exposure is treated: under an Article 150(1) permission (c0030), under an Article 148(1) roll-out plan (c0040), under the IRB approach (c0050). Annex II itself describes a fourth population in the class: exposures on the standardised approach with neither permission yet, whose RWEA goes in column 0140. Those exposures are in the denominator (column 0020, all exposures of the class) and in none of the three numerators, so the shares total less than 100% and the equality fails. The PS1/26 instructions no longer say the three percentage columns total 100%: paragraph 84 now makes that statement about the RWEA columns 0070-0150 (which boe_b1045 checks and which include column 0140). The rule's own label asks only that the percentages not exceed 100%. The Bank may answer that Art. 147C(1) does not permit such exposures. But Annex II (pp.133-134) instructs firms to report exactly this position in column 0140, and a rule should not make an instructed figure unfilable at ERROR; if the position is to be flagged, a WARNING on c0140 > 0 does it directly.

**The two rules together.** Arelle accepts a return that satisfies both: total IRB share 1.8 (the row sum) and total PPU share -0.8. So the pair is satisfiable, but only by figures that are not shares. For a return whose percentages are true shares (each between 0 and 1, the total row computed on the totals) the two rules hold together only when sum(s_i) = sum(w_i x s_i), the single-class case above. The defect is boe_b0779's column 0050 on its own; boe_b0778 is what stops a firm from simply filing the row sum, and the absence of any bound on the percentage cells is what leaves the nonsense solution open.

#### Worked example

OF 08.07 for an IRB firm with two roll-out classes (reference date 31 March 2027). Row 0210 (financial, large and other general corporates): exposure value 1,000,000 (c0020), of which 700,000 under the IRB approach (c0010), 200,000 under a permanent-partial-use permission and 100,000 from an acquired portfolio on the standardised approach with no Article 148(1) or 150(1) permission yet; shares by the Annex II definitions c0030 = 0.2, c0040 = 0, c0050 = 0.7 (total 0.9); RWEA c0060 = 720,000 = 200,000 (c0090) + 100,000 (c0140, 'other') + 420,000 (c0150). Row 0230 (retail secured by residential property): 3,000,000, all IRB; shares 0 / 0 / 1.0; RWEA 450,000. Row 0260 (Total): c0010 = 3,700,000, c0020 = 4,000,000, shares 200,000 / 4,000,000 = 0.05, 0 and 3,700,000 / 4,000,000 = 0.925; RWEA 1,170,000 = 200,000 + 100,000 + 870,000. boe_b0779 fails on column 0050 only (0.925 against 0.7 + 1.0 = 1.7) and holds on the amount columns; boe_b0778 fails on rows 0210 (0.9) and 0260 (0.975) and holds on row 0230; boe_b1045 (the RWEA columns add up) holds on every row.

Arelle's result on it:

| Rule | Satisfied | Unsatisfied | What the example shows |
|---|---|---|---|
| boe_b0320 | 16 | 0 | holds |
| boe_b0778 | 1 | 2 | fails |
| boe_b0779 | 6 | 1 | fails |
| boe_b1045 | 3 | 0 | holds |
| boe_b1046 | 0 | 0 | - |
| boe_b1047 | 0 | 0 | - |
| boe_b1048 | 0 | 0 | - |

#### Other ways of reporting considered

**The share column summed down the roll-out classes (boe_b0779).** On the two-class return of the paragraph above (class IRB shares 0.8 and 1.0, all shares true): (a) Report the row sum (1.8, i.e. 180%) as the total IRB share: boe_b0779 [6,0] but boe_b0778 fails on r0260 [2,1] (0.05 + 0 + 1.8). (b) As (a) and a total PPU share of -0.8: both rules pass, with a 180% and a -80% share that mean nothing. (c) Leave the three share cells of r0260 blank, reading the row-0260 instruction literally: boe_b0779 still fails on column 0050 [5,1] because the blank total defaults to 0 against a row sum of 1.8. (d) Leave c0050 blank on the class rows: boe_b0778 then fails on every class with an IRB share. No compliant alternative.

**Shares must equal 100% where the label says 'shall not exceed' (boe_b0778).** (a) Count the acquired exposures in c0030: contradicts the column definition (no Article 150(1) permission exists) and is inconsistent with their RWEA sitting in column 0140 instead of 0070-0120. (b) Count them in c0040: contradicts 'subject to a roll-out plan under Article 148(1)'. (c) Count them in c0050: they are not under the IRB approach. (d) Leave the shares blank on the row: the instruction requires them where the class has exposure. None is compliant; (a) is what a firm would do in practice to get through the gateway.

**The two rules together.** With true class-row shares, the only way to pass both rules with two or more classes is a total IRB share equal to the sum of class shares with the excess over 100% offset by a negative share in c0030 or c0040. It is not Annex-II-compliant (c0030, c0040 and c0050 on row 0260 would not be percentages of the total exposure value).

#### Proposed change

**The share column summed down the roll-out classes (boe_b0779).** Remove 0050 from the column scope of boe_b0779: scope({t: OF08.07.01.01, c:0010;0020;0060;0070;0080;0090;0100;0110;0120;0130;0140;0150}). boe_b0778 already checks the three shares on row 0260.

**Shares must equal 100% where the label says 'shall not exceed' (boe_b0778).** Make the formula match its label: isum({t: OF08.07.01.01, c: 0030; 0040; 0050}) i<= 1 on the same rows (this also accepts a zero-filled empty class; see Appendix B). Alternatively deactivate it, as the EBA did with v09796_m on 10 June 2025, or at least downgrade it to WARNING, or amend Annex II to say in which share column exposures reported in column 0140 are counted.

**The two rules together.** As above (remove 0050 from boe_b0779's column scope). Optionally add the EBA's bounds for OF 08.07 columns 0030, 0040 and 0050 (each >= 0 and <= 1 on rows 0180-0260) so that an out-of-range share cannot satisfy boe_b0778.

#### EBA precedent

**The share column summed down the roll-out classes (boe_b0779).** The Bank's v4.0.0 extract names EBA v09797_m as the equivalent: '{r0170} = {r0010} + {r0040} + {r0050} + {r0090} + {r0150} + {r0160}' (WARNING). The EBA deactivated it on 2021-06-30, when it applied to all columns of C 08.07, and reactivated it on 2022-03-10 (framework 3.2.0) on columns 0010 and 0020 only. The EBA thus dropped the percentage columns that boe_b0779 keeps. The Bank itself withdrew the same pattern elsewhere in v4.1.1: boe_b0752_1 (PD), _22/_23 (LGD) and _24 (maturity), which summed averaged OF 08.02 columns into OF 08.01 row 0070, are in the v4.0.0 workbook and absent from the v4.1.1 workbook and rule book.

**Shares must equal 100% where the label says 'shall not exceed' (boe_b0778).** EBA v09796_m, the same equality on C 08.07 (WARNING), was deactivated by the EBA on 10 June 2025; the Bank carries it as an ERROR. CRR Annex II paragraph 84 reads 'Columns 0020 to 0040 should cover the full spectrum of exposures, so the sum of each row for those three columns should be 100%', an apparent misnumbering of the three percentage columns 0030-0050 (that reading is an interpretation); PS1/26 paragraph 84 makes the 100% statement about the RWEA columns 0070-0150 instead, and adds column 0140.

**The two rules together.** The EBA bounds every C 08.07 share: v09769_m '{c0030} <= 1', v09770_m '{c0040} <= 1', v09771_m '{c0050} <= 1' and v10300_s '{C 08.07} >= 0' on columns 0010-0050 (all live WARNINGs). None of the four has a PRA001 counterpart for OF 08.07, which is why the out-of-range solution passes the Bank's rules.

#### Who is affected

**The share column summed down the roll-out classes (boe_b0779).** Every IRB firm reporting OF 08.07 with exposure in two or more roll-out classes, at least one of them with IRB exposure, on every return. Not in the Bank's known-issues logs of 27 August and 16 November 2026.

**Shares must equal 100% where the label says 'shall not exceed' (boe_b0778).** Narrow: a firm with standardised-approach exposures in a roll-out class that have neither an Article 150(1) permission nor an Article 148(1) roll-out plan, which Annex II calls exceptional (an acquired portfolio).

**The two rules together.** Not a separate break: the same population as above.

#### What a firm can do meanwhile

Report the figures the instructions require; do not change correct figures to satisfy the rule. An Error-severity break blocks the submission at the gateway: if the gateway rejects the return on this rule, raise it with the PRA, citing this issue.

**Status:** identified by rwa-filer, not yet raised with the Bank of England.

**Severity:** ERROR (boe_b0735, boe_b0736, boe_b0738, boe_b0739, boe_b0740, boe_b0737).

**Effect:** a return that follows the reporting instructions fails it. **Cause:** contradicts the reporting instructions; the rounding allowance the rule gives.

#### The rules

| boe_b0736 | PRA001 | ERROR | the rule at issue | OF08.01.01.01 sheets 0002, 0010; OF08.01.01.02 sheets 0002, 0010 (a break there may also be the return's own) | run as published |
| boe_b0738 | PRA001 | ERROR | the rule at issue | OF08.01.01.01 sheets 0002, 0010; OF08.01.01.02 sheets 0002, 0010 (a break there may also be the return's own) | run as published |
| boe_b0739 | PRA001 | ERROR | the rule at issue | OF08.01.01.01 sheets 0002, 0010; OF08.01.01.02 sheets 0002, 0010 (a break there may also be the return's own) | run as published |
| boe_b0740 | PRA001 | ERROR | the rule at issue | OF08.01.01.01 sheets 0002, 0010; OF08.01.01.02 sheets 0002, 0010 (a break there may also be the return's own) | run as published |

#### What the rule requires

**Exposure, RWEA, expected loss and provisions (boe_b0735, boe_b0736, boe_b0738-b0740).** On each of 17 sheets, including 0002 'Total (FIRB approach and slotting approach)' and 0010 'Corporates - Specialised Lending (FIRB approach or slotting approach)', OF 08.01 row 0010 (Total exposures) less the three counterparty-credit-risk rows 0040, 0050 and 0060 must equal the sum of the OF 08.03 PD-range rows 0010, 0040, 0050, 0060, 0070, 0100, 0130 and 0170: exposure value (boe_b0736, c0110 against c0040), RWEA (boe_b0738, c0260 against c0090), expected loss after post-model adjustments (boe_b0739, c0282 against c0100) and value adjustments and provisions (boe_b0740, c0290 against c0110). boe_b0735 requires OF 08.01.01.02 row 0010 c0100 (exposure after CRM substitution, pre-conversion factors, of which off-balance-sheet items) to equal the sum of OF 08.03 c0020 over the same rows; that column holds no CCR, so the rule has no CCR term. None of the rules takes off row 0080 (slotting). In the XBRL formula the OF 08.03 sum falls back to an empty sequence, so a sheet with no OF 08.03 fact is read as zero.

**Obligor counts (boe_b0737).** On the same 17 sheets as boe_b0736: OF 08.01 row 0010 c0300 (number of obligors) less the sum of c0300 on the CCR rows 0040, 0050 and 0060 must equal the sum of OF 08.03 c0060 (number of obligors) over PD rows 0010, 0040, 0050, 0060, 0070, 0100, 0130 and 0170. Row 0080 (slotting obligors) is not subtracted.

#### What the instructions and rules say

> SPECIALISED LENDING SLOTTING APPROACH: TOTAL Exposures subject to the slotting approach. This shall only apply to the exposure sub-class ‘corporate – specialised lending’.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 08.01 row 0080, PDF page 117

> In OF CR IRB 2, OF CR IRB 3, OF CR IRB 5 and OF 34.7, “FIRB” in cases where the FIRB approach is applied; and “AIRB” in cases where the AIRB approach is applied.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, paragraph 75, PDF page 101

> (The Total template must be reported for the FIRB and the slotting approaches and, separately for the AIRB approach.)
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, paragraph 76, PDF page 99

> OF CR IRB 6 provides all relevant parameters used for the calculation of credit risk capital requirements under the slotting approach for specialised lending.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, paragraph 76, PDF page 99

> Exposures shall be allocated to an appropriate bucket of the fixed PD range based on the PD estimated for each obligor assigned to this exposure class
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 08.03 rows (PD range), PDF page 122

> shall be submitted solely by institutions subject to an equivalent disclosure requirement, with the same disclosure frequency and at the same consolidated level
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Appendix 1: the PRA Rulebook instruments (Basel 3.1), Reporting (CRR) Part, Article 8(1), PDF page 484

> the institution shall report the number of legal entities/obligors which were separately rated, regardless of the number of different loans or exposures granted.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 08.01 column 0300, PDF page 114

> Information reported in this template shall not include data on specialised lending exposures on the slotting approach, which is included in template OF08.06.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, section 3.3.5.1, paragraph 77 (OF 08.03 general remarks), PDF page 119

#### Why a correct return fails

**Exposure, RWEA, expected loss and provisions (boe_b0735, boe_b0736, boe_b0738-b0740).** On sheets 0002 and 0010, OF 08.01 row 0010 includes row 0080 (slotting) as well as row 0070 (exposures assigned to obligor grades); in the example row 0010 = row 0070 + row 0080, because rows 0170, 0175 and 0180 are empty. Paragraph 77 keeps slotting out of OF 08.03, so the OF 08.03 PD rows add up to the non-CCR part of row 0070 only. Left side minus right side is therefore row 0080 in the rule's column. In the example, sheet 0010: exposure value 36,000,000 against 12,000,000 (gap 24,000,000 = r0080 c0110); RWEA 29,790,000 against 8,190,000 (gap 21,600,000); expected loss 222,000 against 30,000 (gap 192,000); provisions -80,000 against -30,000 (gap -50,000); off-balance-sheet pre-conversion-factor amount 15,000,000 against 5,000,000 (gap 10,000,000 = OF 08.01.01.02 r0080 c0100). At this scale the gaps far exceed any rounding allowance, at any decimals the Filing Manual permits for monetary facts (rule 2.18: decimals >= -3). Each rule breaks whenever the slotting figure in its own column is non-zero beyond the rounding allowance. So boe_b0735 needs the slotting book to have undrawn or other off-balance-sheet items (with fully drawn slotting loans it holds), and boe_b0740 needs provisions on slotting exposures. A book whose specialised lending is all on slotting breaks too: row 0010 on sheets 0010 and 0002 carries the slotting amounts, OF 08.03 has nothing to report for them, and the empty sum is read as zero. Paragraph 76, 'The Total template must be reported for the FIRB and the slotting approaches and, separately for the AIRB approach', read alone is the best counter-argument: that the OF 08.03 Total sheet includes slotting. But the same sentence covers OF CR IRB 2, which paragraph 76 itself defines as the exposures of row 0070 of OF CR IRB 1, so it cannot hold slotting either: 'FIRB and slotting' names the sheet, and paragraph 77 is the specific instruction.

**Obligor counts (boe_b0737).** The gap is the number of slotting obligors (row 0080 c0300), as for the monetary rules. When counts are filed with decimals 0 (the Filing Manual's setting for integers), each count carries an allowance of 0.5 and the interval arithmetic adds them up; filed with decimals INF ('exact as written', which the Manual accepts for every numeric type), there is no allowance. At decimals 0 the rule tolerates a gap of 0.5 times the number of count facts it reads on the sheet (row 0010, each reported CCR row, each reported OF 08.03 PD row). It breaks only when the slotting obligors exceed that. Measured in Arelle: one populated PD row and 1 slotting obligor, 2 against 1, satisfied (at decimals INF the same position is unsatisfied [1,1]); the same with 2 slotting obligors, 3 against 1, unsatisfied (the example); three populated PD rows and 2 slotting obligors, 5 against 3, allowance 2.0, satisfied; a sheet holding only slotting with 1 obligor and no OF 08.03 fact, 1 against an exact 0, allowance 0.5, unsatisfied. So whether one slotting obligor breaks the rule depends on the decimals and on the number of count facts; the rule is wrong on sheets 0002 and 0010 and breaks for any firm whose slotting obligors outnumber half the count facts involved.

#### Worked example

Sheet 0010 (Corporates - Specialised Lending, FIRB approach or slotting approach), reference date 31 March 2027. One F-IRB object-finance obligor: drawn 10,000,000 plus an undrawn commitment of 5,000,000 at a 40% conversion factor, exposure value 12,000,000, PD 0.625% (OF 08.03 row 0060, 0.50 to <0.75), LGD 40%, maturity 2.5 years, RWEA 8,190,000 (8,190,357 by the Article 153(1) formula, rounded to thousands for readability), expected loss 30,000, provisions -30,000. Two slotting project-finance obligors, graded Good with 2.5 years or more remaining (Art. 153(5): 90%; Art. 158(6): 0.8% expected loss): drawn 20,000,000 plus undrawn 10,000,000 at 40%, exposure value 24,000,000, RWEA 21,600,000, expected loss 192,000, provisions -50,000. Annex II asks for: OF 08.01 row 0010 = 36,000,000 / 29,790,000 / 222,000 / -80,000 / 3 (c0110 / c0260 / c0282 / c0290 / c0300); row 0070 = 12,000,000 / 8,190,000 / 30,000 / -30,000 / 1; row 0080 = 24,000,000 / 21,600,000 / 192,000 / -50,000 / 2; OF 08.01.01.02 c0100: row 0010 = 15,000,000, row 0070 = 5,000,000, row 0080 = 10,000,000; OF 08.02 one grade with 1 obligor; OF 08.03 sheet 0010 row 0060 = the F-IRB obligor alone (c0020 5,000,000, c0040 12,000,000, c0060 1, c0090 8,190,000, c0100 30,000, c0110 -30,000). In the same return, sheet 0012 (Corporates - Other general corporates - non-SME, FIRB) holds one F-IRB obligor (8,000,000 drawn, PD 0.3125%, LGD 40%, RWEA 3,948,000; 3,948,145 by the formula, rounded likewise) in OF 08.01 and OF 08.03 row 0050, where every tie holds, and OF 02.00 r0290 c0010 = 8,190,000 for boe_b0618, which subtracts row 0080 and holds. Counts are stated with decimals 0.

#### Other ways of reporting considered

**Exposure, RWEA, expected loss and provisions (boe_b0735, boe_b0736, boe_b0738-b0740).** (a) Put the slotting exposure into an OF 08.03 PD row: all six rules then hold [3,0], but paragraph 77 forbids it and a slotting exposure has no PD estimate to bucket on. (b) Leave slotting out of OF 08.01 row 0010: row 0010 is 'TOTAL EXPOSURES', row 0080 is part of it, and the Bank's boe_b0618 would then misstate OF 02.00 r0290 by the slotting RWEA. (c) Report slotting on another sheet: Annex II row 0080 applies only to corporate specialised lending and boe_b0206 expects row 0080 empty elsewhere. (d) Not filing OF 08.03: the rules run only when both tables carry a filing indicator (assertion sets aset-of08.01.01.01_of08.03.01.01 and aset-of08.01.01.02_of08.03.01.01), but firms within Reporting (CRR) Part Article 8(1) must file it. No compliant alternative satisfies the rules.

**Obligor counts (boe_b0737).** As for the monetary rules: counting slotting obligors in OF 08.03 would satisfy the rule and is what paragraph 77 forbids; leaving them out of OF 08.01 row 0010 misstates the total. The allowance depends on the decimals the count is stated with (0 or INF), not on the figures.

#### Proposed change

**Exposure, RWEA, expected loss and provisions (boe_b0735, boe_b0736, boe_b0738-b0740).** Either (A), scope: remove 0002 and 0010 from both z lists of boe_b0735, b0736, b0738, b0739 and b0740 (and b0737), leaving the 15 sheets that cannot hold slotting. This is the change that is never wrong. Or (B), expression, to keep the check on those sheets. boe_b0735: read row 0070 instead of row 0010, i.e. {t: OF08.01.01.02, r: 0070, c: 0100, dv: 0, seq: False} i= isum({t: OF08.03.01.01, r: 0010; 0040; 0050; 0060; 0070; 0100; 0130; 0170, c: 0020, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True}). boe_b0736, b0738, b0739, b0740: also subtract the slotting row, i.e. {t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0010, c: C, dv: 0, seq: False} i- isum({t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0040; 0050; 0060, c: C, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True}) i- {t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0080, c: C, dv: 0, seq: False} i= isum({t: OF08.03.01.01, r: 0010; 0040; 0050; 0060; 0070; 0100; 0130; 0170, c: D, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True}) with (C, D) = (0110, 0040), (0260, 0090), (0282, 0100), (0290, 0110). On the example this gives 36,000,000 - 24,000,000 = 12,000,000, 29,790,000 - 21,600,000 = 8,190,000, 222,000 - 192,000 = 30,000, -80,000 + 50,000 = -30,000, and 5,000,000 = 5,000,000 for boe_b0735. Caveat on (B): a slotting exposure that is itself a derivative or SFT sits in rows 0040-0060 and in row 0080, so it would be subtracted twice; the taxonomy provides for that case (OF 08.01.01.02 r0080 c0130) but splits it for exposure value only. (B) follows the Bank's own boe_b0618 (r0010 - r0080 on sheet 0010) and the boe_b0752 / boe_b0814 family (row 0070).

**Obligor counts (boe_b0737).** Take sheets 0002 and 0010 out of both z lists of boe_b0737, together with the rest of the family (option A above). If the check is kept there, subtract the slotting row: {t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0010, c: 0300, dv: 0, seq: False} i- isum({t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0040; 0050; 0060, c: 0300, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True}) i- {t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0080, c: 0300, dv: 0, seq: False} i= isum({t: OF08.03.01.01, r: 0010; 0040; 0050; 0060; 0070; 0100; 0130; 0170, c: 0060, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True}). On the example: 3 - 0 - 2 = 1. An obligor count is a distinct count, so the Bank may prefer WARNING for this member whatever it does with the others.

#### EBA precedent

**Exposure, RWEA, expected loss and provisions (boe_b0735, boe_b0736, boe_b0738-b0740).** These are the Bank's restatements of EBA v09773_m to v09778_m (C 08.01 against C 08.03); the Bank's v4.0.0 workbook names them as the equivalents. In the EBA rule list all six are severity WARNING, added in release 3.0.0, deactivated on 2021-03-10 and never reactivated; the extract records no reason. The Bank carries them at ERROR. The EBA's v4248_i ('{C 02.00, r0290, c0010} == {C 08.01.a, r0010, c0260, s0010}') does not subtract row 0080; the subtraction is the Bank's own addition in boe_b0618, its restatement of v4248_i. So the Bank adjusted that restated EBA check for slotting on sheet 0010, but made no such adjustment when restating v09773_m-v09778_m.

**Obligor counts (boe_b0737).** EBA v09775_m (C 08.01 c0300 against C 08.03 c0060): WARNING, added in release 3.0.0, deactivated 2021-03-10, not reactivated, per the EBA rule list. The Bank carries it at ERROR.

#### Who is affected

**Exposure, RWEA, expected loss and provisions (boe_b0735, boe_b0736, boe_b0738-b0740).** Every firm that files OF 08.03 (Reporting (CRR) Part Art. 8(1): firms with the equivalent disclosure requirement) and has any exposure on the slotting approach, on both sheet 0010 and sheet 0002, every period from 1 January 2027. A mixed F-IRB and slotting book is not needed: a specialised-lending book that is all on slotting breaks as well.

**Obligor counts (boe_b0737).** Firms that file OF 08.03 and whose slotting obligors on sheet 0010 or 0002 exceed half the number of count facts the rule reads there. A slotting-only specialised-lending sheet breaks from the first obligor, and so does any sheet with slotting for a firm that files counts with decimals INF, whatever the number of populated PD rows. A firm with many populated PD rows and one or two slotting obligors passes by rounding, which also shows how weak the check is on a well-populated sheet.

#### What a firm can do meanwhile

Report the figures the instructions require; do not change correct figures to satisfy the rule. An Error-severity break blocks the submission at the gateway: if the gateway rejects the return on this rule, raise it with the PRA, citing this issue.
