### PI-25 - boe_b0793 checks the output floor as x * (S-TREA + OF-ADJ)

**Status:** identified by rwa-filer, not yet raised with the Bank of England.

**Severity:** ERROR (boe_b0793).

**Effect:** a return that follows the reporting instructions fails it. **Cause:** contradicts the reporting instructions.

#### The rules

| Rule | Module | Severity | Part in the issue | Where the issue applies | At the gateway |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| boe_b0793 | PRA001 | ERROR | the rule at issue | every evaluation | run as published |
| boe_b1092 | PRA001 | WARNING | holds on the example (control) | - | run as published |
| boe_b0383 | PRA001 | WARNING | holds on the example (control) | - | run as published |
| boe_b0957 | PRA001 | ERROR | related | - | run as published |
| boe_b0359 | PRA001 | ERROR | related | - | run as published |

boe_b0793, as published in taxonomy 4.1.1 (label: "Total credit risk RWAs under standardised approaches should reflect the sum of SA on the SA, and IRB exposures on the SA|"):

```text
if not(isNull({t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0010, c: 0030, dv: emptySequence(), seq: False, id: v0, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting})) then {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0010, c: 0030, dv: emptySequence(), seq: False, id: v0, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i= ({t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0036, c: 0030, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v5, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i+ {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0040, c: 0020, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v1, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i+ {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0490, c: 0010, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v2, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i+ {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0520, c: 0020, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v3, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i+ {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 5898, c: 0010, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v12, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i+ {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0590, c: 0010, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v6, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i+ {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0630, c: 0010, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v7, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i+ {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0640, c: 0020, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v8, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i+ {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0680, c: 0020, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v9, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i+ {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0690, c: 0020, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v10, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting}) i* {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0035, c: 0030, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v11, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} else true()
```

#### What the rule requires

Whenever OF 02.00 row 0010 column 0030 (the output floor) is reported, it must equal (r0036 c0030 [OF-ADJ] + r0040 c0020 + r0490 c0010 + r0520 c0020 + r5898 c0010 + r0590 c0010 + r0630 c0010 + r0640 c0020 + r0680 c0020 + r0690 c0020) multiplied by r0035 c0030 (the output floor multiplier x). The nine risk rows are S-TREA; the adjustment sits inside the bracket, so the rule states x * (S-TREA + OF-ADJ). The workbook text and the XBRL formula say the same thing.

#### What the instructions and rules say

> TREA = max {U-TREA; x ∙ S-TREA + OF-ADJ}
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Appendix 1: the PRA Rulebook instruments (Basel 3.1), Required Level of Own Funds (CRR) Part, Article 92(2A), PDF page 13

> S-TREA= the standardised total risk exposure amount of the entity calculated in accordance with paragraph 3A; x= 72.5%; [...] OF-ADJ= 12.5 * (IRB T2 – IRB CET1 – GCRA + SA T2);
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Appendix 1: the PRA Rulebook instruments (Basel 3.1), Article 92(2A), definitions (the heading 'Output Floor Adjustments' left out), PDF page 13

> The standardised total risk exposure amount shall be calculated as the sum of points (a) to (f) of paragraph 3: (a) after having taken into account paragraph 4; and (b) calculated without using any of the following approaches or as if permission to use the following approaches has not been granted:
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Appendix 1: the PRA Rulebook instruments (Basel 3.1), Article 92(3A), PDF page 15

> an institution or CRR consolidation entity may apply the following factor x during the periods specified below: (a) 60% during the period from 1 January 2027 to 31 December 2027; (b) 65% during the period from 1 January 2028 to 31 December 2028; (c) 70% during the period from 1 January 2029 to 31 December 2029.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Appendix 1: the PRA Rulebook instruments (Basel 3.1), Article 92(5), PDF page 15

> The output floor (reported in row 0010 column 0030) should reflect the formula provided in Article 92 (2a) of the Required Level of Own Funds (CRR) Part of the PRA Rulebook: “x ∙ S-TREA + OF-ADJ” where x = the output floor multiplier, reported in row 0035 S-TREA = the total of all SA exposures provided in columns 0010 and 0020; and OF-ADJ = the output floor adjustment, reported in row 0036
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 02.00 row 0010, PDF page 29

> 1.03 Output floor adjustment (OF-ADJ) Indicate the total adjustment to the output floor described in Article 92 (2a) of the Required Level of Own Funds (CRR) Part of the PRA Rulebook as “OF-ADJ”.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 02.00 row 0036, PDF page 29

> This should be reported after applying the output floor multiplier and output floor adjustment as per Article 92 of the Required Level of Own Funds (CRR) Part of the PRA Rulebook.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 02.00 column 0030, PDF page 39

#### Why a correct return fails

Article 92(2A) and Annex II give floor = x * S-TREA + OF-ADJ. The rule checks floor = x * (S-TREA + OF-ADJ). The two differ by (1 - x) * OF-ADJ, and x is never above 0.725 (boe_b0359), so the gap is at least 27.5% of OF-ADJ and 40% of it in 2027. Row 0036 is OF-ADJ itself: the taxonomy labels the row and its metric boe_met:mi10099 'Output floor adjustment (OF-ADJ)', Annex II says to report 'the total adjustment ... described in Article 92 (2a) ... as OF-ADJ', and neither Annex II nor the rules define a pre-multiplier adjustment (the term OF-ADJ appears only on Annex II p.29 and Appendix 1 p.13, and the phrase 'output floor adjustment' in the column 0030 instruction on Annex II p.39; it is 12.5 times own-funds items, not an RWEA). In the example the floor is 0.60 x 1,170,000 + 50,000 = 752,000 and the rule expects (50,000 + 1,170,000) x 0.60 = 732,000: 20,000 apart. The rule holds only when (1 - x) * |OF-ADJ| is inside the propagated rounding allowance, roughly 0.00005 x (S-TREA + OF-ADJ) when x is filed to 4 decimals: on S-TREA 1,170,000 a gap of 40 is satisfied (OF-ADJ 100) and a gap of 80 is not (OF-ADJ 200). The Filing Manual's accuracy table gives percentages at 4 decimals or more and accepts INF, so the multiplier's allowance can only be that small or smaller: the break does not depend on the filer's decimals.

#### Worked example

An IM firm at 31 March 2027, GBP units, x = 60% (Article 92(5)(a)). Credit risk RWEA 700,000 on all approaches and 1,000,000 on standardised approaches only (r0040 c0010 / c0020); market risk 50,000 on both (r0520); operational risk 100,000 (r0590 c0010); CVA 20,000 on both (r0640). U-TREA = 870,000 (r0010 c0010); S-TREA = 1,170,000. OF-ADJ = 12.5 x (IRB T2 4,000 - IRB CET1 0 - GCRA 0 + SA T2 0) = 50,000 (r0036 c0030). Annex II and Article 92(2A): r0010 c0030 = 0.60 x 1,170,000 + 50,000 = 752,000; r0034 = false because 752,000 is below 870,000. boe_b0793 expects 732,000.

Arelle's result on it:

| Rule | Satisfied | Unsatisfied | What the example shows |
|---|---|---|---|
| boe_b0359 | 1 | 0 | - |
| boe_b0383 | 1 | 0 | holds |
| boe_b0712 | 1 | 0 | - |
| boe_b0793 | 0 | 1 | fails |
| boe_b0957 | 1 | 0 | - |
| boe_b1092 | 1 | 0 | holds |

#### Other ways of reporting considered

(1) Report the floor the rule's way, 732,000: boe_b0793 is satisfied, but the figure is not the Article 92(2A) floor, and boe_b0787 to b0792, b0560, b0561 and b0565 take row 0010 c0030 as TREA whenever it exceeds c0010. (2) Gross row 0036 up to OF-ADJ / x = 83,333 and keep the floor at 752,000: satisfied, but row 0036 is then not the OF-ADJ of Article 92(2A). (3) Leave row 0036 blank: boe_b0957 (ERROR) requires rows 0034, 0035 and 0036 whenever row 0010 c0030 is reported. (4) Leave row 0010 c0030 blank: the rule is then true(), but Annex II p.28 makes column 0030 a requirement for IM firms in scope. None is a compliant way to report the position.

#### Proposed change

Move row 0036 out of the bracket: if not(isNull({t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0010, c: 0030, dv: emptySequence(), seq: False, id: v0})) then {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0010, c: 0030, dv: emptySequence(), seq: False, id: v0} i= ({t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0040, c: 0020, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v1} i+ {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0490, c: 0010, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v2} i+ {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0520, c: 0020, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v3} i+ {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 5898, c: 0010, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v12} i+ {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0590, c: 0010, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v6} i+ {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0630, c: 0010, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v7} i+ {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0640, c: 0020, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v8} i+ {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0680, c: 0020, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v9} i+ {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0690, c: 0020, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v10}) i* {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0035, c: 0030, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v11} i+ {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0036, c: 0030, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v5} else true(). In the formula: iaf:numeric-equal($v0, iaf:numeric-add(iaf:numeric-multiply(<the nine-term sum without $v5>, $v11), $v5)). On the example: 1,170,000 x 0.60 + 50,000 = 752,000. The label could also be changed to say what the rule checks, for example 'Output floor (r0010 c0030) = output floor multiplier x S-TREA + OF-ADJ, Article 92(2A)'; today it reads 'Total credit risk RWAs under standardised approaches should reflect the sum of SA on the SA, and IRB exposures on the SA'.

#### EBA precedent

None. boe_b0793 is Bank-authored (the v4.0.0 extract lists no EBA equivalent) and reads the same in v4.0.0 and v4.1.1. The Bank's known-issues logs of August and November 2026 and the v4.1.1 release note do not mention it.

#### Who is affected

Every firm in scope of the output floor that reports OF 02.00 column 0030 with a non-zero OF-ADJ, every period from 1 January 2027. OF-ADJ is 12.5 x (IRB T2 - IRB CET1 - GCRA + SA T2), so it is non-zero whenever IRB provisions differ from expected loss, which is the normal case. A firm that passes by reporting the rule's figure misstates the floor by (1 - x) x OF-ADJ: too low when OF-ADJ is positive, too high when it is negative.

#### What a firm can do meanwhile

Report the figures the instructions require; do not change correct figures to satisfy the rule. An Error-severity break blocks the submission at the gateway: if the gateway rejects the return on this rule, raise it with the PRA, citing this issue.

### PI-26 - boe_b0346: average LGD of all exposures must be at least that of defaulted exposures

**Status:** identified by rwa-filer, not yet raised with the Bank of England.

**Severity:** WARNING (boe_b0346).

**Effect:** a return that follows the reporting instructions fails it. **Cause:** states as a rule what holds only as a tendency.

#### The rules

| Rule | Module | Severity | Part in the issue | Where the issue applies | At the gateway |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| boe_b0346 | PRA001 | WARNING | the rule at issue | every evaluation | run as published |
| boe_b0349 | PRA001 | WARNING | holds on the example (control) | - | run as published |
| boe_b0668 | PRA001 | ERROR | related | - | run as published |
| boe_b0682 | PRA001 | ERROR | related | - | run as published |

boe_b0346, as published in taxonomy 4.1.1 (label: "OF WHICH: DEFAULTED (%) exposures shall not exceed EXPOSURE WEIGHTED AVERAGE LGD (%)|"):

```text
{t: OF09.02.01.01, c: 0090, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v0, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i>= {t: OF09.02.01.01, c: 0100, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v1, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting}
scope({t: OF09.02.01.01, r:0020;0030;0042;0048;0049;0050;0055;0060;0071;0072;0073;0074;0100;0105;0120;0130;0150, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting})
```

#### What the rule requires

On 17 class rows of every OF 09.02 country sheet, the exposure-weighted average LGD of all exposures (col 0090) must be greater than or equal to the exposure-weighted average LGD of the defaulted exposures (col 0100). Label: 'OF WHICH: DEFAULTED (%) exposures shall not exceed EXPOSURE WEIGHTED AVERAGE LGD (%)'.

#### What the instructions and rules say

> Same definition as for columns 0230 and 0240 of OF CR IRB template: the exposure weighted average LGD (%) shall refer to all exposures, including exposures to large financial sector entities and unregulated financial sector entities as defined in Rules 1.3 and 1.4 of the Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part. Article 181(1)(h) of the Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part shall be taken into account.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 09.02 col 0090, PDF page 142

> Exposure weighted LGD for those exposures which have been classified as defaulted exposures in accordance with Article 178 of the Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 09.02 col 0100 'Of which: defaulted', PDF page 142

> the institution shall, subject to point (h)(ii), for the specific case of exposures already in default, ensure that the LGD in default reflects downturn conditions where the estimates of LGD in default that are appropriate for an economic downturn are more conservative than the long-run average LGD for defaulted exposures;
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Appendix 1: the PRA Rulebook instruments (Basel 3.1), Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part, Article 181(1)(h)(i), PDF page 135

> if PD = 1, i.e., for defaulted exposures: RW = max{0 , 12.5 ∙(LGD −BEEL)};
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Appendix 1: the PRA Rulebook instruments (Basel 3.1), Article 154(1)(a) (retail; Art. 153(1)(b) is the AIRB corporate equivalent, p.101), PDF page 104

#### Why a correct return fails

Cols 0090 and 0100 are the same metric (eba_met:pi128 'Exposure weighted average LGD'); col 0100 only adds the dimension member 'defaulted'. An average over a population and the average over one of its subsets have no ordering: with weights w for defaulted and (1-w) for the rest, col 0090 = (1-w) x LGD_performing + w x LGD_defaulted, which is below col 0100 exactly when LGD_defaulted > LGD_performing. Under the AIRB approach that is the normal state: LGD in default must reflect downturn conditions and sit above BEEL by an unexpected-loss margin (Art. 181(1)(h)), while performing LGDs average over cured and low-loss outcomes. The rule copies the additive 'of which <= total' pattern (as in boe_b0349, cols 0107/0105) onto an averaged column. The Bank's own boe_b0668 / boe_b0682 treat these same columns as averages (the total row must lie between the minimum and maximum of the class rows).

#### Worked example

An AIRB residential-mortgage book (the firm's only IRB class), total sheet eba_GA:x1: exposure value 100,000,000 of which 5,000,000 defaulted; LGD 12% on the non-defaulted exposures and LGD in default 30%. Col 0090 = (95,000,000 x 12% + 5,000,000 x 30%) / 100,000,000 = 12.9%; col 0100 = 30%. Rows 0072 (retail secured by residential immovable property, non-SME), 0060 (retail) and 0150 (total) all report 0.129 / 0.3 with exposure value 100,000,000 / 5,000,000. Arelle: boe_b0346 unsatisfied on all three rows. In a mixed book the FIRB corporate rows, where defaulted and performing exposures both carry the 40% supervisory LGD, pass and the retail and total rows fail: boe_b0346 [2, 3].

Arelle's result on it:

| Rule | Satisfied | Unsatisfied | What the example shows |
|---|---|---|---|
| boe_b0346 | 0 | 3 | fails |
| boe_b0349 | 3 | 0 | holds |
| boe_b0668 | 2 | 0 | - |
| boe_b0682 | 2 | 0 | - |
| boe_b1049 | 6 | 0 | - |

<summary>The example's 12 cells</summary>

| Table | Sheet | Key | Row | Column | Value |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| OF09.02.01.01 |  | x1 | 0072 | 0090 | 0.129 |
| OF09.02.01.01 |  | x1 | 0072 | 0100 | 0.3 |
| OF09.02.01.01 |  | x1 | 0072 | 0105 | 100,000,000 |
| OF09.02.01.01 |  | x1 | 0072 | 0107 | 5,000,000 |
| OF09.02.01.01 |  | x1 | 0060 | 0090 | 0.129 |
| OF09.02.01.01 |  | x1 | 0060 | 0100 | 0.3 |
| OF09.02.01.01 |  | x1 | 0060 | 0105 | 100,000,000 |
| OF09.02.01.01 |  | x1 | 0060 | 0107 | 5,000,000 |
| OF09.02.01.01 |  | x1 | 0150 | 0090 | 0.129 |
| OF09.02.01.01 |  | x1 | 0150 | 0100 | 0.3 |
| OF09.02.01.01 |  | x1 | 0150 | 0105 | 100,000,000 |
| OF09.02.01.01 |  | x1 | 0150 | 0107 | 5,000,000 |

</details>

#### Other ways of reporting considered

(a) Leave col 0100 empty: the rule passes on the default of 0 but the firm has not reported a required figure. (b) Read col 0100 as the defaulted exposures' contribution to the overall average (sum over defaulted of EV x LGD, divided by total EV), which would always be <= col 0090: not a credible reading - the instruction says 'Exposure weighted LGD for those exposures which have been classified as defaulted', and the data point is the average-LGD metric restricted to defaulted exposures, exactly as cols 0230/0240 of OF 08.01 are defined. No compliant alternative.

#### Proposed change

Deactivate boe_b0346. The two columns are already bounded as averages by boe_b1049 (each between 0 and 1) and boe_b0668 / boe_b0682 (total row between the class rows' minimum and maximum). No inequality between col 0090 and col 0100 holds in either direction.

#### EBA precedent

None. The EBA rule list has no C 09.02 rule comparing col 0090 with col 0100 (its live of-which rules on C 09.02 are v4783_m, col 0110 >= col 0120, and v4784_m, col 0010 >= col 0030); the v4.0.0 Bank workbook gives boe_b0346 no EBA equivalent. It is a Bank-origin rule.

#### Who is affected

Any IRB firm whose defaulted exposures in a class (or in total) carry an average LGD above the class average - common in AIRB retail books with defaults (wherever a row's defaulted exposure-weighted LGD exceeds the row's overall average), and in mixed books on aggregate rows, where defaulted AIRB retail LGD is averaged with performing FIRB corporates, where the defaulted exposures are concentrated in a higher-LGD class. FIRB-only corporate books pass unless the mix differs. WARNING severity, every OF 09.02 country sheet, from the first PS1/26 return.

#### What a firm can do meanwhile

Report the figures the instructions require; do not change correct figures to satisfy the rule. A Warning-severity break does not stop the submission: explain it when you submit, citing this issue.

### PI-27 - boe_b0908: exposure value must be at least RWEA

**Status:** identified by rwa-filer, not yet raised with the Bank of England.

**Severity:** WARNING (boe_b0908).

**Effect:** a return that follows the reporting instructions fails it. **Cause:** states as a rule what holds only as a tendency.

#### The rules

| Rule | Module | Severity | Part in the issue | Where the issue applies | At the gateway |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| boe_b0908 | PRA001 | WARNING | the rule at issue | every evaluation | run as published |
| boe_b0347 | PRA001 | WARNING | holds on the example (control) | - | run as published |
| boe_b0349 | PRA001 | WARNING | holds on the example (control) | - | run as published |

boe_b0908, as published in taxonomy 4.1.1 (label: "Exposure value should exceed Risk-weighted exposure amount|"):

```text
{t: OF09.02.01.01, c: 0105, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v0, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} >= {t: OF09.02.01.01, c: 0110, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v1, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting}
scope({t: OF09.02.01.01, r:0020;0030;0042;0045;0048;0049;0050;0055;0060;0071;0072;0073;0074;0100;0105;0120;0130;0150, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting})
```

#### What the rule requires

On 18 class rows of every OF 09.02 country sheet, exposure value (col 0105) must be greater than or equal to the risk-weighted exposure amount (col 0110), i.e. the row's average risk weight must not exceed 100%. Label: 'Exposure value should exceed Risk-weighted exposure amount'.

#### What the instructions and rules say

> IPRE exposures 50% 70% 70% 90% 115% 250% 0%
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Appendix 1: the PRA Rulebook instruments (Basel 3.1), Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part, Article 153(5) Table A (slotting; row 0045 of OF 09.02 is in the rule's scope): risk weights for IPRE, in the order Strong A, Strong B, Good C, Good D, Satisfactory, Weak, Default, PDF page 103

> where an institution uses the Advanced IRB Approach, RW shall be: RW = max (0, 12.5 ∙(LGD −BEEL))
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Appendix 1: the PRA Rulebook instruments (Basel 3.1), Article 153(1)(b), PDF page 101

> Same definition as for column 0110 of OF CR IRB template.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 09.02 col 0105, PDF page 142

> Data regarding ‘exposure value’ and ‘Risk-weighted exposure amounts’ shall be reported as of the country of residence of the ultimate obligor.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, paragraph 87 (the only Annex II text on OF 09.02's RWEA columns: the column table on p.142-143 goes from 0107 to 0130 with no entry for 0110 or 0120), PDF page 136

#### Why a correct return fails

RWEA = RW x exposure value, and nothing in the IRB approach caps RW at 100%. The slotting table assigns 115% to 'Satisfactory' and 250% to 'Weak' specialised lending (140% / 250% for HVCRE); the Art. 153(1)(c) formula gives a senior unsecured FIRB corporate exposure (LGD 40%, M 2.5) a risk weight of 102.1% at PD 2% and 114.2% at PD 3%; an AIRB defaulted exposure is weighted 12.5 x (LGD - BEEL), above 100% as soon as the gap exceeds 8 percentage points. Any row whose exposure-weighted risk weight is above 100% has col 0110 > col 0105.

#### Worked example

A slotting book reported on the total sheet eba_GA:x1: income-producing real estate, exposure value 10,000,000, every exposure graded 'Satisfactory' (115%), so RWEA = 11,500,000. Rows 0045 (specialised lending under the slotting approach), 0030 (corporates) and 0150 (total) each report col 0105 = 10,000,000 and col 0110 = 11,500,000. No model figure is involved - the 115% is the rule's own table. Arelle: boe_b0908 unsatisfied on all three rows. In a mixed book (the slotting book above, FIRB other general corporates on row 0055 with exposure value 20,000,000, of which 1,000,000 defaulted and weighted 0 under FIRB (Art. 153(1)(b)), RWEA 21,691,708 = 19,000,000 x 114.17%, plus AIRB residential mortgages), boe_b0908 is [3, 3]: rows 0045, 0055 and 0030 fail; the retail and total rows pass.

Arelle's result on it:

| Rule | Satisfied | Unsatisfied | What the example shows |
|---|---|---|---|
| boe_b0341 | 2 | 0 | - |
| boe_b0347 | 3 | 0 | holds |
| boe_b0349 | 3 | 0 | holds |
| boe_b0785 | 2 | 0 | - |
| boe_b0786 | 2 | 0 | - |
| boe_b0908 | 0 | 3 | fails |

#### Other ways of reporting considered

None exists: both columns are single, unambiguous amounts (exposure value and RWEA of the row) and no instruction, grey cell, default or precondition changes either. The rule can only be met by a book whose average risk weight is at or below 100%.

#### Proposed change

Deactivate boe_b0908, as the EBA did with its original v4786_m on 10 December 2020. If a ceiling is wanted, use the 1,250% maximum risk weight rather than 100%, at WARNING severity: {t: OF09.02.01.01, c: 0110, dv: 0} <= 12.5 * {t: OF09.02.01.01, c: 0105, dv: 0}. One caveat: Annex II does not say whether OF 09.02 column 0110 is before or after the RWEA adjustments of OF 08.01 columns 0252-0254 (post-model adjustments, mortgage floor, unrecognised exposure adjustment); if after, a row with little exposure value could exceed 12.5 times it. Separately, Annex II has no entry for OF 09.02 cols 0110 and 0120 (p.142-143); ask the Bank to restore them.

#### EBA precedent

boe_b0908 restates EBA v4786_m ({c0105} >= {c0110} on C 09.02, WARNING). The EBA validation rules list shows it 'Deactivated on 2020-12-10' in every sheet from v2.8 to 3.5 (the v2.6 sheet shows an earlier deactivation on 2017-12-08; it is listed live again in the v2.7.0.1 sheet). The EBA's v4786_m row scope had no slotting row; the Bank's adds row 0045, where the slotting weights of 115%, 140% and 250% make the failure certain. Note: the v4.0.0 Bank workbook also puts the label 'v4786_m' on boe_b0349 and boe_b0350, but neither restates it - v4786_m is the exposure-value-versus-RWEA check only.

#### Who is affected

Every IRB firm with a class or country row whose average risk weight exceeds 100%: slotting books weighted to 'Satisfactory' / 'Weak' (row 0045 and, through it, row 0030), corporate and SME books with PDs of about 2% and above, AIRB defaulted exposures with LGD well above BEEL, and small country sheets holding one or two higher-risk obligors. WARNING severity, from the first PS1/26 return.

#### What a firm can do meanwhile

Report the figures the instructions require; do not change correct figures to satisfy the rule. A Warning-severity break does not stop the submission: explain it when you submit, citing this issue.

### PI-28 - boe_b0350: OF 09.01 defaulted-exposures column treated as a subset of the row's original exposure

**Status:** identified by rwa-filer, not yet raised with the Bank of England.

**Severity:** WARNING (boe_b0350).

**Effect:** a return that follows the reporting instructions fails it. **Cause:** contradicts the reporting instructions; conflicts with another published rule.

#### The rules

| Rule | Module | Severity | Part in the issue | Where the issue applies | At the gateway |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| boe_b0350 | PRA001 | WARNING | the rule at issue | every evaluation | run as published |
| boe_b0730 | PRA001 | ERROR | cannot hold together with it | - | run as published |
| boe_b0729 | PRA001 | ERROR | cannot hold together with it | - | run as published |
| boe_b0263 | PRA001 | WARNING | cannot hold together with it | - | run as published |
| boe_b0237 | PRA001 | WARNING | cannot hold together with it | - | run as published |
| boe_b0987 | PRA001 | WARNING | cannot hold together with it | - | run as published |
| boe_b0348 | PRA001 | WARNING | related | - | run as published |
| boe_b0349 | PRA001 | WARNING | related | - | run as published |
| boe_b0262 | PRA001 | ERROR | holds on the example (control) | - | run as published |
| boe_b0222 | PRA001 | WARNING | related | - | run as published |

boe_b0350, as published in taxonomy 4.1.1 (label: "Original Exposures pre-CFs for the relevant IRB exposure class shall exceed Defaulted Exposures|"):

```text
{t: OF09.01.01.01, c: 0010, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v0, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i>= {t: OF09.01.01.01, c: 0020, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v1, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting}
scope({t: OF09.01.01.01, r:0010;0020;0030;0040;0050;0060;0070;0071;0072;0073;0075;0080;0085;0090;0091;0092;0093;0094;0095;0100;0110;0120;0140;0141;0142;0143;0150;0160;0170, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting})
```

#### What the rule requires

On 29 rows of every OF 09.01 country sheet (the standardised-approach geographical breakdown: every exposure class, every of-which row and the total), original exposure pre-conversion factors (column 0010) must be at least 'defaulted exposures' (column 0020). A cell that is not reported is read as 0. Label: 'Original Exposures pre-CFs for the relevant IRB exposure class shall exceed Defaulted Exposures' (the template is the standardised one).

#### What the instructions and rules say

> Original exposure pre-conversion factors for those exposures which have been classified as “exposures in default” and for defaulted exposures assigned to the exposure classes “exposures associated with particularly high risk” or “subordinated debt, equity and other own funds instruments”.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 09.01 col 0020 'Defaulted exposures' (heading on p.136), PDF page 137

> This column shall provide additional information about the obligor structure of defaulted exposures. Exposures classified as “exposures in default” as referred to in Article 112(1)(j) of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part shall be reported where the obligors would have been reported if those exposures were not assigned to the exposure classes 'exposures in default'.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, second paragraph, PDF page 137

> Where an exposure meets the criteria for more than one exposure class it shall be assigned to the exposure class that has the highest position in Table A2.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Appendix 1: the PRA Rulebook instruments (Basel 3.1), Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part, Article 112(2); Table A2 puts 'Exposures in default' at position (5), above covered bonds (6), real estate (7), institutions (10), retail (14) and corporates (15), and below CIUs (2), subordinated debt/equity (3) and high risk (4) (p.33-34), PDF page 33

> Same definition as for column 0010 of OF CR SA template
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 09.01 column 0010, PDF page 136

> Article 112(1)(j) of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 09.01 row 0100 (Exposures in default), PDF page 140

> the part of any item or facility which is not secured by recognised collateral or covered by recognised unfunded credit protection and is a defaulted exposure shall be assigned a risk weight of:
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Appendix 1: the PRA Rulebook instruments (Basel 3.1), Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part, Article 127(1), PDF page 59

#### Why a correct return fails

Under Art. 112(2) and Table A2 a defaulted corporate, retail, real estate, institution or sovereign exposure belongs to the class 'exposures in default' (position (5), above every class it can come from; Article 127 weights every defaulted exposure): its original exposure is in row 0100 column 0010, not in the row of the class it came from. Column 0020 then shows it, as a memorandum item, against the class 'where the obligors would have been reported' (p.137). So on those class rows column 0010 is the non-defaulted book and column 0020 the defaulted book of that kind of obligor - two disjoint populations, not a total and its part. The rule fails on any row, on any country sheet, whose exposures are mostly or wholly in default: one defaulted obligor in a country, a run-off sub-portfolio, a single project-finance loan or the firm's only land acquisition, development and construction loan in default (row 0094: column 0010 empty, read as 0, against column 0020 of 2,000,000). The identity is genuine only where defaulted exposures stay in their own class - rows 0110 (high risk), 0140-0143 (CIUs) and 0150 (subordinated debt and equity) - and on the total row 0170; on row 0100 column 0020 is not a cell at all. That is 21 rows where the rule is not an identity, 7 where it is, and 1 where it is trivial.

The Bank's own rules read the template this way: boe_b0730 adds row 0100 into the column 0010 total, boe_b0729 leaves row 0100 out of the column 0020 total, boe_b0263 ties the column 0020 total (less high risk, equity and CIUs) to the OF 07.00 'exposures in default' sheet 'in accordance with exposure class hierarchy in Article 112', and boe_b0237 ties row 0100 column 0010 to the same sheet; all of them pass on the return that fails boe_b0350. The counter-argument the Bank may raise is the taxonomy: OF 09.01 column 0020 on each class row has the same metric (eba_met:mi180) and the same exposure-class member as column 0010, plus eba_dim:IMS = eba_IM:x3, so the data model encodes column 0020 as an 'of which' of column 0010 - probably why the rule was written. The reply is Annex II p.137, Art. 112(2) with Table A2, Article 127 and the Bank's own boe_b0222, boe_b0730 and boe_b0263; the exposure-class membership of column 0020 may itself be worth correcting in the data model. The label says 'IRB exposure class' on a standardised template; the IRB siblings boe_b0348 and boe_b0349 are correct, because in OF 09.02 a defaulted exposure stays in its class.

#### Worked example

An SA firm above the Article 5(5) threshold reports the total sheet (x1), GB and FR. GB: corporates, non-defaulted 40,000,000; one project-finance loan in default, 2,000,000. FR: institutions, non-defaulted 8,000,000; one corporate obligor in default, 500,000. Reported: total sheet r0070 (corporates) c0010 40,000,000 / c0020 2,500,000; r0073 (of which project finance) c0020 2,000,000 and no c0010; r0100 (exposures in default) c0010 2,500,000; r0170 c0010 50,500,000 / c0020 2,500,000; the country sheets likewise (FR r0070: c0020 500,000, no c0010); and the OF 07.00 original exposures the Bank's cross-template rules tie to (sheet 0001 50,500,000; 0007 8,000,000; 0008 40,000,000; 0011 2,500,000). Arelle: boe_b0350 [10, 3] - unsatisfied on x1 r0073, GB r0073 and FR r0070 - with boe_b0729, boe_b0730, boe_b0263, boe_b0237, boe_b0222, boe_b0258, boe_b0262 and boe_b0904 all satisfied.

Arelle's result on it:

|---|---|---|---|
| boe_b0222 | 1 | 0 | - |
| boe_b0237 | 1 | 0 | - |
| boe_b0258 | 1 | 0 | - |
| boe_b0262 | 1 | 0 | holds |
| boe_b0263 | 1 | 0 | - |
| boe_b0350 | 10 | 3 | fails |
| boe_b0604 | 5 | 0 | - |
| boe_b0605 | 5 | 0 | - |
| boe_b0606 | 5 | 0 | - |
| boe_b0674 | 15 | 0 | - |
| boe_b0729 | 3 | 0 | - |
| boe_b0730 | 3 | 0 | - |
| boe_b0904 | 2 | 0 | - |
| boe_b0976 | 0 | 0 | - |

#### Other ways of reporting considered

(1) Report the defaulted exposure in its original class row's column 0010 as well as in row 0100: boe_b0350 then passes, but the exposure is counted twice, which breaks the Bank's ERROR rule boe_b0730 and the ties to OF 07.00 and contradicts Art. 112(2). For the real-estate case the extra figure in row 0094 column 0010 also breaks boe_b0987, which ties that cell to OF 07.00 sheet 0010 row 0360 (whose published label, 'regulatory commercial real estate', does not match its expression, the ADC row; boe_b0978's label likewise mismatches its expression), and if row 0090 is then made the sum of rows 0091-0094 as Annex II p.140 requires, boe_b0234 fails too. (2) Leave column 0020 empty on the class rows and report it only on the total: contradicts the instruction that the amount 'shall be reported where the obligors would have been reported', and by their expressions breaks boe_b0729 or boe_b0262 / boe_b0263. (3) Report an explicit 0 in column 0010: the comparison is the same. No compliant alternative.

#### Proposed change

Restrict boe_b0350 to the rows where column 0020 is a part of column 0010: scope({t: OF09.01.01.01, r:0110;0140;0141;0142;0143;0150;0170}), and correct the label ('IRB exposure class' -> SA exposure class). Or withdraw it: boe_b0262 to boe_b0265 and boe_b0967 already tie column 0020 to OF 07.00. If a check on the other class rows is wanted, the true relation there is that a class's defaulted exposures cannot exceed the country's 'exposures in default' class: {t: OF09.01.01.01, c: 0020, dv: 0} i<= {t: OF09.01.01.01, r: 0100, c: 0010, dv: 0} over r:0010;0020;0030;0040;0050;0060;0070;0071;0072;0073;0075;0080;0085;0090;0091;0092;0093;0094;0095;0120;0160.

#### EBA precedent

None for the rule: the EBA list has no C 09.01 rule comparing column 0010 with column 0020, and its rules on column 0020 treat it as the memorandum (v8727_m: {C 07.00.a, r0010, c0010, s0011} = {C 09.01.b, r0170, c0020, x1} - {r0110, c0020} - {r0150, c0020}; and v6404_m, both live in the 3.5 sheet). The v4.0.0 Bank workbook labels boe_b0350 (and boe_b0349) 'v4786_m', which is a different check on a different template (C 09.02 column 0105 >= column 0110, deactivated by the EBA on 10 December 2020). The rule looks like the IRB of-which pattern (EBA v4784_m, C 09.02 column 0010 >= column 0030, live and valid, because under IRB a defaulted exposure stays in its class) carried over to the standardised template, where it does not hold.

#### Who is affected

Any standardised-approach firm with a class, of-which row or country whose defaulted original exposure exceeds its non-defaulted original exposure - typical of country sheets with one or two obligors, narrow of-which rows (specialised lending, land acquisition, development and construction, SME) and run-off books. WARNING severity, from the first PS1/26 OF 09.01 return.

#### What a firm can do meanwhile

Report the figures the instructions require; do not change correct figures to satisfy the rule. A Warning-severity break does not stop the submission: explain it when you submit, citing this issue.

### PI-29 - Annex II has no instruction for OF 08.01 column 0010 (PD), which boe_b0356 requires

**Status:** identified by rwa-filer, not yet raised with the Bank of England.

**Severity:** WARNING (boe_b0356).

**Effect:** a return that follows the reporting instructions fails it. **Cause:** the instructions leave a gap; conflicts with the template.

#### The rules

| Rule | Module | Severity | Part in the issue | Where the issue applies | At the gateway |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| boe_b0356 | PRA001 | WARNING | the rule at issue | every evaluation | run as published |
| boe_b0410 | PRA001 | WARNING | holds on the example (control) | - | run as published |
| boe_b0749 | PRA001 | ERROR | holds on the example (control) | - | run as published |

boe_b0356, as published in taxonomy 4.1.1 (label: "PD floor for these exposures is 0.05%|"):

```text
if {t: OF08.01.01.01, c: 0110, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v0, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} > 0 then {t: OF08.01.01.01, c: 0010, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v1, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} >= 0.0005 else true()
scope({t: OF08.01.01.01, r:0001;0010;0017;0020;0030;0031;0032;0033;0034;0035;0040;0050;0060;0070;0175;0180;0190;0200,z:0001;0002;0006;0009;0010;0011;0012;0016;0017;0018;0019;0020;0021;0022;0023;0024, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting})
```

#### What the rule requires

On 18 rows of 16 sheets of OF 08.01, wherever exposure value (c0110) is positive, the PD in c0010 must be at least 0.05%; a PD that is not reported is read as 0 (dv: 0) and fails. The sheets include 0002 (Total FIRB and slotting) and 0010 (Specialised lending, FIRB or slotting); the rows include 0010 Total, 0020 on-balance-sheet and 0030 off-balance-sheet, but not 0080 (slotting total).

#### What the instructions and rules say

> Columns Instructions 0020 ORIGINAL EXPOSURE PRE-CONVERSION FACTORS Institutions shall report the exposure value before taking into account any value adjustments, provisions, effects due to credit risk mitigation techniques or credit conversion factors.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, first entry of the OF 08.01 column table, PDF page 102

> 0010-0300 Instructions for each of these columns are the same as for the corresponding numbered columns in OF CR IRB 1 template.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 08.02 columns, PDF page 118

> INTERNAL RATING SCALE/ PD ASSIGNED TO THE OBLIGOR GRADE OR POOL (%) Same definition as for column 0010 of OF CR IRB 1 template.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 09.02 column 0080, PDF page 142

> INTERNAL RATING SCALE | PD ASSIGNED TO THE OBLIGOR GRADE OR POOL (%) | 0010
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex I: the reporting templates, linked from ps126app17.pdf p.2)

> SPECIALISED LENDING SLOTTING APPROACH: TOTAL Exposures subject to the slotting approach. This shall only apply to the exposure sub-class ‘corporate – specialised lending’.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 08.01 row 0080, PDF page 117

> For figures corresponding to an aggregation of obligor grades or pools (e.g. total exposures), the exposure weighted average of the PDs assigned to the obligor grades or pools included in the aggregation shall be provided. The exposure value (column 0110) shall be used for the calculation of the exposure-weighted average PD.
>
> - CRR COREP Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, C 08.01 column 0010 (the instruction PS1/26 did not carry over), PDF page 98

#### Why a correct return fails

Two separate things. (1) Documentation: the Annex II column table for OF 08.01 begins at 0020 (p.102). Column 0010 exists - in the Annex I template (code 0010, 'PD assigned to the obligor grade or pool (%)', greyed only on rows 0080 and 0170) and in the taxonomy (eba_met:pi187, 306 cells on all 17 sheets, rows 0080 and 0170 not reportable) - and two other instructions (pp.118, 142) define their own PD column by reference to it. Nothing says what it holds on an aggregate row, how it is weighted, or whether it is before or after the PD input floor. (2) Rule: a firm that slots all of its specialised lending reports sheet 0010 with exposure value on rows 0010, 0020 and 0030, which are open for c0010 in template and taxonomy; a slotted exposure has a category, not a PD, so there is nothing to average and c0010 stays empty. boe_b0356 reads the empty PD as 0 and fires on each such row. The taxonomy itself greys the PD on the slotting row 0080, but the rule's scope takes the sheet's total rows.

#### Worked example

A firm with 1,000,000 of specialised lending, all on the slotting approach (sheet 0010: rows 0010, 0020 and 0080 each 1,000,000 exposure value, RWEA 700,000, no PD), and 500,000 of FIRB general corporates at PD 1.2% (sheet 0012). Total FIRB-and-slotting sheet 0002: exposure value 1,500,000, PD 1.2% (the average over the PD-rated part). boe_b0356 fails on sheet 0010's rows 0010 and 0020 and holds wherever a PD is reported.

Arelle's result on it:

| Rule | Satisfied | Unsatisfied | What the example shows |
|---|---|---|---|
| boe_b0356 | 4 | 2 | fails |
| boe_b0410 | 4 | 0 | holds |
| boe_b0749 | 3 | 0 | holds |

</details>

#### Other ways of reporting considered

Report a PD on the slotting-only rows: there is none - Annex II gives no instruction, the CRR text it replaced averages 'the PDs assigned to the obligor grades or pools included', and none is included. Report the exposure only on row 0080: row 0010 is the sheet total and must include it. Row 0080 itself is outside the rule and greyed for c0010. A sheet that mixes FIRB and slotted specialised lending passes (the PD is the average of the rated part), as does sheet 0002 whenever any FIRB exposure exists.

#### Proposed change

(1) Annex II: restore an instruction for OF 08.01 column 0010 - what is reported on aggregate rows (exposure-weighted average, weight c0110), whether it is the PD before or after the input floor, and that it is left blank where no exposure on the row has a PD (slotting). (2) boe_b0356: do not evaluate the total rows of the two sheets that contain slotting - for z:0002;0010 restrict the scope to r:0070 (exposures assigned to obligor grades or pools), keep the present rows on the other 14 sheets; or drop 'dv: 0' from the c0010 reference so that an unreported PD is not read as 0, as in the EBA original.

#### EBA precedent

The v4.0.0 workbook names the EBA original: v10670_m, 'if {c0110} > 0 then {c0010} >= 0.0003' on C 08.02 (the obligor-grade template, which holds no slotting), severity Warning, 'If value missing: do not run rule'. The Bank moved the check to OF 08.01, added total rows and the FIRB-or-slotting sheets, and treats a missing PD as zero.

#### Who is affected

Instruction gap: every IRB firm. Rule: any firm whose sheet 0010 carries only slotted exposure on a row in scope, every period, at WARNING (does not block).

#### What a firm can do meanwhile

Report the figures the instructions require; do not change correct figures to satisfy the rule. A Warning-severity break does not stop the submission: explain it when you submit, citing this issue.

### PI-31 - boe_b0748 sums average maturity (c0250) and obligor counts (c0300) across the AIRB class sheets

**Status:** identified by rwa-filer, not yet raised with the Bank of England.

**Severity:** ERROR (boe_b0748).

**Effect:** a return that follows the reporting instructions fails it. **Cause:** contradicts the reporting instructions; conflicts with another published rule.

#### The rules

| Rule | Module | Severity | Part in the issue | Where the issue applies | At the gateway |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| boe_b0748 | PRA001 | ERROR | the rule at issue | OF08.01.01.01 columns 0250, 0300 (a break there may also be the return's own) | run as published |
| boe_b0749 | PRA001 | ERROR | holds on the example (control) | - | run as published |

boe_b0748, as published in taxonomy 4.1.1 (label: "Total Exposures in 'Total AIRB' sheet should equal the sum of the individual exposure classes in each AIRB sheets for the columns listed|"):

```text
{t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0010, z: 0001, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v0, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i= {t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0010, z: 0009, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v1, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i+ {t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0010, z: 0023, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v2, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i+ {t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0010, z: 0011, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v3, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i+ {t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0010, z: 0020, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v4, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i+ {t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0010, z: 0021, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v5, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i+ {t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0010, z: 0018, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v6, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i+ {t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0010, z: 0019, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v7, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i+ {t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0010, z: 0015, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v8, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i+ {t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0010, z: 0016, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v9, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i+ {t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0010, z: 0017, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v10, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting}
scope({t: OF08.01.01.01, c:0020;0030;0035;0040;0050;0060;0070;0080;0090;0101;0102;0103;0104;0110;0125;0140;0150;0160;0170;0171;0172;0173;0180;0190;0200;0210;0250;0251;0252;0253;0254;0260;0265;0270;0275;0276;0280;0281;0282;0290;0300;0310, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting})
```

#### What the rule requires

**Average maturity, column 0250.** For each of 42 columns, row 0010 of the Total AIRB sheet (0001) must equal the sum of row 0010 over the ten AIRB class sheets (0009, 0011, 0015-0021, 0023). The column list includes 0250, the exposure-weighted average maturity in days. A sheet that does not report the column counts as 0.

**Number of obligors, column 0300: a question.** Row 0010 c0300 of the Total AIRB sheet must equal the sum of row 0010 c0300 over the ten AIRB class sheets.

#### What the instructions and rules say

> The exposure value (column 0110) shall be used for the calculation of the exposure-weighted averages. The average maturity shall be reported in days. This data shall not be reported for the exposure values for which the maturity is not an element in the calculation of risk-weighted exposure amounts. This column shall therefore not be filled in for the exposure class ‘retail’ or for exposures subject to the slotting approach.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 08.01 column 0250, PDF page 111

> The templates OF CR IRB 1, OF CR IRB 2, OF CR IRB 3 and OF CR IRB 5 shall be reported separately for the following exposure and sub-exposure classes: 1) Total (The Total template must be reported for the FIRB and the slotting approaches and, separately for the AIRB approach.)
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, para 76, PDF page 99

> v4769_m: The rule requires that the total of all exposure classes equals the sum of the exposure classes for template C08.01. However it is incorrectly applied to columns that contain exposure-weighted non-monetary values (c0230-0240: %s, c0250: days), which cannot be aggregated.
>
> - EBA Single Rulebook Q&A, submitted 23/04/2026

> This question has been rejected because the matter it refers to has already been identified and will be considered for a forthcoming version of the Reporting framework / release of the respective validation rules.
>
> - EBA Single Rulebook Q&A, published 15/10/2026

> (0020;0030;0040;0050;0060;0070;0080;0090;0110;0140;0150;0160;0170;0180;0190;0200;0210;0220;0255;0260;0270;0280;0290)
>
> - EBA validation rules (list of 10 June 2026, up to framework 3.5), sheets v3.0 to 3.5  - v4769_m, column 'columns'

> For all exposure classes, with the exception of the exposure class ‘retail’ and, for other exposures classes, the cases mentioned in the second sentence of Article 172(1)(e) of the Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part, the institution shall report the number of legal entities/obligors which were separately rated, regardless of the number of different loans or exposures granted.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 08.01 column 0300, PDF page 114

> Within the exposure class ‘retail’, or if separate exposures to the same obligor are assigned to different obligor grades in accordance with the second sentence of Article 172(1)(e) of the Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part in other exposure classes, the institution shall report the number of exposures which were separately assigned to a certain rating grade or pool.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 08.01 column 0300, PDF page 114

#### Why a correct return fails

**Average maturity, column 0250.** The Total sheet is a sheet like any other, so its c0250 is the exposure-weighted average over the AIRB exposures for which maturity enters the risk weight. With class sheets A and B: M_total = (EAD_A x M_A + EAD_B x M_B) / (EAD_A + EAD_B), which lies between M_A and M_B; the rule demands M_total = M_A + M_B. The two agree only when at most one AIRB class sheet reports a maturity. Retail sheets report none (p.111), so the sheets that matter are 0009, 0011 and 0023: an AIRB firm with both SME and non-SME general corporates fails.

**Number of obligors, column 0300: a question.** Is OF 08.01 column 0300 on the AIRB Total sheet the sum of the class sheets, or a count of distinct legal entities? Mostly the two agree. Retail sheets count EXPOSURES (p.114), which add up; non-retail sheets count legal entities, and SME / non-SME is a property of the obligor, so an entity is normally on one corporate sheet. The sum differs from the Total only when one legal entity is counted on two AIRB non-retail sheets (a hypothetical case such as a corporate with a general facility and an exposure classed as specialised lending; Article 147(4B) makes a specialised-lending obligor an entity with few or no other activities, so such overlaps should be rare) - the Total counts it once. Even then the interval arithmetic absorbs small differences: each integer fact carries +/-0.5, so with two class sheets a difference of 1 is satisfied and a difference of 2 is not (tested). It is not shown that this is a common position; what is certain is that the Bank's FIRB twin boe_b0749 and the EBA's v4769_m (frameworks 3.0-3.5) both leave 0300 out.

#### Worked example

AIRB general corporates: non-SME book (sheet 0011) exposure value 1,000,000, average maturity 900 days; SME book (sheet 0023) exposure value 1,000,000, average maturity 1,100 days. Total AIRB sheet 0001: exposure value 2,000,000, average maturity (1,000,000 x 900 + 1,000,000 x 1,100) / 2,000,000 = 1,000 days, 30 obligors (10 + 20). The same figures are filed on the FIRB side (sheets 0012, 0024, total 0002) as the control. Rows 0017 / 0035 on the two AIRB sheets carry the figures of PI-32.

Arelle's result on it:

| Rule | Satisfied | Unsatisfied | What the example shows |
|---|---|---|---|
| boe_b0355 | 3 | 1 | - |
| boe_b0748 | 3 | 1 | fails |
| boe_b0749 | 2 | 0 | holds |

#### Other ways of reporting considered

**Average maturity, column 0250.** Report the sum (2,000 days) on the Total sheet: not an average, and not what p.111 defines. Leave the Total sheet's c0250 empty: read as 0, still unequal to 900 + 1,100. Leave the class sheets empty: contrary to p.111 for corporate exposures. There is no compliant way once two AIRB non-retail sheets carry a maturity.

**Number of obligors, column 0300: a question.** Report the Total as the plain sum of the class sheets (counting a shared entity twice): satisfies the rule, and p.114 does not say explicitly that the Total sheet de-duplicates across classes - so a firm has a defensible way to pass. That is why this part is put as a question.

#### Proposed change

**Average maturity, column 0250.** Remove 0250 (and, depending on the answer to the question below, 0300) from the scope of boe_b0748 (new scope with both 0250 and 0300 removed: c:0020;0030;0035;0040;0050;0060;0070;0080;0090;0101;0102;0103;0104;0110;0125;0140;0150;0160;0170;0171;0172;0173;0180;0190;0200;0210;0251;0252;0253;0254;0260;0265;0270;0275;0276;0280;0281;0282;0290;0310; if the answer on 0300 is 'sum', keep 0300), leaving out 0250 and 0300, as boe_b0749 does.

**Number of obligors, column 0300: a question.** Remove 0300 from boe_b0748's scope together with 0250 (so that it matches boe_b0749), or state in Annex II that the Total sheet's number of obligors is the sum of the class sheets.

#### EBA precedent

**Average maturity, column 0250.** The v4.0.0 workbook names v4769_m as the original. In the EBA rule lists for frameworks 3.0-3.5 its columns exclude 0230, 0240, 0250, 0300 and 0310; the Bank's list adds 0250 and 0300 (and the additive 0310). EBA Q&A 2026_7840 reports that the DPM 4.2 version of v4769_m does reach c0230-0250 and calls that incorrect; the EBA rejected the question only because the matter 'has already been identified and will be considered for a forthcoming version'.

**Number of obligors, column 0300: a question.** v4769_m (EBA frameworks 3.0-3.5) omits column 0300. Related counts problems (OF 34.07 / OF 08.03 obligor counts summed or subtracted) are reported under other findings.

#### Who is affected

**Average maturity, column 0250.** Any AIRB firm that reports an average maturity on two or more of sheets 0009, 0011 and 0023 - typically any AIRB lender with both SME and non-SME general corporates - every period, at ERROR (the return is rejected).

**Number of obligors, column 0300: a question.** Only an AIRB firm with at least two legal entities rated on two AIRB non-retail sheets, and only if it de-duplicates the Total. ERROR severity.

#### What a firm can do meanwhile

Report the figures the instructions require; do not change correct figures to satisfy the rule. An Error-severity break blocks the submission at the gateway: if the gateway rejects the return on this rule, raise it with the PRA, citing this issue.

### PI-32 - boe_b0355 applies a subset inequality to average maturity (c0250)

**Status:** identified by rwa-filer, not yet raised with the Bank of England.

**Severity:** WARNING (boe_b0355).

**Effect:** a return that follows the reporting instructions fails it. **Cause:** states as a rule what holds only as a tendency.

#### The rules

| Rule | Module | Severity | Part in the issue | Where the issue applies | At the gateway |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| boe_b0355 | PRA001 | WARNING | the rule at issue | OF08.01.01.01 columns 0250 | run as published |

boe_b0355, as published in taxonomy 4.1.1 (label: "only conversion factors for exposures to revolving commitments should be modelled|"):

```text
iabs({t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0017, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v0, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting}) i>= iabs({t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0035, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v1, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting})
scope({t: OF08.01.01.01, c:0020;0030;0035;0040;0050;0060;0070;0080;0090;0101;0102;0103;0104;0110;0125;0140;0150;0160;0170;0171;0172;0173;0180;0190;0200;0210;0250;0251;0252;0253;0254;0260;0265;0270;0275;0276;0280;0281;0282;0290;0300;0310,z:0001;0002;0006;0009;0010;0011;0012;0015;0016;0017;0018;0019;0020;0021;0022;0023;0024, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting})
```

#### What the rule requires

On every sheet of OF 08.01, for each of 42 columns, the absolute value on row 0017 (exposures to revolving loan commitments) must be at least the absolute value on row 0035 (off-balance-sheet items with an own-estimate conversion factor). The label is 'only conversion factors for exposures to revolving commitments should be modelled'. The column list is the same one boe_b0748 uses and includes 0250 (average maturity, days); it leaves out the other averages (0010 PD, 0230 / 0240 LGD).

#### What the instructions and rules say

> (a) for revolving loan commitments which would not be subject to a 100% conversion factor under Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part Article 111: an own estimate of conversion factor that the institution shall provide in accordance with Section 6; (b) for all other off-balance sheet items: the conversion factor that would be applicable to the off-balance sheet item under the Standardised Approach, as set out in Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part Article 111.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Appendix 1: the PRA Rulebook instruments (Basel 3.1), Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part, Article 166D(1), PDF page 119

> For exposures subject to the AIRB approach for which conversion factors are estimated, or where EADs are estimated directly, institutions shall report values in row 0035.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 08.01 rows 0031, 0032, 0001, 0033, 0035, PDF page 116

> The exposure value (column 0110) shall be used for the calculation of the exposure-weighted averages. The average maturity shall be reported in days.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 08.01 column 0250, PDF page 111

> it is not possible to establish a relation between the sum of the exposure-weighted average maturity value of the rows 15 and 16 and the row 10.
>
> - EBA Single Rulebook Q&A, EBA Single Rulebook Q&A 2026_7880 (rejected 15/10/2026 as the same matter as 2026_7840)

#### Why a correct return fails

Row 0035 is a subset of row 0017 (Article 166D(1)(a): only revolving commitments are modelled), so for amounts and counts the inequality is an identity. An average is not monotone in the population: the modelled revolvers can have a longer average maturity than all revolvers together. Row 0017 also holds the revolving commitments that are NOT modelled - those that would take a 100% conversion factor, which 166D(1)(a) excludes - so the two rows are genuinely different populations. (Annex II p.115 does not say whether row 0017 includes the drawn part of a revolving facility; the point does not depend on it.) With modelled revolvers at 1,400 days and the rest at 400 days, row 0017 averages 900 and row 0035 is 1,400: 900 >= 1,400 is false.

#### Worked example

AIRB non-SME corporates, sheet 0011. Revolving commitments, exposure value 200,000 (row 0017): half with an own-estimate conversion factor and an average maturity of 1,400 days (row 0035, exposure value 100,000), half taking the standardised factor with 400 days. Row 0017 c0250 = (100,000 x 1,400 + 100,000 x 400) / 200,000 = 900 days; row 0035 c0250 = 1,400 days. Sheet 0023 carries the opposite case (row 0017 1,100 days, row 0035 800 days) as the control.

Arelle's result on it:

| Rule | Satisfied | Unsatisfied | What the example shows |
|---|---|---|---|
| boe_b0355 | 3 | 1 | fails |
| boe_b0748 | 3 | 1 | - |
| boe_b0749 | 2 | 0 | - |

#### Other ways of reporting considered

Leave c0250 empty on row 0035 or row 0017: both cells are open in the Annex I template and the taxonomy and p.111 asks for the average wherever maturity enters the risk weight; an empty row 0017 against a reported row 0035 fails anyway (0 >= 1,400). Retail sheets are unaffected (no maturity). No compliant alternative on a corporate AIRB sheet with a mixed revolving book.

#### Proposed change

Remove 0250 from the scope of boe_b0355, leaving the additive columns and the count 0300.

#### EBA precedent

No EBA equivalent is recorded for boe_b0355 (it is the Bank's own). The Bank's own boe_b0378_1 (ERROR), the subset relation one level up (row 0017 <= row 0010), leaves c0250 out of its scope, which suggests its inclusion in boe_b0355 is an oversight. The same class of defect is before the EBA: Q&A 2026_7840 / 2026_7880 on v903250_h, a row-hierarchy inequality on C 08.01 that reaches c0250 - 'incorrectly applied to columns that contain exposure-weighted non-monetary values (c0230-0240: %s, c0250: days), which cannot be aggregated' - rejected because the matter 'has already been identified and will be considered for a forthcoming version'.

#### Who is affected

AIRB firms with corporate revolving commitments of which only part is modelled, whenever the modelled part has the longer average maturity. WARNING (does not block).

#### What a firm can do meanwhile

Report the figures the instructions require; do not change correct figures to satisfy the rule. A Warning-severity break does not stop the submission: explain it when you submit, citing this issue.

### PI-33 - boe_b0359 accepts 0.55 as an output-floor multiplier, which Article 92 does not give

**Status:** identified by rwa-filer, not yet raised with the Bank of England.

**Severity:** ERROR (boe_b0359).

**Effect:** it accepts figures the rules do not permit. **Cause:** the rule allows more values than the requirement it checks.

#### The rules

| Rule | Module | Severity | Part in the issue | Where the issue applies | At the gateway |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| boe_b0359 | PRA001 | ERROR | the rule at issue | every evaluation | run as published |

boe_b0359, as published in taxonomy 4.1.1 (label: "Output Floor multiplier should be limited to 55, 60, 65, 70, 72.5|"):

```text
({t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0035, c: 0030, seq: False, id: v0, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} = 0.55) or ({t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0035, c: 0030, seq: False, id: v0, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} = 0.60) or ({t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0035, c: 0030, seq: False, id: v0, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} = 0.65) or ({t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0035, c: 0030, seq: False, id: v0, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} = 0.70) or ({t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0035, c: 0030, seq: False, id: v0, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} = 0.725)
```

#### What the rule requires

OF 02.00 row 0035 column 0030 (output floor multiplier, metric boe_met:pi10061, a percentage filed as a fraction) must be exactly one of 0.55, 0.60, 0.65, 0.70, 0.725. Label: 'Output Floor multiplier should be limited to 55, 60, 65, 70, 72.5'.

#### What the instructions and rules say

> TREA = max {U-TREA; x ∙ S-TREA + OF-ADJ}
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Appendix 1: the PRA Rulebook instruments (Basel 3.1), Required Level of Own Funds (CRR) Part, Article 92(2A), PDF page 13

> x= 72.5%;
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Appendix 1: the PRA Rulebook instruments (Basel 3.1), Article 92(2A), definitions (the heading 'Output Floor Adjustments' left out), PDF page 13

> When calculating TREA for the purposes of paragraph 2A(a), an institution or CRR consolidation entity may apply the following factor x during the periods specified below: (a) 60% during the period from 1 January 2027 to 31 December 2027; (b) 65% during the period from 1 January 2028 to 31 December 2028; (c) 70% during the period from 1 January 2029 to 31 December 2029.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Appendix 1: the PRA Rulebook instruments (Basel 3.1), Article 92(5), PDF page 15

> Indicate the output floor multiplier applicable during the reporting period, as per Article 92 (5) of the Required Level of Own Funds (CRR) Part of the PRA Rulebook.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 02.00 row 0035, PDF page 29

#### Why a wrong return passes

A correct return never fails: the four values the rules allow - 60%, 65%, 70% (Article 92(5), optional, by year) and 72.5% (Article 92(2A)) - are all accepted, and an entity outside the floor reports nothing and the rule does not run (tested: not evaluated). A wrong one passes: 0.55 is also accepted; a search of the Required Level of Own Funds Part (pp.11-16) finds 72.5% on p.13 and 60%, 65%, 70% on p.15 and no 55% anywhere. The rule is also not date-aware (0.60 would be accepted in 2030), which is likewise permissive.

#### Worked example

A firm reporting for 2027 files multiplier 0.60: satisfied. A firm that wrongly files 0.55: also satisfied (ERROR-severity rule lets it through). 0.50: unsatisfied. The return below files 0.55, the value Article 92 does not give; Arelle accepts it.

Arelle's result on it:

| Rule | Satisfied | Unsatisfied | What the example shows |
|---|---|---|---|
| boe_b0359 | 1 | 0 | holds |

</details>

#### Other ways of reporting considered

Not applicable - no correct return is rejected, so there is nothing to work around.

#### Proposed change

Delete the first disjunct: ({t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0035, c: 0030} = 0.60) or (... = 0.65) or (... = 0.70) or (... = 0.725), and change the label to '60, 65, 70, 72.5'. Low priority.

#### EBA precedent

None; the rule is the Bank's own (no EBA equivalent recorded in the v4.0.0 workbook).

#### Who is affected

No firm is affected adversely. A firm that files 0.55 by mistake is not stopped.

#### What a firm can do meanwhile

A pass of this rule is no evidence that the figure is one the rules permit: check it against the rules yourself.

<a id="pi-34"></a>

### PI-34 - CVA transitional (rule 7.1(2)): boe_b0946-b0948 equate the total before the discount scalar with the total after it

**Status:** identified by rwa-filer, not yet raised with the Bank of England.

**Severity:** ERROR (boe_b0946, boe_b0947).

**Effect:** a return that follows the reporting instructions fails it. **Cause:** contradicts the reporting instructions; conflicts with another published rule.

#### The rules

| Rule | Module | Severity | Part in the issue | Where the issue applies | At the gateway |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| boe_b0946 | PRA001 | ERROR | the rule at issue | every evaluation (a break there may also be the return's own) | run as published |
| boe_b0947 | PRA001 | ERROR | the rule at issue | every evaluation (a break there may also be the return's own) | run as published |
| boe_b0271 | PRA001 | ERROR | cannot hold together with it | - | run as published |
| boe_b0273 | PRA001 | WARNING | cannot hold together with it | - | run as published |
| boe_b0275 | PRA001 | WARNING | cannot hold together with it | - | run as published |
| boe_b0196 | PRA001 | ERROR | holds on the example (control) | - | run as published |
| boe_b0944 | PRA001 | ERROR | holds on the example (control) | - | run as published |
| boe_b0948 | PRA001 | ERROR | related | - | run as published |
| boe_b0270 | PRA001 | ERROR | related | - | run as published |
| boe_b0192 | PRA001 | ERROR | related | - | run as published |
| boe_b0943 | PRA001 | ERROR | related | - | run as published |

| boe_b0194 | PRA001 | ERROR | related | - | run as published |
| boe_b0267 | PRA001 | ERROR | related | - | run as published |

boe_b0946, as published in taxonomy 4.1.1 (label: "Under the transitional arrangements of rule 7.1(2), exposures subject to SA-CVA Capital requirements must be consistent with post-weighted Total SA-CVA Capital Requirements post-discount factor|"):

```text
if ({t: OF25.01.01.04, r: 0020, c: 0010, dv: false(), seq: False, id: v0, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} = true()) then ({t: OF25.01.01.03, r: 0020, c: 0030, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v1, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i= {t: OF25.03.01.01, r: 0080, c: 0040, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v2, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting}) else true()
```

boe_b0947, as published in taxonomy 4.1.1 (label: "Under the transitional arrangements of rule 7.1(2), exposures subject to full BA-CVA Capital requirements must be consistent with post-weighted Total full BA-CVA Capital Requirements after applying the discount factor|"):

```text
if ({t: OF25.01.01.04, r: 0020, c: 0010, dv: false(), seq: False, id: v0, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} = true()) then ({t: OF25.01.01.03, r: 0030, c: 0030, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v1, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i= {t: OF25.02.01.01, r: 0100, c: 0010, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v2, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting}) else true()
```

#### What the rule requires

For a firm that has chosen the rule 7.1(2) transitional (OF 25.01.01.04 row 0020 = true), boe_b0946 requires OF 25.01 row 0020 column 0030 (the SA-CVA capital requirement) to equal OF 25.03 row 0080 column 0040 (the SA-CVA total AFTER the discount scalar); boe_b0947 and boe_b0948 require the same for full BA-CVA (OF 25.01 row 0030 = OF 25.02.01.01 row 0100) and reduced BA-CVA (OF 25.01 row 0040 = OF 25.02.01.02 row 0050). In the Bank's taxonomy the OF 25.01 cells are the same data points as the methodology totals BEFORE the scalar: OF 25.01.01.03 r0020 c0030 and OF 25.03.01.01 r0070 c0040 are one data point (eba_met:mi184; APR boe_eba_AP:x10003; BAS x9, MCY x110, PRP x10, TMA x5, TRI x7); r0030 c0030 and OF 25.02.01.01 r0090 c0010 are one data point (the same, with APR x10005); r0040 c0030 and OF 25.02.01.02 r0040 c0010 are one data point (the same, with APR x10004). The Bank's table linkbases (tab/of25.01.01.03-rend.xml, of25.03.01.01-rend.xml, of25.02.01.01-rend.xml and of25.02.01.02-rend.xml) give identical coordinates for the shared cells. The after-scalar cells are separate facts: OF 25.03.01.01 r0080 c0040 and OF 25.02.01.01 r0100 c0010 add eba_dim:APE = boe_eba_AP:x10039, and OF 25.02.01.02 r0050 c0010 (reduced BA-CVA) adds it as well and has no APR member, which boe_b0948's second variable matches by filtering APR = eba_AP:x0. Each rule therefore requires 'total before the scalar' = 'total after the scalar'. Arelle binds the shared fact: a return that writes the SA-CVA figure only in the OF 25.03 row 0070 cell still evaluates boe_b0946, and it fails.

#### What the instructions and rules say

#### Why a correct return fails

Annex II defines the shared facts before the scalar (OF 25.03 row 0070 column 0040, p.277; OF 25.02 Total row 0090, pp.275-276, 'K-full multiplied by DS'; the reduced BA-CVA table, p.276). The final scalar of rule 7.1(2) is below 1 whenever the legacy exempt ratio LER is above 0: in 2027 the intermediate scalar is max(70%, 1 - LER x 3/5 x 0.3/0.5), and the final scalar is at most 1. A firm with LER = 0 has no reason to elect 7.1(2). So the before-scalar figure X and the after-scalar figure P = wX differ, and each rule demands X = P.

Neither reading of the Annex II p.273 note ('if firms use the transitional described under rule 7.1(2), this number should be total capital requirements after applying the discount scalar') escapes this. (i) If the note covers row 0010 only, the shared cells hold the before-scalar figures, so boe_b0946-b0948 fail, and boe_b0270 and boe_b0192 (row 0010 = sum of rows 0020-0050) fail as well, because row 0010 (after the scalar) is no longer the sum of the methodology rows (before it); Annex II's 'sum of rows 0020 to 0050' and 'after applying the discount scalar' already conflict under this reading. (ii) If the note covers every methodology row, the shared cells hold after-scalar figures, so OF 25.03 row 0070 column 0040 is misreported against p.277 and boe_b0271 (SA-CVA total = delta + vega) fails; for BA-CVA the same holds with boe_b0273 (Total = 0.65 x K-full) or boe_b0275 (0.65 x K-reduced). Under reading (i) an SA-CVA firm fails ERROR rules; under reading (ii) a BA-CVA firm fails only the WARNING boe_b0273 / b0275, at the cost of a misreported OF 25.02 Total. The p.273 note is made for columns 0010, 0020 and 0040 as well as column 0030, so the question of what 'this number' covers applies to all four. The sibling rules boe_b0943-b0945 (the rule 7.1(1) twins) and boe_b0193 / b0194 compare the shared data point with itself, which suggests the rules were written as if these cells were separate facts.

boe_b0948 has the same defect for reduced BA-CVA (measured separately: [0,1] on a reduced BA-CVA return under 7.1(2)); it cannot be shown in the same example, because full and reduced BA-CVA are alternatives (boe_b0400 forbids both). Two asides: Annex II p.276 calls OF 25.02.01.01 row 0100 'CVA RWAs', but its data point is eba_met:mi184 (own funds requirements) and boe_b0947 compares it with a capital-requirement cell; and Annex II p.274 heads OF 25.01.01.04 row 0010 'Transitional arrangement described under rule 7.1(2), or partial reintegration of legacy trades...', while the taxonomy labels that row 'rule 7.1(1)' (row 0020 is 7.1(2) in both).

#### Worked example

A firm using SA-CVA for part of its portfolio and full BA-CVA (hedges recognised) for the rest, on the rule 7.1(2) transitional, reporting date 31 March 2027 (cap 70%). Legacy exempt ratio 55.56%, so the intermediate scalar is max(70%, 100% - 0.5556 x 3/5 x 0.3/0.5) = 80%, and with K_T = K_1 the final scalar is also 80%. SA-CVA: interest-rate delta 60,000 and vega 40,000, mCVA 1; OF 25.03 row 0070 column 0040 = 100,000 (before the scalar), row 0080 column 0040 = 80,000 (after it). Full BA-CVA: K-reduced 4,000,000 = sqrt(9.6e12 + 6.4e12); K-hedged 3,200,000 = sqrt(6.0e12 + 4.0e12 + 2.4e11); K-full = 0.25 x 4,000,000 + 0.75 x 3,200,000 = 3,400,000; Total 0.65 x 3,400,000 = 2,210,000 (row 0090); after the scalar 1,768,000 (row 0100). OF 25.01, as Annex II p.273 reads (row 0010 after the scalar, the methodology rows before it): row 0020 capital 100,000 (the OF 25.03 data point), RWA 1,250,000; row 0030 capital 2,210,000 (the OF 25.02 data point), RWA 27,625,000; rows 0040 and 0050 zero; row 0010 capital 1,848,000 = 80,000 + 1,768,000, RWA 23,100,000. Other inputs: OF 25.01.01.01 SA-CVA and full BA-CVA true, reduced BA-CVA and the alternative approach false; OF 25.01.01.04 row 0010 false, row 0020 true with the legacy exempt ratio; notional 5,000,000,000. boe_b0946 and boe_b0947 fail; boe_b0270, b0192 and b0261 (row 0010 = the methodology rows) fail under this reading too; the square-root, K-full, 0.65 and 0.08 rules hold.
