#### Other ways of reporting considered

Every layout was run through Arelle. SA-CVA: row 0010 after the scalar and the methodology rows before it fails boe_b0946, b0270 and b0192; everything before the scalar (the p.273 note ignored) fails boe_b0946; every OF 25.01 row after the scalar (so the shared OF 25.03 row 0070 column 0040 is after it, against p.277) fails boe_b0271; that plus every OF 25.03 delta and vega figure scaled by the scalar (misreporting the rule 5.15 / 5.17 amounts) passes everything. Full BA-CVA: reading (i) fails boe_b0947, b0270, b0267 and b0192 (all ERROR); everything before the scalar fails boe_b0947; the after-scalar figure in the shared OF 25.02 Total fails only the WARNING boe_b0273, and so contradicts pp.275-276. Scaling K-full as well (row 0080 = K-full / 0.65 of the after-scalar figure, rows 0090 and 0100 both after the scalar) passes all 27 OF 25 rules, but row 0080 must be K-full for all trades under rule 4.5 and row 0090 must be DS x K-full; it passes only because boe_b0272, which checks K-full, is gated on the SA-CVA flag (PI-39). Reduced BA-CVA: the same pattern with boe_b0948, b0268 and the WARNING b0275. Reporting OF 25.01 row 0030 after the scalar while OF 25.02 row 0090 is before it is not possible: they are one fact. Leaving rows 0080 / 0100 / 0050 blank does not help, because the default 0 still fails boe_b0946-b0948. An SA-CVA firm therefore has no compliant return that passes every ERROR rule; a BA-CVA firm escapes them only by misreporting the OF 25.02 Total.

#### Proposed change

Preferred, keeping the shared data points (which make the OF 25.01 methodology rows before-scalar figures): (1) replace boe_b0946 with if ({OF25.01.01.04 r0020 c0010} = true()) then ({OF25.03.01.01 r0080 c0040} <= {OF25.03.01.01 r0070 c0040} and {OF25.03.01.01 r0080 c0040} >= 0.7 * {OF25.03.01.01 r0070 c0040}) else true(), and boe_b0947 (OF 25.02.01.01 row 0100 against row 0090) and boe_b0948 (OF 25.02.01.02 row 0050 against row 0040) the same way. The bounds hold for 2027-2029 because 70% <= cap <= intermediate scalar <= final scalar <= 100% under rules 7.1(2) and 7.2; for boe_b0947 they hold only if row 0100 is a capital amount (mi184), not the 'CVA RWAs' Annex II p.276 calls it, which the Bank should confirm. A simpler short-term form is the one-sided inequality (after <= before). (2) Add the precondition {OF25.01.01.04 r0020 c0010} != true() to boe_b0270, b0192, b0261, b0266, b0267 and b0268, and to the column twins boe_b0200 (r0010 c0020 = sum of rows 0020-0040) and boe_b0203 (column 0040) and the Alternative Approach rule boe_b0269, which carry the same p.273 note; for 7.1(2) firms add {OF25.01.01.03 r0010 c0030} i= isum({OF25.03.01.01 r0080 c0040}, {OF25.02.01.01 r0100 c0010}, {OF25.02.01.02 r0050 c0010}), and the same with /0.08 for column 0010. (3) Amend Annex II p.273 to say the after-scalar note applies to row 0010 only. Alternative, matching the apparent intent (boe_b0946's label says 'post-weighted ... post-discount factor'): give OF 25.01.01.03 rows 0020-0040 data points of their own in the next taxonomy release, then retarget boe_b0271, b0193 and b0194 and drop the 7.1(1) twins boe_b0943-b0945, which are tautologies under the current model.

#### EBA precedent

None: the rule 7.1(2) discount scalar, OF 25.01.01.04 and the after-scalar rows are PRA-specific, and all of these rules are the Bank's own. The workbook text matches the formula for boe_b0947.

#### Who is affected

Any firm that elects the rule 7.1(2) transitional and has a final discount scalar below 100% - whenever its legacy exempt ratio is above 0 - for reporting dates from 1 January 2027 until the transitional ends on 1 January 2030. Each methodology used gives one ERROR per return. SA-CVA users fail an ERROR under every reading; BA-CVA users fail an ERROR or, by misreporting, a WARNING.

#### What a firm can do meanwhile

Report the figures the instructions require; do not change correct figures to satisfy the rule. An Error-severity break blocks the submission at the gateway: if the gateway rejects the return on this rule, raise it with the PRA, citing this issue.

<a id="pi-35"></a>

### PI-35 - OF 25.02: boe_b0205 states K-reduced as a sum where boe_b0076 takes the square root, on the same data points

**Status:** identified by rwa-filer, not yet raised with the Bank of England.

**Severity:** WARNING (boe_b0205).

**Effect:** a return that follows the reporting instructions fails it. **Cause:** conflicts with another published rule; contradicts the PRA Rulebook as amended by PS1/26.

#### The rules

| Rule | Module | Severity | Part in the issue | Where the issue applies | At the gateway |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| boe_b0205 | PRA001 | WARNING | the rule at issue | every evaluation | run as published |
| boe_b0076 | PRA001 | WARNING | cannot hold together with it | - | run as published |
| boe_b0275 | PRA001 | WARNING | holds on the example (control) | - | run as published |

boe_b0205, as published in taxonomy 4.1.1 (label: "Under the full BA-CVA approach, the capital requirements are equal to 0.65 times K-full|"):

```text
if {t: OF25.01.01.01, r: 0020, c: 0010, dv: false(), seq: False, id: v2, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} = true() then {t: OF25.02.01.02, r: 0010, c: 0010, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v0, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i= isum({t: OF25.02.01.02, r: 0020; 0030, c: 0020, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True, id: v1, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting}) else true()
```

#### What the rule requires

For a full BA-CVA firm that files OF 25.02.01.02, b0205 requires K-reduced (r0010 c0010) to equal r0020 c0020 + r0030 c0020. OF25.02.01.02 r0010/r0020/r0030 are the same data points (metrics boe_met:mi10012 / mi10013 / mi10014, APR boe_eba_AP:x10004) as OF25.02.01.01 r0010/r0020/r0030. On those data points b0076 requires K-reduced = sqrt(r0020 + r0030). Both hold only if the sum S satisfies S = sqrt(S), i.e. S is 0 or 1.

#### What the instructions and rules say

> Aggregation of systematic components (K-reduced) refers to the first term under the square root sign in rule 4.2 of the Credit Valuation Adjustment Risk Part of the PRA rulebook., i.e. (ρ ∙∑SCVAC C )2 [...] Aggregation of idiosyncratic components (K-Reduced) refers to the second term under the square root sign in rule 4.2 of the Credit Valuation Adjustment Risk Part of the PRA Rulebook, i.e. ((1 −ρ2) ∙∑SCVAC 2 C
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 25.02 reduced BA-CVA r0020 / r0030, PDF page 276

> If a firm does not use any eligible BA-CVA hedges to hedge CVA risk it must calculate its own funds requirement for CVA risk in accordance with the following formula: DSBA−CVA × Kreduced where: DSBA−CVA = 0.65; and Kreduced is calculated in accordance with the following formula: Kreduced = √(ρ ∙∑SCVAC C ) 2 + (1 −ρ2) ∙∑SCVAC 2 C
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Appendix 1: the PRA Rulebook instruments (Basel 3.1), CVA Risk Part rule 4.2, PDF page 399

> If a firm uses one or more eligible BA-CVA hedges to hedge CVA risk it must calculate its own funds requirement for CVA risk in accordance with the following formula: DSBA−CVA × Kfull where: DSBA−CVA = 0.65; Kfull = β ∙Kreduced + (1 −β) ∙Khedged; where: β = 0.25;
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Appendix 1: the PRA Rulebook instruments (Basel 3.1), CVA Risk Part rule 4.5, PDF page 401

#### Why a correct return fails

The rule runs only for a full BA-CVA firm that also files the reduced BA-CVA table, and such a firm can avoid it by not filing that table (below); where it does run, it is wrong as written. Rule 4.2 and Annex II p.276 make K-reduced the square root of r0020 + r0030. b0205 asserts the sum itself. Its label ('Under the full BA-CVA approach, the capital requirements are equal to 0.65 times K-full', the same as boe_b0273's) does not describe its expression either. For any realistic portfolio (S far from 0 and 1), a correct K-reduced fails b0205. The firm cannot satisfy both rules, because b0076 asserts the square root on the same three facts.

#### Worked example

A full BA-CVA firm with no transitional (OF 25.01.01.04 rows 0010 and 0020 false): K-reduced 4,000,000 = sqrt(9.6e12 + 6.4e12); K-hedged 3,200,000 = sqrt(6.0e12 + 4.0e12 + 2.4e11); K-full 0.25 x 4,000,000 + 0.75 x 3,200,000 = 3,400,000; Total 0.65 x 3,400,000 = 2,210,000 (RWA 27,625,000). The firm also files OF 25.02.01.02 with its three K-reduced cells, which are the same data points as in OF 25.02.01.01, so the return holds 25 facts for 28 cells. The reduced table's Total (row 0040) is the same data point as OF 25.01 row 0040 column 0030, which a full BA-CVA firm reports as 0, so it is reported as 0. boe_b0076 holds on the very facts boe_b0205 fails (4,000,000 against 16,000,000,000,000); boe_b0274 fails as well (PI-40).

#### Other ways of reporting considered

A full BA-CVA firm avoids b0205 entirely by not filing OF 25.02.01.02. Annex II gives that table no scope line. However, its r0040 'Total' is the same data point as OF 25.01 r0040 c0030 (the reduced BA-CVA methodology row), which p.272 tells a firm not using reduced BA-CVA to report as 0. The table is therefore built for reduced BA-CVA firms. b0205's guard picks exactly the firms that would not normally file it. For reduced BA-CVA firms, the table's real population, there is no square-root check at all. No Bank rule requires a full BA-CVA firm to file OF 25.02.01.02 (boe_b0402 gates the table's row 0040 on the reduced BA-CVA flag only), while boe_b0205 and boe_b0274 presuppose that it does. No figure for K-reduced satisfies both b0076 and b0205 when S is not 0 or 1.

#### Proposed change

Change b0205's guard to reduced BA-CVA and its formula to the square root: if ({OF25.01.01.01 r0010 c0010} = true() and isum({OF25.02.01.02 r0020; 0030, c0020}) >= 0) then {OF25.02.01.02 r0010 c0010} i= exp(isum({OF25.02.01.02 r0020; 0030, c0020}), 1, 2) else true(). Keep the precondition tOF25.01.01.01 and tOF25.02.01.02. Relabel it 'Under the reduced BA-CVA approach, K-reduced is equal to the square root of the sum of the systematic and idiosyncratic components'. Optionally state the scope of the reduced decomposition table in Annex II (reduced BA-CVA firms).

#### EBA precedent

Not checked; the OF 25.02 tables are PRA templates.

#### Who is affected

WARNING only. It fires only for a full BA-CVA firm that also files OF 25.02.01.02, a narrow population.

#### What a firm can do meanwhile

Report the figures the instructions require; do not change correct figures to satisfy the rule. A Warning-severity break does not stop the submission: explain it when you submit, citing this issue.

### PI-36 - OF 18.00: v6019_m (currency sheets sum to the Total) lacks the 1.3 SSA scalar that boe_b0824 applies

**Status:** identified by rwa-filer, not yet raised with the Bank of England.

**Severity:** ERROR (v6019_m).

**Effect:** a return that follows the reporting instructions fails it. **Cause:** conflicts with another published rule; contradicts the PRA Rulebook as amended by PS1/26.

#### The rules

| Rule | Module | Severity | Part in the issue | Where the issue applies | At the gateway |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| v6019_m | PRA001 | ERROR | the rule at issue | every evaluation (a break there may also be the return's own) | run as published |
| boe_b0824 | PRA001 | ERROR | cannot hold together with it | - | run as published |
| v0571_m | PRA001 | ERROR | related | - | run as published |
| v0569_m | PRA001 | ERROR | related | - | run as published |
| v7321_n | PRA001 | WARNING | related | - | run as published |
| v7322_n | PRA001 | WARNING | related | - | run as published |

v6019_m, as published in taxonomy 4.1.1 (label: `[v6019_m];[sum({t: OF18.00.01.01, r: 0010, c: 0070, z: 0002; 0003; 0004; 0005; 0006; 0007; 0008; 0009; 0012; 0013; 0014; 0015; 0016; 0017; 0018; 0019; 0020; 0021; 0022; 0023; 0024; 0025; 0026}) = {t: OF18.00.01.01, r: 0010, c: 0070, z: 0001} - 12.5 * ({t: OF18.00.01.01, r: 0325, c: 0060, z: 0001} + {t: OF18.00.01.01, r: 0330, c: 0060, z: 0001})]|`):

```text
isum({t: OF18.00.01.01, r: 0010, c: 0070, z: 0002; 0003; 0004; 0005; 0006; 0007; 0008; 0009; 0012; 0013; 0014; 0015; 0016; 0017; 0018; 0019; 0020; 0021; 0022; 0023; 0024; 0025; 0026, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True, id: v0, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting}) i= {t: OF18.00.01.01, r: 0010, c: 0070, z: 0001, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v1, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i- 12.5 i* ({t: OF18.00.01.01, r: 0325, c: 0060, z: 0001, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v2, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i+ {t: OF18.00.01.01, r: 0330, c: 0060, z: 0001, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v3, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting})
```

#### What the rule requires

The sum of the currency sheets' total risk exposure amount (r0010 c0070) equals the Total sheet's r0010 c0070 less 12.5 × (securitisation charge r0325 + CTP charge r0330) on the Total sheet.

#### What the instructions and rules say

> (a) the own funds requirements for position risk referred to in the Market Risk: Simplified Standardised Approach (CRR) Part, multiplied by: (i) 1.3 for own funds requirements relating to general and specific risk of positions in debt instruments as calculated in accordance with Market Risk: Simplified Standardised Approach (CRR) Part Articles 334 to 340;
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Appendix 1: the PRA Rulebook instruments (Basel 3.1), Market Risk: General Provisions (CRR) Part, Article 325(2)(a)(i), PDF page 226

> The specific risk associated with exposures included in MKR SA SEC and MKR SA CTP has only to be reported in the Total template of the MKR SA TDI. The own funds requirements reported in those templates shall be transferred to cell {0325;0060} (securitisations) and {0330;0060} (CTP) respectively.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 18.00 general remarks, para 160, PDF page 227

> 0250 SPECIFIC RISK Sum of amounts reported in rows 0251, 0325 and 0330. ... 0325 Own funds requirement for securitisation instruments Total own funds requirements reported in column 0601 of template MKR SA SEC. Those total own funds requirements shall only be reported on Total level of the MKR SA TDI.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 18.00 rows 0250, 0325 and 0330, PDF pages 229-230

> Result of the multiplication of the own funds requirements by 12,5.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 18.00 column 0070, PDF page 228

#### Why a correct return fails

Let S = r0325 + r0330, reported on the Total sheet only. boe_b0824 puts 1.3 × S into the Total sheet's r0010 c0060, which is right: Art. 325(2)(a)(i) covers Articles 334 to 340, including Article 337 (securitisation instruments); Article 338, the correlation trading portfolio, is '[Provision left blank]' in PS1/26, although Annex II still cites Article 338(2) and (3) for OF 20 (p.233). The currency sheets carry no S. So Σ currency r0010 c0070 = Total r0010 c0070 − 12.5 × 1.3 × S, whereas v6019_m requires Total − 12.5 × S. Both hold only if S = 0. v6019_m is an EBA rule written for CRR, where r0010 was the unscaled sum.

#### Worked example

A firm on the simplified standardised approach for market risk. GBP sheet: general risk on debt instruments (maturity-based) 100,000, so r0010 c0060 = 1.3 x 100,000 = 130,000 and c0070 = 1,625,000. USD sheet: general risk 60,000, so 78,000 and 975,000. A trading-book securitisation position carries a specific-risk charge of 40,000 (OF 19 row 0010 column 0601), reported on the Total sheet only, in rows 0325 and 0250. Total sheet: r0011 = 160,000, r0010 c0060 = 1.3 x (160,000 + 40,000) = 260,000, c0070 = 3,250,000. The currency sheets add to 2,600,000; v6019_m asks for 3,250,000 - 12.5 x 40,000 = 2,750,000, while with the scalar it would ask for 3,250,000 - 16.25 x 40,000 = 2,600,000. boe_b0824 (the 1.3 scalar) and v3388_i (the Total's row 0325 = OF 19 column 0601) hold.

|---|---|---|---|
| boe_b0824 | 3 | 0 | - |
| v0002_h | 3 | 0 | - |
| v0569_m | 3 | 0 | - |
| v0571_m | 1 | 0 | - |
| v3388_i | 1 | 0 | - |
| v3763_s | 3 | 0 | - |
| v3764_s | 11 | 0 | - |
| v6019_m | 0 | 1 | fails |
| v7321_n | 0 | 0 | - |
| v7322_n | 0 | 0 | - |
| v7780_m | 1 | 0 | - |

#### Other ways of reporting considered

Leaving the securitisation charge unscaled in the Total r0010 (1.3 × 160,000 + 40,000 = 248,000): v6019_m then passes [1,0], but boe_b0824 fails [2,1] (ERROR) and the figure contradicts Art. 325(2)(a)(i). Reporting r0325/r0330 on currency sheets is excluded by Annex II para 160 and the r0325/r0330 instructions, and is flagged by v7321_n/v7322_n. No compliant alternative.

#### Proposed change

v6019_m: replace the factor 12.5 with 16.25 (= 12.5 × 1.3). Corrected expression: isum({t: OF18.00.01.01, r: 0010, c: 0070, z: 0002; ...; 0026}) i= {t: OF18.00.01.01, r: 0010, c: 0070, z: 0001} i- 16.25 i* ({t: OF18.00.01.01, r: 0325, c: 0060, z: 0001} i+ {t: OF18.00.01.01, r: 0330, c: 0060, z: 0001}).

#### EBA precedent

v6019_m is an EBA-origin rule (v-prefix), written when r0010 = r0011 + r0250 + r0350 with no scalar. The Bank added boe_b0824 (the 1.3 scalar) but left v6019_m unchanged. v6020_m (OF 21) has no subtraction term and is not affected; the other OF 19-23 cross-sheet sums were not rechecked.

#### Who is affected

Firms on the simplified standardised approach with specific risk on trading-book securitisation instruments (Art. 337): one ERROR per return per period, from the first Basel 3.1 market-risk return.

#### What a firm can do meanwhile

Report the figures the instructions require; do not change correct figures to satisfy the rule. An Error-severity break blocks the submission at the gateway: if the gateway rejects the return on this rule, raise it with the PRA, citing this issue.

### PI-37 - boe_b0920 ties the IMA default-risk requirement to the most recent figure, not the higher of most recent and average

**Status:** identified by rwa-filer, not yet raised with the Bank of England.

**Severity:** ERROR (boe_b0920).

**Effect:** a return that follows the reporting instructions fails it. **Cause:** contradicts the reporting instructions; contradicts the PRA Rulebook as amended by PS1/26.

#### The rules

| Rule | Module | Severity | Part in the issue | Where the issue applies | At the gateway |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| boe_b0920 | PRA001 | ERROR | the rule at issue | every evaluation (a break there may also be the return's own) | run as published |
| boe_b1091 | PRA001 | WARNING | related | - | run as published |
| v3346_i | PRA001 | WARNING | related | - | run as published |

boe_b0920, as published in taxonomy 4.1.1 (label: "Value should match aggregated own fund requirements and RWAs for Default risk charge in IMA1b|"):

```text
{t: OF24.02.01.01, r: 0010, c: 0120, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v0, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i= {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0583, c: 0010, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v1, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting}
```

#### What the rule requires

The IMA default-risk row of OF 02.00 (r0583) must equal OF 24.02 r0010 c0120, the most recently measured internal default-risk-model own funds requirement.

#### What the instructions and rules say

> An institution which holds positions in traded debt and equity instruments that are included in the scope of the internal default risk model and assigned to the trading desks referred to in paragraph 1 shall fulfil an additional own funds requirement, expressed as the higher of the following values: (a) the most recent own funds requirement for default risk, calculated in accordance with Section 3 of this Part; or (b) the average of the amount referred to in point (a) over the preceding 12 weeks.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Appendix 1: the PRA Rulebook instruments (Basel 3.1), Art. 325ba(2), PDF page 241

> 0110 The average of the internal default risk model own fund requirements measured over the previous 12 weeks calculated in accordance with Article 325bn [...] 0120 The most recent measured internal default risk model own fund requirements calculated in accordance with Article 325bn of the Market Risk: Internal Model Approach (CRR) Part of the PRA rulebook
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 24.02 c0110 / c0120, PDF page 248

> 0583 1.3.3.3 Default risk charge (DRC) The IMA own funds requirements for desks under IMA. This is applicable only to IMA firms. This corresponds to aggregated own fund requirements and RWAs for Default risk charge in IMA1b. Firms must not complete this row during the IMA transitional period.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 02.00 r0583, PDF page 35

> 0580 1.3.3 Risk exposure amount for position, foreign exchange and commodities risks under internal model approach (IMA) – for IMA desks only The IMA own funds requirements for desks under IMA. This is applicable only to IMA firms.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 02.00 r0580, PDF page 34

> 0130 TOTAL RISK EXPOSURE AMOUNT Point (b) of Article 92(4) CRR. Result of the multiplication of the own funds requirements by 12.5
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, C 24.00 c0130 (same data point as OF 02.00 r0580), PDF page 253

> IMA transitional period means the period beginning with 1 January 2027 and ending with 31 December 2027.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Appendix 1: the PRA Rulebook instruments (Basel 3.1), Glossary, PDF page 5

> Template OF 02.00 summarises total risk exposure amounts where standardised approaches have been applied for the purposes of calculating the output floor (column 0020).
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 02.00 general remarks, PDF page 28

#### Why a correct return fails

Row 0583 carries the IMA default-risk requirement, which Art. 325ba(2) sets at max(most recent, 12-week average) = max(c0120, c0110). Its taxonomy metric is mi235 'Total risk exposure amount' (labels from the EBA dictionary shipped in the Bank's package), Annex II says OF 02.00 'summarises total risk exposure amounts' (p.28), its parent row 0580 is the C 24.00 TREA data point, and b1091 adds r0580 into market-risk RWAs, so the cell is a risk exposure amount: 12.5 x max(c0110, c0120). b0920 compares it with c0120 (metric mi184, own funds requirements). As a risk exposure amount, the rule fails for every IMA firm with a non-zero DRC. Even in own-funds units, it fails whenever the 12-week average exceeds the most recent figure.

#### Worked example

An IMA firm with an internal default-risk model, at a reporting date after the IMA transitional period (the rule does not read the date). Most recent default-risk own funds requirement 80,000 (OF 24.02 row 0010 column 0120), 12-week average 100,000 (column 0110), so the requirement is the higher, 100,000, and the risk exposure amount 12.5 x 100,000 = 1,250,000, which is what OF 02.00 row 0583 reports under its metric. boe_b0920 compares 1,250,000 with 80,000. The non-negativity rule boe_b0428 holds.

Arelle's result on it:

| Rule | Satisfied | Unsatisfied | What the example shows |
|---|---|---|---|
| boe_b0428 | 2 | 0 | - |
| boe_b0920 | 0 | 1 | fails |

<details>
<summary>The example's 3 cells</summary>

| Table | Sheet | Key | Row | Column | Value |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| OF24.02.01.01 |  |  | 0010 | 0110 | 100,000 |
| OF24.02.01.01 |  |  | 0010 | 0120 | 80,000 |
| OF02.00.01.01 |  |  | 0583 | 0010 | 1,250,000 |

</details>

#### Other ways of reporting considered

Reporting r0583 = 100,000 (the requirement in own-funds units) fails [0,1]. With the most recent figure the higher one (100,000 against an average of 80,000) and r0583 = 1,250,000 as a risk exposure amount, the rule fails [0,1] too, so under the risk-exposure-amount reading the rule fails even when the most recent figure is the higher one. The only passing value is r0583 = c0120, the most recent figure in own-funds units. That contradicts Art. 325ba(2) whenever the average is higher, and contradicts the cell's metric always. One piece of contrary evidence on units: OF 02.00 r0584 c0010 and OF 24.01 r0010 c0210 (a capital surcharge, described as an own-funds item) are one data point (metric eba_met:mi235). The taxonomy is therefore internally inconsistent on the unit of rows 0581-0585, but the rule fails under either unit.

#### Proposed change

Replace b0920 with {OF02.00.01.01 r0583 c0010} i= 12.5 i* imax({OF24.02.01.01 r0010 c0110}, {OF24.02.01.01 r0010 c0120}), consistent with mi235 'Total risk exposure amount' and the parent row 0580. If the Bank instead intends rows 0581-0585 in own-funds units, drop the 12.5, change those rows' metric to mi184 and reword Annex II p.35. Either way, resolve the same unit conflict on the data point OF 02.00 r0584 c0010 and OF 24.01 r0010 c0210 share (metric eba_met:mi235).

#### EBA precedent

None: OF 02.00 rows 0581-0585 and OF 24.02 are PRA templates.

#### Who is affected

IMA firms with an internal default-risk model, from the end of the IMA transitional period (reporting dates from 1 January 2028; Annex II p.35 forbids completing row 0583 before then). It fails on every such return under the risk-exposure-amount reading, and whenever the 12-week average exceeds the latest figure under the own-funds reading.

#### What a firm can do meanwhile

Report the figures the instructions require; do not change correct figures to satisfy the rule. An Error-severity break blocks the submission at the gateway: if the gateway rejects the return on this rule, raise it with the PRA, citing this issue.

## Clarification questions

The rule, or the text it rests on, can be read in more than one way, and a return that complies on one reading fails it. A compliant return that passes does exist, so each of these is put as a question.

<a id="pi-06"></a>

### PI-06 - boe_b1041 makes the slotting row mandatory for every OF 08.01 filer

**Status:** identified by rwa-filer, not yet raised with the Bank of England.

**Severity:** ERROR (boe_b1041).

**Effect:** a return that follows the reporting instructions fails it. **Cause:** conflicts with another published rule; the instructions leave a gap.

**The Bank's known-issues log, entry 28** (published 5 November 2026; related):

> Issue description: OF08.01 columns 0125, 0140, 0170, 0180 are greyed out for row 0080 on sheet 0002 and 0010 and therefore unnecessariy referenced in the expression context
>
> Solution: Although greyed-out cells in an expression do not constitute a validation-design issue since they are skipped during assertion evaluation, we endeavour to remove these four columns from the validation in the next taxonomy update.

#### The rules

| Rule | Module | Severity | Part in the issue | Where the issue applies | At the gateway |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| boe_b1041 | PRA001 | ERROR | the rule at issue | every evaluation (a break there may also be the return's own) | run as published |
| boe_b0631 | PRA001 | ERROR | cannot hold together with it | - | run as published |
| boe_b1039 | PRA001 | ERROR | holds on the example (control) | - | run as published |
| boe_b0206 | PRA001 | WARNING | related | - | run as published |
| boe_b0816 | PRA001 | ERROR | related | - | run as published |

boe_b1041, as published in taxonomy 4.1.1 (label: "slotting is only available for specialised lending exposures|"):

```text
not(isNull({t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0080, c: 0020; 0035; 0040; 0050; 0060; 0070; 0090; 0101; 0102; 0103; 0104; 0110; 0125; 0140; 0170; 0180; 0251; 0252; 0260; 0280; 0281; 0282; 0290; 0300, z: 0002; 0010, dv: emptySequence(), seq: False, id: v0, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting}))
```

#### What the rule requires

Whenever OF 08.01 is filed (filing indicator OF08.01.01 positive), at least one fact must be reported in row 0080 'Specialised lending slotting approach: Total' of OF 08.01.01.01 on sheet 0002 (Total, FIRB approach and slotting approach) or sheet 0010 (Corporates - Specialised Lending, FIRB approach or slotting approach), in any of the listed columns. Of the 24 listed columns, 20 are cells of that row on those sheets (0020, 0035, 0040, 0050, 0060, 0070, 0090, 0101, 0102, 0103, 0104, 0110, 0251, 0252, 0260, 0280, 0281, 0282, 0290, 0300); 0125, 0140, 0170 and 0180 are not cells of row 0080 at all. Each matching fact is one satisfied evaluation; with no matching fact there is exactly one evaluation and it is unsatisfied. It does not require every cell, both sheets, or a non-zero value.

#### What the instructions and rules say

> SPECIALISED LENDING SLOTTING APPROACH: TOTAL Exposures subject to the slotting approach. This shall only apply to the exposure sub-class 'corporate - specialised lending'.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 08.01 row 0080, PDF page 117

> In cases where an institution uses the AIRB approach for a part of its IRB exposures and the FIRB or slotting approach to calculate risk-weighted exposure amounts for the other part of its IRB exposures, one OF CR IRB Total for exposures subject to the FIRB approach or the slotting approach and one OF CR IRB Total for exposures subject to the AIRB approach shall be reported.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, section 3.3, paragraph 75, PDF page 101

> Total (The Total template must be reported for the FIRB and the slotting approaches and, separately for the AIRB approach.)
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, section 3.3.2, paragraph 76 item 1, PDF page 99

> Missing fact The fact doesn't appear in the XBRL report. Template including this fact is reported The value is treated as equivalent to zero (if numeric fact) or empty (if non-numeric) by the recipient.
>
> - Bank of England XBRL Filing Manual v1.0.1, section 2.19, missing facts, PDF page 28

> Inapplicable information should not be included in an XBRL report, i.e. inapplicable facts MAY be omitted.
>
> - Bank of England XBRL Filing Manual v1.0.1, section 2.19, PDF page 28

> Zero values SHOULD, preferably, be explicitly reported where they are interesting supervisory reporting information.
>
> - Bank of England XBRL Filing Manual v1.0.1, section 2.19, PDF page 28

> In case of error severity, failing validation should block the submission of the report.
>
> - Bank of England XBRL Filing Manual v1.0.1, section 1.10, PDF page 13

#### The question

Is a firm with no slotting exposure meant to file an explicit zero in OF 08.01 row 0080? A firm with no slotting exposure has nothing to put in the slotting row: Annex II p.117 defines row 0080 as exposures subject to the slotting approach, restricted to specialised lending, and asks for no zero. The Bank's XBRL Filing Manual (section 2.19) treats a missing fact on a reported template as equivalent to zero and lets inapplicable facts be omitted, while saying that zero values SHOULD preferably be reported where they are interesting supervisory information. Elsewhere in the rule set an unreported row 0080 and a zero are the same statement: boe_b0631 compares OF 02.00 row 0411 ('Exposures subject to the slotting approach') with OF 08.01 row 0080 on sheet 0002 using dv: 0 on both sides, and Arelle satisfies it with r0411 = 0 and no row 0080. boe_b1041 alone turns the absence into an ERROR, which blocks the submission (Filing Manual section 1.10).

A firm passes by filing a single explicit zero in row 0080 on sheet 0002 or 0010; the zero is a true statement and no other rule objects to it. So the question is whether the Bank intends to require that zero. The rule's label is boe_b0206's ('only on' sheets 0002 and 0010), which states a restriction, not a presence requirement. For an A-IRB-only firm the zero would have to sit on the FIRB and slotting Total sheet: Annex II para 76 item 1 can be read as asking every IRB filer for that Total, para 75 as asking only firms that use FIRB or slotting; a zero on the firm's own Total sheet 0001 does not satisfy boe_b1041 and breaks boe_b0206 instead. Where slotting exists the rule adds nothing: boe_b0816, b0819 and b0822 are each [0,1] when OF 08.06 reports slotting exposure and row 0080 is missing. And without 'Always execute' it could never fail, because it would evaluate only when a fact is bound. As published it either requires a zero the instructions do not ask for, or checks nothing.

#### Worked example

An F-IRB firm with a corporate loan book and no specialised lending: a collateralised loan with original exposure, exposure after CRM and exposure value of 1,000,000, PD 1.25%, RWEA 600,000 (pre-adjustment RWEA 600,000), 10 obligors. OF 08.01 is reported on sheet 0012 (Corporates - Other general corporates - non-SME, FIRB) and on the Total sheet 0002, rows 0010, 0020 (on-balance sheet) and 0070 (obligor grades total). Row 0080 is not reported, because there is no slotting exposure. OF 02.00 row 0411 (slotting RWEA) is reported as 0, so that the Bank's own cross-check boe_b0631 evaluates; it holds. Filing a 0 in row 0080 column 0020 on sheet 0002 makes boe_b1041 hold as well.

| boe_b0751 | 6 | 0 | - |
| boe_b1039 | 1 | 0 | holds |
| boe_b1040 | 6 | 0 | - |
| boe_b1041 | 0 | 1 | fails |

#### Other ways of reporting considered

To pass, a firm must file at least one fact, which may be 0, in OF 08.01.01.01 row 0080 on sheet 0002 or sheet 0010, in any of the 20 reportable columns. For an F-IRB firm that is an extra zero on a sheet it already files. For an A-IRB-only firm it means filing a fact on the FIRB/slotting Total sheet, a sheet for approaches it does not use. Zero-filling its own Total sheet 0001 does not work (boe_b1041 still [0,1], boe_b0206 [0,1]). Not filing OF 08.01 is not open to an IRB firm. The zero is a true statement and breaks no other rule, so it is a workable course, but nothing in Annex II asks for it.

#### Proposed change

If the zero is not intended, withdraw (deactivate) boe_b1041: the restriction its label states is already enforced by boe_b0206 and boe_b0206_1, and the presence of row 0080 whenever slotting exposure exists by boe_b0816, b0817, b0819, b0822, b0823 and b0829 against OF 08.06 row 0095. If a presence check is wanted where slotting is reported, make it conditional and stop executing it unconditionally, for example: if not(isNull({t: OF08.06.01.01, r: 0095, c: 0010, dv: emptySequence()})) then not(isNull({t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0080, c: 0020, z: 0002; 0010, dv: emptySequence()})) else true(), with Always execute = no. If the zero is intended, say so in the Annex II instruction for row 0080, including which sheet an A-IRB-only firm uses, and give the rule its own label. The Bank already intends to drop columns 0125, 0140, 0170 and 0180, which are not cells of row 0080 (known-issues log entry 28).

#### EBA precedent

None. The Bank's v4.0.0 extract gives boe_b1041 no EBA equivalent. The equivalent of boe_b0206 is EBA v10673_m, '{r0080} = 0' on the non-specialised-lending sheets of C 08.01, Warning, 'if value missing: do not run rule' in the EBA list's v3.2-v3.5 sheets (v3.0 and v3.1 say 'treat as zero/empty string'). The EBA has no rule that requires row 0080 to be present.

#### Who is affected

ERROR severity, every reporting date. Every firm that reports OF 08.01, has no slotting exposure and does not file the zero: F-IRB firms with no slotted specialised lending, and A-IRB-only firms, including retail-only IRB lenders whose sheets are 0001 and 0015 to 0021. boe_b1041 is not on the November 2026 deny list; the Bank's known-issues log entry 28 concerns four greyed columns in the rule's expression, not the presence check.

#### What a firm can do meanwhile

Until the Bank answers, report on the reading you hold to be right and say which when you submit. An Error-severity break blocks the submission at the gateway: if the gateway rejects the return on this rule, raise it with the PRA, citing this question.

<a id="pi-09"></a>

### PI-09 - OF 08.03 sub-band sums include column 0030 (average conversion factor) in boe_b0768-b0770 but not in boe_b0767

**Status:** identified by rwa-filer, not yet raised with the Bank of England.

**Severity:** ERROR (boe_b0768, boe_b0769, boe_b0770).

**Effect:** a return that follows the reporting instructions fails it. **Cause:** conflicts with another published rule; the rounding allowance the rule gives.

#### The rules

| Rule | Module | Severity | Part in the issue | Where the issue applies | At the gateway |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| boe_b0768 | PRA001 | ERROR | the rule at issue | OF08.03.01.01 columns 0030 (a break there may also be the return's own) | run as published |
| boe_b0769 | PRA001 | ERROR | the rule at issue | OF08.03.01.01 columns 0030 (a break there may also be the return's own) | run as published |
| boe_b0770 | PRA001 | ERROR | the rule at issue | OF08.03.01.01 columns 0030 (a break there may also be the return's own) | run as published |
| boe_b0767 | PRA001 | ERROR | holds on the example (control) | - | run as published |

boe_b0768, as published in taxonomy 4.1.1 (label: "Sum of PD ranges from 0.75 to 2.5|"):

```text
{t: OF08.03.01.01, r: 0070, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v0, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i= isum({t: OF08.03.01.01, r: 0080; 0090, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True, id: v1, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting})
scope({t: OF08.03.01.01, c:0010;0020;0030;0040;0060;0090;0100;0110,z:0001;0002;0006;0009;0010;0011;0012;0015;0016;0017;0018;0019;0020;0021;0022;0023;0024, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting})
```

boe_b0769, as published in taxonomy 4.1.1 (label: "Sum of PD ranges from 2.5 to 10|"):

```text
{t: OF08.03.01.01, r: 0100, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v0, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i= isum({t: OF08.03.01.01, r: 0110; 0120, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True, id: v1, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting})
scope({t: OF08.03.01.01, c:0010;0020;0030;0040;0060;0090;0100;0110,z:0001;0002;0006;0009;0010;0011;0012;0015;0016;0017;0018;0019;0020;0021;0022;0023;0024, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting})
```

boe_b0770, as published in taxonomy 4.1.1 (label: "Sum of PD ranges from 10 to 100|"):

```text
{t: OF08.03.01.01, r: 0130, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v0, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i= sum({t: OF08.03.01.01, r: 0140; 0150; 0160, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True, id: v1, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting})
scope({t: OF08.03.01.01, c:0010;0020;0030;0040;0060;0090;0100;0110,z:0001;0002;0006;0009;0010;0011;0012;0015;0016;0017;0018;0019;0020;0021;0022;0023;0024, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting})
```

#### What the rule requires

For each column in scope and each sheet, the parent PD band (0.75 to <2.5; 2.5 to <10; 10 to <100) must equal the sum of its sub-bands. Column 0030 is in scope of the three rules. Its data point is eba_met:mi796, declared in the Bank's package as <xs:element name="mi796" type="xbrli:monetaryItemType" ...> (label 'Exposure weighted conversion factors'), so its rounding allowance is whatever decimals the filer states for a monetary fact. The other averaged columns of the template (0050 PD, 0070 LGD, 0080 maturity) are correctly outside the scope; the XBRL formula of boe_b0767 no longer lists mi796, those of boe_b0768-b0770 still do.

#### What the instructions and rules say

> EXPOSURE WEIGHTED AVERAGE CONVERSION FACTORS For all exposures included in each bucket of the fixed PD range, the average conversion factor used by institutions in their calculation of risk-weighted exposure amounts, weighted by the off-balance sheet exposure pre-CCF as reported in column 0020.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 08.03 column 0030, PDF pages 119-120

> Exposures shall be allocated to an appropriate bucket of the fixed PD range based on the PD estimated for each obligor assigned to this exposure class
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 08.03 rows (PD RANGE), PDF page 122

> The Bank will interpret the decimals setting on reported data as specifying that the absolute difference between the true value of the number as known to the reporter and its reported lexical representation (known as the “absolute error” of the representation - eabs) is less than or equal to 0.5 x 10-n.
>
> - Bank of England XBRL Filing Manual v1.0.1, 30 May 2024, rule 2.18, PDF page 23

> The reported accuracy of a numeric fact SHOULD be a realistic indication of the accuracy to which the lexical representation represents the true value. In particular, it SHOULD NOT be excessively high.
>
> - Bank of England XBRL Filing Manual v1.0.1, rule 2.18(c) and footnote 11, PDF page 24

> E.g. decimals setting of greater than 2 would generally be inappropriate for calculated “monetary” values resulting from e.g. multiplications or divisions, “INF” is often unlikely to be appropriate for calculated values.
>
> - Bank of England XBRL Filing Manual v1.0.1, footnote 11 to rule 2.18(c), PDF page 24

> INF (meaning exact as written) is acceptable for the decimal attribute of all numeric types.
>
> - Bank of England XBRL Filing Manual v1.0.1, Accuracy Requirements for 2.18 (table: Monetary '>= -3'; Percentage '>= 4', 'Must be expressed as a ratio in reports'; Integer '0'), PDF page 25

#### The question

Is column 0030 meant to be in the scope of boe_b0768-b0770, and at what accuracy should an average conversion factor be stated? The Bank's own boe_b0767, the same check one level up, has dropped column 0030 in v4.1.1, as the EBA did for all four rules in framework 3.2.0; boe_b0768-b0770 keep it. A parent band's average conversion factor is the nominal-weighted mean of its sub-bands' factors, so it lies between them and cannot equal their sum unless only one sub-band has off-balance-sheet exposure. Band 0.75 to <2.5: sub-bands 0.40 (60m nominal) and 0.20 (20m) give a parent of (24m + 4m) / 80m = 0.35 against a required 0.40 + 0.20 = 0.60. The comparison is |parent - sum| <= sum of allowances, each 0.5 x 10^-decimals. Measured in Arelle on the same figures: decimals 4, 2 and INF, all three rules unsatisfied on c0030; decimals 0, boe_b0768 and boe_b0769 satisfied (tolerance 1.5 swallows a factor that cannot exceed 1) and boe_b0770 unsatisfied (0.40 against 1.10: its plain sum leaves only the parent's 0.5); decimals -3, all three satisfied (tolerance in the hundreds, vacuous). So the outcome depends on an accuracy attribute and not on the figures: as measured here, all three rules pass at decimals -1 or below, boe_b0770 alone fails at 0, and all three fail at 1 or above (the thresholds depend on the figures; with two sub-bands boe_b0768 / boe_b0769 cannot fail at decimals 0). The Bank's own sample instance states every mi796 fact at decimals -3, at which all three rules pass; a filer stating the factor to two places, or as exact, fails. A compliant passing return therefore exists, which is why this is put as a question: the rules' outcome on column 0030 turns on how precisely the filer says it knows the figure.

#### Worked example

OF 08.03 sheet 0012 (Corporates - Other general corporates - non-SME, FIRB; conversion factors from Article 111 Table A1). For each PD sub-band: off-balance-sheet nominal (c0020), its exposure-weighted average conversion factor (c0030) and exposure value (c0040); each parent row carries the totals and the nominal-weighted average factor. 0.75 to <2.5: 60m at 0.40 and 20m at 0.20, parent 80m at 0.35. 2.5 to <10: 15m at 0.50 and 5m at 0.10, parent 20m at 0.40. 10 to <100: 4m at 0.50, 2m at 0.20, 2m at 0.40, parent 8m at 0.40. 0.00 to <0.15 (control band, boe_b0767): 20m at 0.30, 20m at 0.40, 10m at 0.50, parent 50m at 0.38. c0030 stated to two places (decimals 2, pence, the Filing Manual's ceiling for a calculated monetary value); amounts exact to units.

Arelle's result on it:

| Rule | Satisfied | Unsatisfied | What the example shows |
|---|---|---|---|
| boe_b0767 | 2 | 0 | holds |
| boe_b0768 | 2 | 1 | fails |
| boe_b0769 | 2 | 1 | fails |
| boe_b0770 | 2 | 1 | fails |

#### Other ways of reporting considered

(1) State c0030 at decimals -3 (or -1, -2): passes, and the Filing Manual's minimum for a monetary fact (>= -3) allows it, though it declares a ratio of 0.35 to be known only to the nearest 1,000; rule 2.18(c) says accuracy 'SHOULD NOT be excessively high' and does not prohibit understating it, and -3 is what the Bank's own sample instance states. (2) Report c0030 on the sub-bands and leave it empty on the parent rows: fails, 0 against the sum. (3) Leave c0030 empty everywhere: passes, but Annex II asks for it 'for all exposures included in each bucket'. (4) Report the parent as the sum of the sub-band factors: passes, misstates the figure and can exceed 100%. (5) Only one sub-band with off-balance-sheet exposure: passes trivially. Which accuracy would a real filing carry? The Manual sets only a floor (monetary >= -3, INF allowed) and asks for values 'as known' with a realistic decimals; for a factor known to two or four places that is 2 (footnote 11's ceiling for calculated monetary values) or INF, and at either the rules fail. Software that stamps one decimals value on every monetary fact carries whatever that value is: -3 passes vacuously, 0 fails boe_b0770 only, 2 fails all three. Real filings were not observed.

#### Proposed change

Remove c0030 from the scope of boe_b0768, boe_b0769 and boe_b0770, giving each the scope boe_b0767 has in v4.1.1 and the EBA has used since framework 3.2.0: scope({t: OF08.03.01.01, c:0010;0020;0040;0060;0090;0100;0110, z:0001;0002;0006;0009;0010;0011;0012;0015;0016;0017;0018;0019;0020;0021;0022;0023;0024}). Separately, eba_met:mi796 holds a ratio and should not be a monetary item (see PI-14; it is declared in the EBA dictionary shipped in the Bank's package, so retyping it is not a change to the Bank's dictionary alone); while it is, the published accuracy floor of -3 makes any check on it depend on the filer's decimals.

#### EBA precedent

The equivalents are v09753_m to v09756_m (C 08.03, WARNING at the EBA, ERROR at the Bank). In EBA releases 3.0 and 3.1 all four had columns (0010;0020;0030;0040;0060;0090;0100;0110); in framework release 3.2.0 ('Last Change: Change') all four became (0010;0020;0040;0060;0090;0100;0110) and remain so in 3.3, 3.4 and 3.5 (EBA validation rules list, sheets 'v3.1(3.1.1)' and '3.2(3.2.1, 3.2.2)' to '3.5'). The Bank's v4.0.0 rules had the pre-3.2 scope on all four; v4.1.1 changed boe_b0767 alone.

#### Who is affected

IRB firms filing OF 08.03 with off-balance-sheet exposure in two or more sub-bands of a parent PD band, whose software states c0030 at decimals >= 1 (boe_b0768, boe_b0769) or >= 0 (boe_b0770): for example any filer stating monetary facts to pence or as exact. Firms stating all monetary facts to thousands are not affected. Neither boe_b0767-b0770 nor column 0030 is mentioned in the Bank's November 2026 known-issues log or deny list.

#### What a firm can do meanwhile

Until the Bank answers, report on the reading you hold to be right and say which when you submit. An Error-severity break blocks the submission at the gateway: if the gateway rejects the return on this rule, raise it with the PRA, citing this question.

#### What the instructions and rules say

>

#### The question

Does 'exposures cleared through a CCP' in OF 34.07 paragraph 129 include a clearing member's exposures to its clients on cleared trades? On the broad reading the two templates cover different populations and the rules fail; on the narrow reading they match and the rules hold. A clearing member's exposure to its client on a cleared derivative is a CCP-related transaction. It is capitalised as a bilateral exposure to the client, so an IRB firm risk-weights it under the IRB approach and reports it in OF 08.01 on the client's sheet, in row 0050 (rows 0020 / 0030 exclude CCR, and rows 0040-0060 carry no CCP exclusion). OF 34.07 'excludes exposures cleared through a CCP', a phrase Annex II itself defines, in OF 07.00 column 0211, as including CCP-related transactions. So OF 08.01 rows 0040-0060 = bilateral + cleared, OF 34.07 Total = bilateral only, and every one of the three equalities on that sheet fails by the cleared amount. On the narrow reading - only trades outstanding with the CCP itself, together with CCP-related transactions whose own funds requirements are calculated under Section 9, as in C 34.10 paragraph 132 and OF 07.00 row 0100 - the client legs belong in OF 34.07 and the templates agree. OF 07.00 has column 0211 to carve these exposures out; OF 08.01 has no counterpart column, so the difference cannot be reconciled from reported data.

#### Worked example

Financial corporates and large corporates (FIRB), sheet 0022. A clearing member has bilateral derivatives with 8 clients (exposure value 400,000, RWEA 200,000) and client-cleared derivatives with 6 other clients (250,000, 125,000), all risk-weighted under FIRB. OF 08.01 r0010 = r0050 = r0070: exposure value 650,000, RWEA 325,000, 14 obligors. OF 34.07 on the broad reading (cleared exposures excluded): one PD band and the Total with exposure value 400,000, 8 obligors, RWEA 200,000, density 0.50. The rules compute 400,000 against 650,000, 200,000 against 325,000 and 8 against 14. On the narrow reading the client legs are in OF 34.07 as well, and the three rules hold.

#### Other ways of reporting considered

(a) Including the cleared client legs in OF 34.07: all three rules pass [1,0], but that contradicts paragraph 129. (b) Leaving them out of OF 08.01 rows 0040-0060 is not open: they are IRB-weighted exposures that belong to the sheet Total, and row 0020 / 0030 instructions send CCR exposures to rows 0040-0060. (c) A narrow reading of paragraph 129 - only trades outstanding with the CCP itself, which are not IRB-weighted - would remove the gap; only OF 07.00 column 0211 (p.86) supports the broad reading. C 34.02 paragraph 124 (p.190) and C 34.10 paragraph 132 (p.210) include CCP-related transactions only where the own funds requirements are calculated under Section 9, which excludes clearing-member-to-client exposures (Article 304(1): Sections 1 to 8); OF 07.00 row 0100 (p.94) is drafted the same way; and Article 107(2) supports the narrow reading, since Section 9 exposures are not IRB-weighted. Under the narrow reading the example with the client legs included passes all three rules: this is an open question of interpretation for the Bank.

#### Proposed change

OF 08.01 has no cell that isolates cleared exposures (OF 07.00 has column 0211; OF 08.01 has no counterpart), so the equality cannot be restored from reported data. In all 51 rules replace 'i=' by 'i<=' ({t: OF34.07.01.01, r: 0180, c: C, z: S} i<= isum({t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0040; 0050; 0060, c: C', z: S})) and set severity WARNING; or deactivate them, as the EBA has (Warning from the start, deleted from release 3.2). Alternatively, and only with a taxonomy change, add to OF 08.01 an 'of which: excluding exposures cleared through a CCP' column on the pattern of OF 07.00 c0211 and point the rules at it.

#### EBA precedent

The EBA equivalents are v10521_h - v10537_h (obligors), v10538_h - v10554_h (RWEA) and v10700_h - v10716_h (exposure value): 51 rules, added in release 3.0.0, all severity Warning. In the v3.0 / v3.1 sheets of the EBA validation rules list eight are deactivated on 2021-09-10 (v10522_h, v10526_h, v10539_h, v10543_h, v10547_h, v10701_h, v10705_h, v10709_h - sheets 0002 Total F-IRB, 0006 Institutions F-IRB and 0010 Specialised lending F-IRB) and five on 2022-12-12 (v10523_h, v10524_h, v10540_h, v10703_h, v10711_h); in the sheets for releases 3.2 to 3.5 all 51 are flagged Deleted = y. Matched by sheet, the Bank's live ERROR rules boe_b0837, b0855, b0873 (0002), b1035, b1067, b1068 (0006), b0859, b0877 (0010) and b0882 (0012, 2022-12-12) restate rules the EBA had deactivated. The Bank's v4.0.0 workbook lists an EBA equivalent for 45 of the 51 (none for boe_b0853, b0871, b0889, b1035, b1067, b1068), but pairs them by position rather than by sheet - a list built from that pairing (b0837, b0841, b0855, b0859, b0863, b0873, b0877, b0881, b0883) differs from the sheet-matched list above. The same exclusion sentence is in the current CRR instructions (CRR COREP Annex II p.185, para 129), so the gap is inherited, not new in PS1/26.

#### Who is affected

Any IRB firm that risk-weights CCP-related transactions under the IRB approach: clearing members' exposures to clients, and clients' exposures to clearing members where the 2% / 4% treatment is not available (the latter fall under Article 305(1), Sections 1 to 8, so the narrow reading applies to them too). All 51 rules in principle, on whichever sheet the counterparty sits (institutions 0006, financial and large corporates 0022, other corporates, and the Totals 0001 / 0002). On the broad reading, blocking from the first PRA001 return under the PS1/26 instructions.

#### What a firm can do meanwhile

Until the Bank answers, report on the reading you hold to be right and say which when you submit. An Error-severity break blocks the submission at the gateway: if the gateway rejects the return on this rule, raise it with the PRA, citing this question.

> - PRA PS1/26, Appendix 1: the PRA Rulebook instruments (Basel 3.1), Market Risk: Internal Model Approach (CRR) Part, Article 325bb(1), PDF page 243

#### The question

What does the Bank intend OF 24.01 row 0010's constrained partial cells, and the 60-day columns, to hold? On one reading of each, an ERROR rule fails a correct return; on another, every rule holds.

**Row 0010, the total across risk classes (boe_b0679, boe_b0677).** Row 0010 c0170 is the sum of the class UES_i: b0552 (c0180 = 0.5 c0130 + 0.5 c0170) and Art. 325bb(1) together fix it. If the row-0010 constrained partials hold the class aggregates, b0679 requires sum_i RS_i x max(FC_i/RC_i, 1) = (sum RS_i) x max(sum FC_i / sum RC_i, 1), which fails in general under the natural (sum) aggregation - whenever the class FC/RC ratios differ and at least one exceeds 1 (it holds when every class ratio is at most 1, or all are equal). boe_b0677, the 60-day twin, follows by the same algebra; it was not exercised in Arelle. Single day: GIRR 100/100/200 gives 200, FX 300/100/100 gives 300, so the total row is 400/200/300 with Total 500, but the rule wants 600. The rules define no row-0010 constrained partials at all.

**The 60-day block (boe_b0676, boe_b0677, boe_b0360-b0364).** Reading (1): every 60-day cell is the 60-day average of its daily value, so c0090 = ES_avg of Art. 325ba(1)(b)(i). The average of daily products is not the product of the averages, so b0676 fails. Days (FC, RC, RS) = (1,000, 1,000, 2,000) and (1,500, 1,000, 3,000) give daily UES of 2,000 and 4,500, average 3,250; the rule wants 2,500 x 1.25 = 3,125. Likewise the square root of a sum of squares does not survive averaging, so b0360 fails: LH rows (400, 300) and (500, 0) give a class value of 500 on both days, while the averaged rows (450, 150) give 474.34. Reading (2): the 325bb(1) formula and the LH cascade are applied to the averaged partials. Then every rule holds, and c0090 is a 'formula on averages' figure rather than ES_avg. Annex II's words, 'calculated in accordance with the formula set out in Article 325bb(1) ... based on the average of past 60 working days observation', support both readings. No rule ties OF 24.01 c0090 to the own funds requirement (it appears only in b0551 and in the non-negativity check b0427), so nothing forces reading (1). A compliant passing reading exists, which is why this is a question.

#### Worked example

An IMA firm's OF 24.01 with both blocks filled (the rules do not read the reporting date). 60-day block: the unconstrained partials are the averages of two observation days standing in for sixty - FC 1,250,000, RC 1,000,000, RS 2,500,000 - with column 0040 = the average daily unconstrained ES, 3,250,000, where the formula applied to the averages gives 2,500,000 x 1.25 = 3,125,000; the constrained classes are constant over the period (GIRR 1,500,000 / 1,500,000 / 3,000,000 giving 3,000,000; FX 900,000 / 300,000 / 600,000 giving 1,800,000), each with one 10-day liquidity-horizon row; row 0010 column 0080 = 4,800,000 and column 0090 = 0.5 x 3,250,000 + 0.5 x 4,800,000 = 4,025,000. Previous-day block: GIRR class FC 1,000,000, RC 1,000,000, RS 2,000,000, UES 2,000,000; FX 3,000,000 / 1,000,000 / 1,000,000, UES 3,000,000; row 0010 constrained, aggregated across classes, FC 4,000,000, RC 2,000,000, RS 3,000,000, Total 5,000,000; row 0010 unconstrained FC 3,000,000, RC 2,000,000, RS 2,800,000, so UES = 4,200,000 and column 0180 = 0.5 x 4,200,000 + 0.5 x 5,000,000 = 4,600,000. No overshootings, multiplier 1.5. On reading (1) of each point, boe_b0676 (60-day) and boe_b0679 (previous day, 5,000,000 against 6,000,000) fail; the liquidity-horizon cascades boe_b0360 / b0364, boe_b0551, boe_b0552 and boe_b0678 hold.

#### Other ways of reporting considered

**Row 0010, the total across risk classes (boe_b0679, boe_b0677).** The firm passes by leaving row 0010 c0140-c0160 and c0050-c0070 blank, which 'Where applicable' (p.247) permits and which no not-null rule forbids. The rule therefore does not force a correct return to fail. It does make it impossible to report meaningful aggregates in those cells: only blanks, RC = 0, or numbers manufactured to satisfy the identity will pass.

**The 60-day block (boe_b0676, boe_b0677, boe_b0360-b0364).** Reading (2) passes every rule and is a defensible reading of Annex II's wording. The Bank's own rules b0676/b0677/b0360 imply that reading. The difference matters only if the Bank wants c0090 to be ES_avg as defined in Art. 325ba(1)(b)(i); Annex II does not say so explicitly.

#### Proposed change

**Row 0010, the total across risk classes (boe_b0679, boe_b0677).** (1) Retarget b0677 and b0679 from row 0010 to the five risk-class rows (0020, 0070, 0130, 0180, 0240). In each rule's group filter, replace PRP = eba_PL:x10 with the class members, keeping LQH = x0. On those rows UES_t^i = PES^RS,i x max(PES^FC,i / PES^RC,i, 1) holds for a single day; keep the 60-day version b0677 only if the 60-day question is resolved as 'formula on averages'. (2) Add the identity row 0010 actually satisfies: {OF24.01.01.01 r0010 c0170} i= isum({OF24.01.01.01 r0020; 0070; 0130; 0180; 0240, c0170}), and the same on c0080 for the 60-day block. (3) Relabel b0679 'The total constrained expected shortfall for the previous day'.

**The 60-day block (boe_b0676, boe_b0677, boe_b0360-b0364).** Clarify Annex II OF 24.01 c0010-c0090. If each 60-day cell is the 60-day average of its daily value (so c0090 = ES_avg), delete b0676 and b0677. Also restrict b0360-b0364 to the previous-day block by adding boe_dim:APA = eba_AP:x0 to their group filter (evaluating c0140-c0170 only). If instead the 60-day figures are the formulas applied to the averaged partials, say so in Annex II for c0040, c0080, c0090 and the risk-class rows, and note that c0090 is then not ES_avg of Art. 325ba(1)(b)(i).

#### EBA precedent

Not checked: OF 24.01 is a PRA template and these are the Bank's own rules.

#### Who is affected

**Row 0010, the total across risk classes (boe_b0679, boe_b0677).** IMA firms from 2028 (after the IMA transitional period) that choose to fill the row-0010 constrained partial cells.

**The 60-day block (boe_b0676, boe_b0677, boe_b0360-b0364).** IMA firms only, and only after the IMA transitional period (PS1/26 Glossary: 1 January 2027 to 31 December 2027; Annex II p.34, OF 02.00 row 0580, distinguishes the two periods), so from 2028 reporting.

#### What a firm can do meanwhile

Until the Bank answers, report on the reading you hold to be right and say which when you submit. An Error-severity break blocks the submission at the gateway: if the gateway rejects the return on this rule, raise it with the PRA, citing this question.

## Already acknowledged by the Bank

The Bank's own known-issues log already records these. They are listed for completeness, with what the log says and any point it does not cover.

<a id="pi-22"></a>

### PI-22 - boe_b0710 family applies the conversion-factor breakdown to on-balance-sheet rows

**Status:** acknowledged by the Bank of England: known issue 22 (published 2 October 2026); the four rules are deactivated on the validations deny list from 19 October 2026.

**Severity:** ERROR (boe_b0710, boe_b0710_1, boe_b0710_2, boe_b0710_3).

**Effect:** a return that follows the reporting instructions fails it. **Cause:** contradicts the reporting instructions; conflicts with another published rule.

**The Bank's known-issues log, entry 22** (published 2 October 2026; records this issue):

> Issue description: The formula requires column 0150 (Fully Adjusted Exposure Value) to equal the sum of columns 0160, 0170, 0171, 0180, 0190. These columns represent the breakdown of fully adjusted exposure values by credit conversion factor and therefore relate solely to off-balance sheet exposures. The scope of the formula has been erroneously extended beyond row 0080 (off-balance sheet exposures)
>
> Solution: The validations have been deactivated. They will be reviewed with the next taxonomy update to ensure they apply only to row 0080

#### What the rule requires

On 26 rows of OF 07.00.01.01 (the total row 0010, its of-which rows, the off-balance-sheet row 0080 and the real-estate rows 0330-0360) on all 16 sheets, column 0150 (fully adjusted exposure value, E*) must equal the sum of the conversion-factor buckets, columns 0160, 0170, 0171, 0180 and 0190. boe_b0710_1, _2 and _3 assert the same on the memorandum rows of OF 07.00.01.03 (rows 0300 / 0320, exposures in default), OF 07.00.01.04 (rows 0371-0374, equity under the transitional approaches) and OF 07.00.01.05 (row 0380, currency mismatch). A missing cell is read as 0; a row with none of the six cells reported is not evaluated.

> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 07.00 rows 0070-0130, PDF page 93

#### Why a correct return fails

The Bank's log states the defect: the buckets 'relate solely to off-balance sheet exposures' and 'the scope of the formula has been erroneously extended beyond row 0080'. On any row holding an on-balance-sheet asset (or, on the total row, a counterparty-credit-risk exposure), column 0150 minus the buckets is that exposure's E*, which is above zero, so the equality is false. The amount cannot go in a bucket instead: the taxonomy has no bucket cells on the on-balance-sheet row 0070, and boe_b0765 (ERROR) ties the total row's buckets to row 0080's.

Two points the log does not cover. (1) The memorandum rows of boe_b0710_1, _2 and _3 are not limited to off-balance-sheet items, so confining those rules 'to row 0080' leaves nothing for them to check: they need an inequality, or withdrawal. (2) Together with boe_b0765, boe_b0471 and boe_b0655 (ERROR) and boe_b0717 (WARNING), boe_b0710 forces the total row's E* and exposure value to equal the off-balance-sheet row's, and, through the WARNING boe_b0717, the exposure value of the on-balance-sheet, SFT, derivative and cross-product rows to zero. A return with honest rows 0070 and 0080 and a total row set to row 0080's figures satisfies every ERROR rule and trips the WARNINGs boe_b0717, boe_b0719 and boe_b0721; a correct return fails boe_b0710 on row 0010. Once boe_b0710 is confined to row 0080 the chain disappears.

#### Worked example

A complete standardised-approach return of a firm with no off-balance-sheet business at all, so no cell of columns 0160-0190 is reported anywhere (reference date 31 March 2027; unrated, no CRM; c0010 = c0040 = c0110 = c0150 = c0200 except where provisions are stated). Sheet 0010 (real estate): regulatory residential real estate of 1,200,000 at 20% (rows 0010, 0070, 0330, 0331 and risk-weight row 0180), of which a 200,000 mortgage to a natural person whose income is in another currency, weighted 20% x 1.5 = 30% under Article 123B and, as p.94 instructs, reported against the 20% row with its RWEA reflecting the multiplier: RWEA 1,000,000 x 20% + 200,000 x 30% = 260,000; the mortgage is also in memorandum row 0380 of OF 07.00.01.05 (RWEA 60,000). Sheet 0008 (corporates): an SME loan of 500,000 at 100% (rows 0010, 0020, 0070 and 0230). Sheet 0011 (exposures in default): a corporate loan of 100,000 with 30,000 of specific provisions (c0030 = -30,000), at 100% under Article 127 (rows 0010, 0070 and 0230), also in memorandum row 0300 of OF 07.00.01.03 on the corporates sheet 0008. Sheet 0016: listed equity of 50,000 under Rule 4.2(1) at 160% (RWEA 80,000), in row 0250 (pp.95-96) and memorandum row 0372 of OF 07.00.01.04. The Total sheet 0001 is the sum of the class sheets (original exposure 1,850,000, exposure value 1,820,000, RWEA 910,000) and repeats memorandum rows 0300 and 0380. Column 0235 (RWEA without an ECAI assessment) = column 0220 on every row that has the cell, as boe_b0703 expects, although Annex II pp.86-87 gives columns 0230/0235 the legal reference Article 112(1)(a-d, f, g, l, o, q). boe_b0710 is unsatisfied on each of the 11 populated rows in its scope (rows 0010, 0020, 0330 and 0331 of the Total sheet and of the class sheets), boe_b0710_1 and _3 on both of their sheets and boe_b0710_2 once, while the sibling rules (boe_b0471 and its _2 and _3, boe_b0556_1 and _2, boe_b0655, boe_b0656, boe_b0657_1 and _2, boe_b0717) and the rules that tie the sheets and rows together (boe_b0713, boe_b0719, boe_b0721, boe_b0703) hold. Run in Arelle against every PRA001 rule (213 run on a return that files only OF 07.00; 99 evaluate), the return breaks only the boe_b0710 family and boe_b1016 / boe_b0491, which any equity under the Standardised Transitional Approach fails in 2027 (PI-01). With an off-balance-sheet item as well (a loan of 1,000,000 and an undrawn commitment of 400,000 at 40%, Total sheet only), boe_b0710 fails on row 0010 (1,400,000 against 400,000) and holds on row 0080 (400,000 = 400,000).

#### Other ways of reporting considered

Passing misreports exist, which is why the Bank's correction matters even though the gateway no longer runs the rules. (a) Moving an on-balance-sheet loan wholly into row 0080 at a 100% conversion factor (row 0070 empty; rows 0080 and 0010 carrying it in column 0190) passes all 306 OF 07.00 rules, warnings included, with total E*, exposure value and RWEA unchanged; but row 0070 holds the 'assets referred to in Article 24 CRR' (p.93), row 0080 only Table A1 items, and Article 111(1)(a) applies to asset items. (b) On the memorandum rows, putting on-balance-sheet E* in column 0190 satisfies boe_b0710_1, _2 and _3 and every other OF 07.00 rule with capital figures unchanged, but contradicts the definition of columns 0160-0190. (c) Annex II heads columns 0160-0190 '(-) Breakdown ...', and paragraph 9 says no positive figure is expected under a '(-)' label; the marker is an editorial inconsistency (the Bank's ERROR rule boe_b0658 requires the buckets to be at least zero) and does not rescue boe_b0710, which with non-positive buckets would fail for any positive E*.

#### Proposed change

The Bank's stated fix - to review the rules 'to ensure they apply only to row 0080' - is right for boe_b0710 and matches the EBA's v6364_m: scope({t: OF07.00.01.01, r:0080, z:0001;0002;0003;0004;0005;0006;0007;0008;0009;0010;0011;0012;0013;0015;0016;0017}). For boe_b0710_1, _2 and _3, whose memorandum rows are not limited to off-balance-sheet items, replace 'i=' with 'i>=' (the form of the EBA's former v4748_m), or withdraw them. boe_b0765, boe_b0471, boe_b0717 and boe_b0655 need no change: a correct return satisfies all of them once boe_b0710 is rescoped.

#### EBA precedent

EBA v6364_m (live, ERROR): '{c0150} = {c0160} + {c0170} + {c0180} + {c0190}' on C 07.00.a row 0080 only; the Bank's v4.0.0 workbook names it as the EBA equivalent of boe_b0710. It replaced v4748_m ('{c0150} >= {c0160} + {c0170} + {c0180} + {c0190}', an inequality on 22 rows that do not include row 0080), which the EBA list shows deactivated on 2018-03-09 and reactivated on 2018-04-17, and marks as replaced. EBA v0311_m (live, ERROR) '{r0010} = {r0080}' on columns 0160-0190 is boe_b0765. So the EBA holds the equality on the off-balance-sheet row and ties the total row's buckets to it; the Bank kept both and widened the equality to 26 rows.

#### Who is affected

Every firm with standardised-approach on-balance-sheet or counterparty-credit-risk exposure: it fails on row 0010 of the Total sheet and of every class sheet with on-balance-sheet exposure, on each populated of-which row, and on the memorandum tables. The Bank deactivated the four rules at its gateway from 19 October 2026 (validations deny list); a return validated before that date fails them.

#### What a firm can do meanwhile

Nothing to change for a submission from 19 October 2026: the gateway no longer runs the four rules (validations deny list; known-issues log entry 22). Do not move on-balance-sheet exposures into the conversion-factor buckets to satisfy them.

<a id="pi-30"></a>

### PI-30 - OF 07.00 memorandum rows 0300 / 0320: sheets the taxonomy does not publish

**Status:** acknowledged by the Bank of England: known issue 27 (published 19 October 2026).

**Effect:** no rule result shows it; the instructions or the taxonomy do. **Cause:** the taxonomy lacks cells the instructions ask for; the instructions leave a gap.

**The Bank's known-issues log, entry 27** (published 19 October 2026; records this issue):

> Issue description: The Credit Risk SA templates OF 07.00 Part 3 – Memo Items (Rows 0300 and 0320) and SC 07.00 Part 3 – Memo Items (Rows 0300 and 0320) do not contain a separate sheet for exposures assigned to the real estate exposure class (as referred to in Article 112(1)(i) of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part of the PRA Rulebook).
>
> Solution: The taxonomy will be corrected in due course. As a temporary solution, the PRA requests that firms report exposures assigned to the real estate exposure class in the total sheet s0001 for rows 0300 and 0320 but do not report such exposures separately to this, until the missing sheet 0010 is provided in the next taxonomy update.

#### The rules

| Rule | Module | Severity | Part in the issue | Where the issue applies | At the gateway |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| boe_b0656 | PRA001 | ERROR | related | - | run as published |
| boe_b0556_2 | PRA001 | ERROR | related | - | run as published |
| boe_b0665 | PRA001 | WARNING | related | - | run as published |

#### What the rule requires

Not a rule. Table OF07.00.01.03 ('Memorandum items - Exposures in default') has a z-axis of seven sheets: 0001 Total, 0002 Central governments or central banks, 0003 Regional governments or local authorities, 0004 Public sector entities, 0007 Institutions, 0008 Corporates, 0009 Retail (read from of07.00.01.03-rend.xml and its code labels in the package). All 11 rules on the table are scoped to exactly those seven sheets and none compares one sheet with another.

#### What the instructions and rules say

> Those memorandum items in rows 0300 and 0320 shall only be reported for the following exposure classes: (a) central governments or central banks (Article 112(1)(a) of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part); (b) regional governments or local authorities (Article 112(1)(b) of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part); (c) public sector entities (Article 112(1)(c) of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part); (d) institutions (Article 112(1)(f) of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part); (e) corporates (Article 112(1)(g) of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part); (f) retail (Article 112(1)(h) of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part). (g) real estate (Article 112(1)(i) of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part).
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, para 52, PDF page 78

> Exposures shall be reported in these rows where the obligors would have been reported in the exposure classes ‘Central governments or central banks’, ‘Regional governments or local authorities’, ‘Public sector entities’, ‘Institutions’, ‘Corporates’, ‘Retail’ and ‘Real estate’ within OF CR SA, if those exposures were not assigned to the exposure classes 'in default'.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, para 54, PDF pages 78-79

> then that information shall be reported in OF CR SA, row 0320 in the total and in the exposure class ‘in default’. If this exposure, before it defaulted, was an exposure to an institution, then that information shall also be reported in row 0320 of exposure class 'institutions'.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, para 55, PDF page 79

> Firms shall report values in this row for exposure classes defined in Article 112 (1)(a) to (i) of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, rows 0300 and 0320, PDF page 97

> Exposures included in the exposure class “exposures in default”, subject to Article 127(1)(b) and (3) of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part, which would otherwise have been assigned to the exposure class being reported on if they were not in default.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, row 0300, PDF page 97

> A residential real estate exposure which is a defaulted exposure and is not materially dependent on the cash-flows of the property shall be assigned a risk weight of 100%.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Appendix 1: the PRA Rulebook instruments (Basel 3.1), Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part, Article 127(3), PDF page 59

> (d) Institutions (point (f) of Article 112 CRR); (e) Corporates (point (g) of Article 112 CRR); (f) Retail (point (h) of Article 112 CRR).
>
> - CRR COREP Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, para 52 (the list the taxonomy still follows), PDF pages 79-80

#### Why it matters

No rule fails; a figure Annex II asks for has no cell. The real-estate part is the Bank's known issue 27 (19 October 2026), with the PRA's interim instruction to report those exposures on the Total sheet s0001 only and a promised taxonomy fix. What follows adds the other missing sheets, and one point of wording: entry 27 speaks of 'exposures assigned to the real estate exposure class', where Annex II para 54 and p.97 mean the exposures that would otherwise have been assigned to it. Where text and taxonomy DISAGREE: (1) Real estate, Article 112(1)(i) - named in para 52(g), para 54 and the row instructions (p.97); the taxonomy has no sheet 0010 on OF07.00.01.03. (2) Multilateral development banks (d) and international organisations (e) - inside 'Article 112(1)(a) to (i)' on p.97 (though absent from para 52, so Annex II contradicts itself); no sheets 0005 / 0006. (3) The exposure class 'in default' - para 55 says 'in the total and in the exposure class in default'; the Total sheet 0001 is published, the 'in default' sheet 0011 is not. Where they AGREE: Total (0001) and classes (a) 0002, (b) 0003, (c) 0004, (f) 0007, (g) 0008, (h) 0009. The published sheet list is the CRR one (six classes plus total); PS1/26 added real estate to the text and the taxonomy did not follow. Consequence under Basel 3.1: a defaulted exposure whose class would otherwise be real estate (for example a defaulted owner-occupied mortgage, which Article 127(3) weights at 100% and which row 0300's own instruction therefore covers) can be shown on the Total sheet only, so the Total no longer equals the sum of the class sheets - harmless today because no rule sums them.

#### Other ways of reporting considered

Report a defaulted real-estate exposure on the Retail or Corporates memorandum sheet instead: contrary to para 54, which now names 'Real estate' as its own would-have-been class. Report it on the Total sheet only: the only thing the taxonomy allows, and what a firm will have to do. Report it in the main table's 'Exposures in default' sheet 0011: that is OF07.00.01.01, which has no rows 0300 / 0320.

#### Proposed change

For real estate, the Bank has said it will add sheet 0010 (known issue 27); please add it to the seven-sheet scopes of the 11 rules on the table too (boe_b0471_2, b0556_2, b0656, b0660, b0665, b0670, b0672_1, b0673, b0708_1, b0710_1, b0733_1; boe_b0710_1 is deactivated at the gateway from 19 October 2026, see PI-22). For multilateral development banks and international organisations (p.97 'Article 112(1)(a) to (i)' against para 52), either add sheets 0005 / 0006 or replace '(a) to (i)' on p.97 with the para 52 list; and reword para 55 ('in the total and in the exposure class in default') to say the Total sheet and the sheet of the original class.

#### EBA precedent

The six-class list is the EBA's (CRR Annex II para 52: central governments, regional governments, PSEs, institutions, corporates, retail). The sentence 'in the total and in the exposure class in default' is also inherited from CRR Annex II para 55, and the EBA's rules on these memorandum rows are scoped to the same seven sheets (the EBA table linkbase itself was not checked). The additions of real estate (paras 52(g), 54) and of '(a) to (i)' (p.97) are the PRA's own.

#### Who is affected

Every SA firm with defaulted real-estate exposure (and the rare defaulted MDB / international-organisation exposure), every period. Nothing is rejected; the breakdown is simply incomplete.

#### What a firm can do meanwhile

Follow the PRA's interim instruction in the Bank's known-issues log entry 27: "As a temporary solution, the PRA requests that firms report exposures assigned to the real estate exposure class in the total sheet s0001 for rows 0300 and 0320 but do not report such exposures separately to this, until the missing sheet 0010 is provided in the next taxonomy update." The entry covers the real-estate sheet only; the other sheets this issue finds missing are not in it.
