### PI-39 - boe_b0272: wrong CVA methodology trigger

**Status:** acknowledged by the Bank of England: known issue 29 (published 11 November 2026); the rule is deactivated on the validations deny list from 16 November 2026.

**Severity:** WARNING (boe_b0272).

**Effect:** it accepts figures the rules do not permit. **Cause:** the rule allows more values than the requirement it checks.

**The Bank's known-issues log, entry 29** (published 11 November 2026; records this issue):

> Issue description: The rule checks the K-full calculation in OF25.02.01.01 (Full-BA CVA). However, its CVA methodology condition references R0030, C0010 in OF25.01.01.01, SA-CVA approach, which is an incorrect CVA methodology trigger for reporting template OF25.02.01.01. The issue is that the rule evaluates for SA-CVA-only firms and is not being triggered by the full BA-CVA applicability condition alone.
>
> Solution: The rule has been deactivated until it is amended in the next taxonomy release. The rule is expected to trigger when full BA-CVA methodology is selected in OF25.01.01.01, including where it is used alongside SA-CVA. The proposed correction is to replace r:0030, c:0010 (SA-CVA) with r:0020, c:0010 (full BA-CVA).

#### The rules

| Rule | Module | Severity | Part in the issue | Where the issue applies | At the gateway |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| boe_b0272 | PRA001 | WARNING | the rule at issue | every evaluation | deactivated by the Bank of England on 16 November 2026 (validations deny list; known issues log #29) |
| boe_b0273 | PRA001 | WARNING | related | - | run as published |

boe_b0272, as published in taxonomy 4.1.1 (label: "K-full is equal to the weighted sum of 25% times K-reduced and 75% K-hedged|"):

```text
if {t: OF25.01.01.01, r: 0030, c: 0010, dv: false(), seq: False, id: v3, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} = true() then {t: OF25.02.01.01, r: 0080, c: 0010, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v0, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i= 0.25 i* {t: OF25.02.01.01, r: 0010, c: 0010, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v1, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i+ 0.75 i* {t: OF25.02.01.01, r: 0040, c: 0010, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v2, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} else true()
```

#### What the rule requires

K-full = 0.25 × K-reduced + 0.75 × K-hedged, but only when the firm reports that it uses SA-CVA.

#### What the instructions and rules say

> If a firm uses one or more eligible BA-CVA hedges to hedge CVA risk it must calculate its own funds requirement for CVA risk in accordance with the following formula: DSBA−CVA × Kfull where: DSBA−CVA = 0.65; Kfull = β ∙Kreduced + (1 −β) ∙Khedged; where: β = 0.25;
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Appendix 1: the PRA Rulebook instruments (Basel 3.1), CVA Risk Part rule 4.5, PDF page 401

#### Why a wrong return passes

A correct return does not fail: this is a missed error, not a false failure. The Bank's log records it. For a firm whose only CVA method is full BA-CVA, the guard is false, so a wrong K-full passes b0272 vacuously. b0273 only ties row 0090 to row 0080, and b0076/b0077 check the two square roots, so a mis-stated K-full passes every rule.

#### Worked example

A firm whose only CVA method is full BA-CVA (SA-CVA flag false), on rule 7.1(1), that misreports K-full as 80,000 instead of 0.25 x 100,000 + 0.75 x 60,000 = 70,000 (K-reduced 100,000 = sqrt(6e9 + 4e9); K-hedged 60,000 = sqrt(2e9 + 1e9 + 6e8)), with the Total r0090 = 0.65 x 80,000 = 52,000, consistent with the wrong K-full. boe_b0272 holds, because its condition reads the SA-CVA flag; so do boe_b0273 (Total = 0.65 x K-full) and the square-root checks boe_b0076 / b0077. With the SA-CVA flag also true, boe_b0272 fails [0,1].

Arelle's result on it:

| Rule | Satisfied | Unsatisfied | What the example shows |
|---|---|---|---|
| boe_b0076 | 1 | 0 | - |
| boe_b0077 | 1 | 0 | - |
| boe_b0193 | 1 | 0 | - |
| boe_b0272 | 1 | 0 | holds |
| boe_b0273 | 1 | 0 | - |

#### Other ways of reporting considered

Not applicable. This is a permissive gap: the wrong figure passes everything.

#### Proposed change

Change the boe_b0272 precondition from {t: OF25.01.01.01, r: 0030, c: 0010, dv: false()} = true() to {t: OF25.01.01.01, r: 0020, c: 0010, dv: false()} = true(), leaving the consequent unchanged - the correction the Bank's log proposes.

#### EBA precedent

None (Bank-authored).

#### Who is affected

Every firm whose only CVA method is full BA-CVA has K-full unchecked. There are no false failures. The Bank deactivated the rule at its gateway from 16 November 2026, so from that date it checks nothing for any firm.

#### What a firm can do meanwhile

The gateway no longer runs boe_b0272 (validations deny list, from 16 November 2026; known-issues log entry 29). Check K-full = 0.25 x K-reduced + 0.75 x K-hedged yourself: no other rule checks it for a firm on full BA-CVA alone.

### PI-40 - boe_b0274: tests an obsolete hedging-benefit row and lacks the rule 7.1(2) condition

**Status:** acknowledged by the Bank of England: known issue 30 (published 11 November 2026); the rule is deactivated on the validations deny list from 16 November 2026.

**Severity:** WARNING (boe_b0274).

**Effect:** a return that follows the reporting instructions fails it. **Cause:** contradicts the reporting instructions.

**The Bank's known-issues log, entry 30** (published 11 November 2026; records this issue):

> Issue description: The rule does not currently explicitly limit its application to firms using the transitional described under rule 7.1(2) and could therefore evaluate outside its intended reporting scope
>
> Solution: The rule has been deactivated until it is amended in the next taxonomy release. The proposed correction is to add the missing applicability condition for the target CVA population requiring OF25.01.01.04, R0020, C0010 = true() to trigger mandatory reporting of Total Full-BA CVA Capital requirements {OF25.02.01.01, r:0100. c:0010} for firms using transitional arrangements.

#### The rules

| Rule | Module | Severity | Part in the issue | Where the issue applies | At the gateway |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| boe_b0274 | PRA001 | WARNING | the rule at issue | every evaluation | deactivated by the Bank of England on 16 November 2026 (validations deny list; known issues log #30) |
| boe_b0273 | PRA001 | WARNING | holds on the example (control) | - | run as published |
| boe_b0076 | PRA001 | WARNING | holds on the example (control) | - | run as published |
| boe_b0947 | PRA001 | ERROR | related | - | run as published |
| boe_b0205 | PRA001 | WARNING | related | - | run as published |

boe_b0274, as published in taxonomy 4.1.1 (label: "Under the full BA-CVA approach, the hedging benefit is equal to the capital requirements for K-reduced (0.65* K-reduced) minus the capital requirements for K-full (0.65* K-full, already calculated in row 0090)|"):

```text
{t: OF25.02.01.01, r: 0100, c: 0010, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v0, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i= {t: OF25.02.01.02, r: 0010, c: 0010, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v1, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting} i- 0.65 i* {t: OF25.02.01.01, r: 0090, c: 0010, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v2, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting}
```

#### What the rule requires

For every firm that files both OF 25.02 tables (no condition on the CVA methods or the transitional): OF 25.02.01.01 row 0100 = K-reduced (OF 25.02.01.02 row 0010) - 0.65 x the Total (OF 25.02.01.01 row 0090). The label describes a 'hedging benefit' (0.65 x K-reduced - 0.65 x K-full), but the expression is not even that formula: it takes K-reduced unscaled and multiplies row 0090, which already includes the 0.65 (boe_b0273), by 0.65 again.

#### What the instructions and rules say

> For firms using the transitional described under rule 7.1(2): Total after applying the discount scalar [...] Firms using the transitional described under rule 7.1(2), should report in this cell the CVA RWAs according to this methodology after applying the discount scalar.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 25.02 full BA-CVA r0100, PDF page 276

> From and including 1 January 2027 to and including 31 December 2027 70%
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Appendix 1: the PRA Rulebook instruments (Basel 3.1), CVA Risk Part rule 7.2 table, PDF page 424

> DSBA−CVA = 0.65; and Kreduced is calculated in accordance with the following formula: Kreduced = √(ρ ∙∑SCVAC C ) 2 + (1 −ρ2) ∙∑SCVAC 2 C
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Appendix 1: the PRA Rulebook instruments (Basel 3.1), CVA Risk Part rule 4.2 (the formula's typesetting is partly lost in the PDF text), PDF page 399

> DSBA−CVA × Kfull where: DSBA−CVA = 0.65; Kfull = β ∙Kreduced + (1 −β) ∙Khedged; where: β = 0.25;
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Appendix 1: the PRA Rulebook instruments (Basel 3.1), CVA Risk Part rule 4.5, PDF page 401

> Aggregation of systematic components for K-Reduced refers to the first term under the square root sign in rule 4.2 of the Credit Valuation Adjustment Risk Part of the PRA rulebook
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 25.02 row 0020, PDF page 275

> For firms using the transitional described under rule 7.1(2): Total after applying the discount scalar Firms using the transitional described under rule 7.1(2), should report in this cell the CVA RWAs according to this methodology after applying the discount scalar.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 25.02 row 0100, PDF page 276

> Decomposition of full BA-CVA capital requirements Scope: firms that use the BA-CVA for at least a subset of their portfolios, and that apply hedging to some of their exposures.
>
> - PRA PS1/26, Annex II: reporting instructions for the credit risk templates, OF 25.02 scope, PDF page 274

#### Why a correct return fails

Row 0100 now holds the full BA-CVA Total after the rule 7.1(2) discount scalar (Annex II p.276), and is blank otherwise. The Bank's log records that the rule lacks the 7.1(2) condition. The point the log does not cover is the expression itself: it tests no Annex II relation and holds only by coincidence. Without the transitional, row 0100 falls back to 0 against 4,000,000 - 0.65 x 2,210,000 = 2,563,500 (the example's figures); with the transitional and an 80% scalar, row 0100 = 1,768,000, still against 2,563,500. Even the label's 'hedging benefit' would be 0.65 x 4,000,000 - 2,210,000 = 390,000. So if only the applicability condition the log proposes is added and the expression kept, the rule would fail a correct 7.1(2) filer of both tables unless, by coincidence, scalar x row 0090 = K-reduced - 0.65 x row 0090. Whether a full BA-CVA firm is expected to file the reduced BA-CVA table at all is itself open (PI-35).

#### Worked example

A full BA-CVA firm on the rule 7.1(2) transitional (final scalar 80%) that files both OF 25.02 tables - the population the Bank's proposed condition would select. K-reduced 4,000,000 = sqrt(9.6e12 + 6.4e12); K-hedged 3,200,000; K-full 3,400,000; Total (row 0090) 2,210,000; after the scalar (row 0100) 1,768,000. OF 25.01 as Annex II p.273 reads (row 0010 after the scalar: capital 1,768,000, RWA 22,100,000; row 0030 before it: 2,210,000, the OF 25.02 data point). boe_b0274 compares 1,768,000 with 4,000,000 - 0.65 x 2,210,000 = 2,563,500. boe_b0205 (PI-35), boe_b0947 (PI-34) and the row-0010 sums boe_b0270 / b0192 / b0267 (PI-34) fail on the same return for their own reasons; boe_b0273 and boe_b0076 hold.

#### Other ways of reporting considered

There is no value of row 0100 that is both what Annex II asks (the after-scalar Total, or blank) and equal to K-reduced - 0.65 x row 0090, except by coincidence. The rule can be avoided only by not filing one of the two OF 25.02 tables, which most firms will do anyway.

#### Proposed change

Do not reactivate boe_b0274 with only the new condition. Either retire it, if boe_b0947 is rewritten as proposed in PI-34, or replace it with: if ({OF25.01.01.04 r0020 c0010} = true()) then ({OF25.02.01.01 r0100 c0010} <= {OF25.02.01.01 r0090 c0010} and {OF25.02.01.01 r0100 c0010} >= 0.7 * {OF25.02.01.01 r0090 c0010}) else true(), with the precondition on OF 25.01.01.04 and OF 25.02.01.01 only (dropping the reference to OF 25.02.01.02), labelled 'Under rule 7.1(2), the full BA-CVA Total after the final discount scalar lies between 70% and 100% of the Total' (subject to the same 'CVA RWAs' point as PI-34).

#### EBA precedent

None: a PRA-specific row and a Bank-authored rule. The workbook text matches the formula.

#### Who is affected

Nil at the gateway since 16 November 2026: the Bank deactivated boe_b0274 and logged it as known issue 30. The remaining point is for the reactivation: with only the logged condition added, the rule would still fail correct 7.1(2) filers of both OF 25.02 tables.

#### What a firm can do meanwhile

Nothing to change: the gateway no longer runs boe_b0274 (validations deny list, from 16 November 2026; known-issues log entry 30).

<a id="appendix-a"></a>

## Appendix A - Rules the Bank re-imposes that the EBA has deactivated

Many PRA001 rules restate an EBA validation rule. The EBA keeps one list for all its framework releases, one sheet per release, and describes a deactivated rule as one 'which should be disregarded (primarily due to being identified as potentially incorrect)'. This appendix lists every enforced PRA001 rule whose EBA counterpart is deactivated in the EBA's latest release sheet, or was deleted while deactivated, checked against every release sheet up to 3.5 (the EBA list of 10 June 2026). The counterpart is the one the Bank's v4.0.0 workbook names, except in group B: for the OF 34.07 / OF 08.01 rules that workbook pairs the Bank's rules with the EBA's by position, not by sheet (PI-08, PI-13), so group B matches each Bank rule to the EBA rule on the same table, row, column and sheet code (the Bank kept the EBA's codes 0002, 0006, 0010, 0011 and 0012 for these sheets; the EBA has no sheet 0020). Matched so, boe_b0841 (sheet 0010), b0863 and b0881 (0011) and b0883 (0020) restate no deactivated rule: the EBA's v10530_h, v10548_h and v10710_h were never deactivated. Deactivation alone is not a defect: the EBA does not publish its reasons, and several of these rules are sound for the Basel 3.1 templates. The last column gives the assessment: the issue in this document that covers the rule, or why it was found sound.

34 enforced rules restate an EBA rule that is deactivated, or was deleted while deactivated, in the latest sheet (groups A, A2, B and E below; boe_b0349 and boe_b0350 in group A carry an EBA label but are not restatements). Seven more restate EBA rules the EBA reactivated on 10 March 2022 in corrected form (group C), so 'never reactivated' is not true of them; four were in the taxonomy package in v4.0.0 and are not in it in v4.1.1 (group D). For each rule in groups A, A2, B and E the Bank may wish to confirm that the EBA's reason for deactivating the original does not apply to the Basel 3.1 template. The Bank already does this for the rules it carries under the EBA's own codes: of the 20 EBA-coded PRA001 rules the EBA has deactivated, 16 are switched off in PRA001 (11 not in the package, 5 deactivated) and 4 are still run (v0611_m, v6566_s, v7336_m, v7430_m, all WARNING). Two points beyond the issues: boe_b0779 keeps percentage column 0050, which the EBA's corrected v09797_m dropped (PI-23); and the EBA deactivated v09796_m, the original of boe_b0778, on 10 June 2025 (PI-23). The 'What the Bank's rule checks' column gives the Bank's form, which can differ from the EBA's: the EBA's v4757_m is {c0280} <= {c0020} with no absolute values, and its 3.2 forms of v09773_m-v09778_m sum over sheets s0001-s0017 where the Bank's apply per sheet; boe_b0739 reads OF 08.01 c0282 where v09777_m reads c0280.

<a id="appendix-b"></a>

## Appendix B - Checked and found sound

These candidate issues were examined with the same method - the instructions and rules read in full, every alternative reporting tried in Arelle - and the published rule was found to be right. They are listed so that the Bank can see what was checked; none is raised.

| Point examined | Rules | Why the published rule is sound |
|---|---|---|
| Does any PS1/26 real-estate risk weight need row 0280 ('Other risk weights') on OF 07.00 sheet 0010? | boe_b0445, boe_b0445_1 | No. Annex II p.95 has a prior-charge exposure reported against the weight that would apply without Art. 124G(2) / 124I(3), and p.94 the same for the Art. 123B multiplier; only the RWEA carries the uplift. Checked weight by weight against the rows boe_b0445 leaves open (Arts. 124F-124L, 123B, 127, 232(3)), every weight but 110% has an open row (110% is PI-05); guarantees, simple-method collateral and life-insurance collateral leave the sheet as an inflow to the protection provider's class (Annex II paras 56A and p.84). Arelle: boe_b0445 [1,0] on the compliant return. |
| Does boe_b0779 wrongly include OF 08.07 columns 0010 and 0020 (exposure values)? | boe_b0779 | No. Both are amounts (eba_met:mi119 'Exposure value', monetary) and each exposure is in exactly one of the eight Article 147B(1) roll-out classes, so they add down the rows to row 0260; Annex II's own row-0260 sum presupposes that the rows partition the population. On a correct return columns 0010 and 0020 are satisfied. Only the wording is missing: the row-0260 instruction names columns 0060-0150 and says nothing of columns 0010-0050. |
| Does boe_b0778 fail a roll-out class with no exposure? | boe_b0778 | No, provided the three share cells of an empty class are left unreported, the natural reading (each share is a quotient over the class's column 0020, and with no exposure there is no quotient): the gateway then does not evaluate the row (Arelle [3,0] on the return with an empty class). Reporting 0 in any of the three share cells fails it [3,1]. Annex II has no general instruction on zero versus blank, so a firm that zero-fills is exposed; the fix proposed in PI-23 ('<= 1') would also accept that. |
| Is boe_b0349 (OF 09.02 exposure value >= of which defaulted) a valid identity? | boe_b0349 | Yes. Column 0107 is an 'of which' of column 0105 on the same row and on the same ultimate-obligor basis (Annex II para 87); under the IRB approach a defaulted exposure stays in its class, and boe_b0321 keeps both columns non-negative, so column 0107 is always contained in column 0105. Substitution of a defaulted obligor's covered part, slotting rows and country sheets all move the two columns together. Arelle [3,0]. (The standardised-approach twin boe_b0350 is not sound: PI-28.) |
